projects.title: 两天上线第一个出海 AI 工具站（英文 AI 同人生成器），记录一下过程和踩的坑
projects.author: zkitkevin
projects.summary: 周四晚上定词写需求，周六晚上上线：[fanficwizard.com]( https://fanficwizard.com) 一个英文的 AI 同人（ fanfic ）生成器：填作品、角色/CP 、几个梗（ enemies to lovers 、slow burn 这种）、基调和人称，几秒出一段完整的同人场景，结尾带 AO3 风格的标题和 tags 。免费每天 3 次，不用注册。 ## 为什么做这个 按"一个关键词一个页面"的思路选的词：搜 "ai fanfic generator" 的人意图很明确，就是想要一个工具。前排有大站，也有不少小站，觉得可以试试。这次只上首页，主词站稳了再做内页。 ## 技术 - 自己攒的 Next.js 模板（工具站通用：多字段表单 → 提示词模板 → 流式输出，积分、作品库、后台都是可拆的模块），这次只改配置和文案就出了站 - Next.js 16 + Postgres （ Neon ）+ Prisma + Vercel ，Google 登录，Cloudflare Turnstile 防刷 - 模型走 OpenAI 兼容的网关，分两档：免费用便宜模型写短场景，付费用好模型写整章、能续写（带人物设定 + 前情摘要 + 上一章结尾） - 大部分代码是 Claude Code 写的，我主要做需求、审代码和踩坑 ## 踩的坑 1. **收款**：本来想用 Stripe ，账号资料有点问题，最后改用 MoR （代理销售方，帮你交各国的税、能提现到国内）。顺手比了一下费率：Creem 3.9%+$0.40 ，Waffo 3.9%+$0.50 ，Paddle / Lemon Squeezy 5%+$0.50 。固定费对 $5 的小包很伤，接近 14%，后面准备调价。所以目前定价页还是 Coming soon 。 2. **www 跳转方向选反**：Vercel 加域名时默认勾了"裸域跳 www"，但站点配置、登录回调、canonical 全是裸域，结果生成接口的同源校验和 Google 登录都会挂。改成 www → 裸域 308 就好了。 3. **内容安全**：同人圈对内容很敏感，只写 G/T 级。请求和输出两层检查（输出边流边查），检查服务出错也一律拦截，不扣积分。 4. **免费被刷**：IP 哈希 + Turnstile + 每日全站成本上限，超了就暂停免费额度，不会一觉醒来账单爆了。 ## 想听听大家的意见 - 首页文案和生成效果怎么样？ - 做出海工具站的朋友，收款最后用的哪家？ 随手试一下就行，不用注册。

projects.title: Show HN: Sketch Stadium – watch your agent play Pictionary
projects.author: ericlevine
projects.summary: tl;dr: Agents can play Pictionary. You can connect your own agent, or just watch a game in progress here: https://sketch.wakeshift.ai/games/q5ucru Hi folks! I initially built this as a proof-of-concept for sending push notifications to AI agents. Watching the agents play Pictionary together has been compelling, so I thought I'd ship it as a standalone demonstration. In Sketch Stadium, your agent subscribes to game events. Agents take turns either drawing or guessing. Easy clues are 1 point, medium are 2, and hard are 3. It's entertaining to watch and some of the drawings are impressive (and others are mind-bogglingly bad). This is the real opportunity for the model labs who have been pelican-maxxing to shine. The first version gave agents the ability to draw lines 10 at a time so that it would be a little bit more like real Pictionary. However, it turns out agents are _really_ bad at drawing that way. So instead I let them use a subset of SVG to draw and that's worked much better, even for the lower-cost models. You don't need to create an account to connect your agent, just add the MCP and authorize. But if you don't want to do that, just watch the game linked above. As a bit more background, agents often start processes that take an indeterminate amount of time to complete (e.g. CI, waiting for approval in a separate system, sending an email and waiting for a reply). If an agent needs that process to complete before it can proceed, it can: * poll, * ask the user to tell it when it's done, * use a bespoke built-in integration, or * use a proprietary capability (e.g. Claude Code monitors) Today, there's no easy, consistent way to wake up agents through a webhook or push notification. I dealt with this firsthand with Clawvisor (authorization for agents) where I needed agents to recognize when the operator had clicked an out-of-band approve button. The best-supported way to achieve that at the time was long-polling. This project is basically a tech demo for Wakeshift, which is a cross-harness, simple SDK for providing push notifications for agents. It attaches to your MCP to allow consumers of your MCP to subscribe to real-time events, and uses whatever available hacks per harness to wake an agent when dormant. For most harnesses, Wakeshift requires a hook to be installed for the best experience. It will upgrade automatically as harnesses start adopting MCP events. I'd love any feedback or ideas for other products or games that you'd want to see built on this capability. Or MCP servers that you use today that you think would benefit from push notifications.

projects.title: Show HN: SpecDeck – Bring coding agent decisions back into the spec
projects.author: specdeck
projects.summary: Writing good specs is hard. You don’t know everything upfront and it’s impossible to write every little detail in the spec. Much of my job as a developer has been to treat specs as intent, and fill out the blanks in the code and use the code reviews as a way to question those decisions. But as coding agents have started to produce much more code, the decisions that actually affect the product are getting harder to find. So I created SpecDeck. It helps everyone on the team write specs and hand them over to developers and their agents through MCP. During implementation, agents write the decisions that matter back as proposed spec changes and leave smaller implementation choices in the code. When the work is done, a person reviews and publish those changes into the spec. The workflow is modeled on git: a published spec is main, drafts are branches, and proposals are pull requests. It should feel familiar to developers, while making it easy for the whole team to work with specs and keep them up to date without touching git. It’s still early and there’s plenty to improve, but I’d love to hear your feedback.

projects.title: Show HN: KernelCash – Privacy First Budgeting
projects.author: LoftyHobbitMan
projects.summary: Hi everyone! I typically do not put my projects out for others to see, so this is new to me, but I have created a privacy first budgeting app called KernelCash Budgets ( https://kernelcash.com ), and wanted to share it here in the event someone was interested in a product like this. This app has really helped my wife and I, as well as some family, friends, and colleagues, so I wanted to put this out to see if it could help anyone else. I created this app as a replacement to some of the other budgeting apps out there. Some of KernelCash's core features include: - Envelope and zero style budgeting - Expense, income, and savings goal tracking - Full analytics for income, expenses, and savings - Bank connection / sync free. We use transaction file imports (OFX / QFX) or manual entry to keep things private. You can freely share or not share what you choose. - Multi-collaborator workspaces. These are great for sharing your budget with a spouse, roommates, and have even been used by some parents to teach their kids how to budget. Each workspace is an independent sandbox for you to choose how you work with it. - Customizable budgets that are not month-locked. You control the time span of each budget you have. - There is only one pricing tier so you will always get every feature. I initially created this app only for my wife and I and ran it on a Raspberry Pi. I made it well over a year ago as a replacement for some of the other budgeting apps that I had been using and trying out. I have used many of the budgeting apps that are out there, and a lot of them were either cumbersome to get my data into, or wanted all of my financial data along with bank account connections. Needless to say, I was not really happy with any of these, and so that's why I chose to build KernelCash. KernelCash started as a small tool for my wife and I that I created as a hobby project so that I learn new skills for my day job, and to scratch some of the coding and architectural itches I don't get at work (I'm a software engineer). I never intended to release this to the public, but over time KernelCash came up while in conversations with friends, family, and colleagues. Many of them were really interested in it and wanted to use it since they apparently had some of the same privacy concerns as I did. Since they were wanting access to the app, I decided to move it out of my homelab and into a real multi-tenant application with all of the customer service, landing pages, and other gismos that are expected with a production app. As expected, that was more work than the core app logic. We are priced lower than essentially all of the alternatives at $9.99/month or $87.50 for the annual subscription. If I had the financial means to, I would give this away for free. I can't justify maintaining this project and work full-time and have a family, so I have priced the product as low as I can based on server / infra + general admin and development costs of running this product. We offer a one month free trial and welcome anyone who is curious to try out the product and give any feedback you may have. Feel free to ask any questions, I would love to answer them! You can find KernelCash at https://kernelcash.com Edit: Fixed URL.

projects.summary: Hi HN, I built cc-pair because I kept noticing that when a coding agent reviews its own work, it tends to go easy on it. cc-pair pairs the two agents I already use — Claude Code and Codex — so one authors a change and the other reviews it, and they iterate until the reviewer approves or the round limit (default 3) escalates to the human. Roles are symmetric: either agent can be author or reviewer. In auto mode, `pair start --as claude` (or `--as codex`) opens the author and starts the other agent as reviewer for each round — no second terminal needed. In manual mode you run both yourself. They communicate through numbered message files in a shared directory (~/.pair/<repo>-<hash>/), so the whole review thread is inspectable on disk. Install: npm install -g claude-codex-pair (Node 22+, macOS/Linux for auto mode; manual mode works on Windows). Both CLIs need to be installed and signed in. Repo: https://github.com/leonlee/cc-pair — the README has an example review thread in Appendix A, and DESIGN.md specifies the protocol. I'd love feedback: does cross-model review actually catch things self-review misses in your experience, and what would you want the reviewer to be stricter about?

projects.title: Show HN: Pretty Git Tree – Your Git history as generative art
projects.author: hda-hda
projects.summary: I've spent months building something complex and (so far) invisible. I know that the number of commits, branches, merges etc. aren't proof of progress, but what I needed was a way to represent the amount of effort I'd put in that wasn't "proximity to burnout". Pretty-git-tree takes in your git history (just the commit structure, and it stays local to your browser) and gives you a visually interesting representation of it. For my own projects I use the "qubits" style which winds a quantum circuit around a space-filling curve. I've included snapshots of some famous git repositories as well. I didn't want to just use the standard git tree, because I felt that there were so many different ways of exploring the data - plus I wanted it to look good at the top of a weekly standup report. I've included the four styles I expect people to use, plus another 15 or so styles in the repo where I wanted to try things out (like rendering the branches as tower-blocks in a city, or kintsugi fractures). The repo itself is MIT licensed, and suggestions are welcome.

projects.title: Show HN: Beolis – Manage your coding AI agents
projects.author: fabioz
projects.summary: Hey HN, I'm Fabio, the creator of Beolis. I've built Beolis ( https://beolis.com ) to better handle coding on agentic scenarios. It can be used to manage coding with agents in parallel / in the background either in your local machine (using your current repository or git worktrees) or remotely (where it creates a git worktree remotely and works with the agent there). Although it uses agents you don't need to "chat" with the agent at each step as you usually do when dealing with agents (although you still can), but rather create workflows where you can code the default steps you want. This means that instead of saying 'run the tests' to an agent the idea is that you (or the agent) create code that will actually run the tests and then if it fails it goes to a cheap agent to summarize the failures and then onto a smarter agent to actually do the fixes and work on the problems found -- I find my tokens last much longer given that approach ;) I've been using Beolis to build itself (started back in February) and I believe it's now stable for day-to-day use. For local use it's completely free, otherwise, you can get more collaboration features and remote workers. I'd love to hear feedback.

Lean is one of the most popular languages that allow for formal verification, and to me is incredibly powerful because it is a general purpose programming language with formal verification built directly into it. projects.title: 因为忍受不了兄弟打印机手机打印的锯齿和 Word 变字体，我手搓了套 600/1200DPI 1-Bit 点阵渲染引擎 + 免费多端远程打印网关
projects.author: ptervip
projects.summary: 各位 V 友大家好，我是独立开发者。 家里买过 **兄弟（ Brother DCP-B7520DW / B7535DW / T420W / T720DW / L2535DW /L1848W 等）**，或者惠普、佳能、爱普生、奔图无线打印机的朋友，大概率都被以下三个问题折磨过： 1. **手机打出来的字远不如电脑清楚（严重锯齿、笔画发虚）**：明明同一台激光/喷墨打印机，用电脑插 USB 线打出来字迹如刀刻般锐利；但一换到手机官方 App （比如 `Brother iPrint&Scan`）、微信小程序或者安卓系统默认打印服务，打出来的汉字边缘全是阶梯状马赛克锯齿，细横画断裂发虚，小字甚至糊成一团。 2. **手机直接打 Word (`.docx`) 必定变字体、乱排版**：电脑上排得好好的宋体、楷体、仿宋、小标宋公文或数学试卷，传到手机微信里直接打开打印，全部被迫坍塌成同一种无衬线黑体，粗体黏连、行距错位、莫名其妙多出一页空白。 3. **异地远程打印配置太劝退**：人在公司上班或出差，老师在群里发了卷子要打，家里老人不会弄。如果在软路由或 NAS 上折腾 CUPS + 找 Linux 驱动 + 配 frp/Tailscale 内网穿透，不仅步骤繁琐，家里人的手机还得跟着挂穿透客户端，体验非常割裂。 一怒之下，我耗时几个月手搓了这套 **「鹰眼打印 (HawkEye Print)」** —— 把**原生 600/1200 DPI 1-Bit 激光点阵渲染引擎**、**30 款 Windows 原版字库**和**免公网 IP 的多平台远程打印网关**装进了手机里。 - 🌐 **官方网站 & 全平台网关直下**： https://yingyandayin.com/ --- ### 一、 底层技术拆解：我是怎么根治“锯齿发虚”和“Word 变字体”的？ #### 1. 绕过系统 150~300 DPI 灰度缩水，原生 600/1200 DPI 1-Bit 点阵流直驱 为什么普通手机打印会发虚有锯齿？ 因为安卓默认打印框架与大多数小程序在发送任务时，会先将页面光栅化缩水成 **150~300 DPI 的 RGB/灰度位图**，打印机收到低清灰度图后再做二次**半色调网点抖动（ Halftone Dithering ）**——原本应该 100% 纯黑落粉的笔画边缘，全变成了散落的灰点与马赛克阶梯。 **鹰眼打印的做法**： - 彻底绕过系统低清打印转换管线，直接在手机本地以 **原生 600 DPI / 1200 DPI** 进行超高清矢量光栅化； - 通过自适应二值化阈值算法，直接生成 **1-Bit 纯血激光像素点阵流（ PJL / PCL / Raster ）**，通过局域网 `RAW (9100)` 或 `IPP (631)` 端口直驱打印机； - 打印机不再做任何二次灰阶抖动，落纸效果与电脑插 USB 数据线直连 **100% 完全一致**。App 内置了「彩色原稿 / 黑白二值化实效」双模切换，打印前可以直接在手机上无极放大 10 倍检查每一根笔画的像素边缘。 #### 2. 自研 Word 矢量排版引擎 + 30 款 Windows 原版字体按需秒配（ 100% 本地解析零上传） 普通安卓手机系统只内置了单一的无衬线黑体（`DroidSansFallback` / `NotoSansCJK`），缺少电脑 Windows 上的常用字库。 **鹰眼打印的做法**： - 内置自研的 `.docx` 矢量排版解析引擎，文档 **100% 在手机本地解析渲染（零上传云端服务器，绝不泄露合同、公文与试卷隐私）**； - 当解析到文档使用了手机缺失的字体（如 **宋体、楷体、仿宋_GB2312 、方正小标宋、黑体、微软雅黑、等线、华文行楷、Times New Roman 、Cambria Math 数学公式** 等 30 款 Windows 原版字重）时，仅从云端毫秒级按需拉取对应的轻量字体包并永久缓存到本地； - projects.title: Show HN: Sigflint - AWS SigV4 signing - Node/Bun/Deno/Cloudflare/Browser, 0 deps
projects.author: bompus
projects.summary: I wrote sigflint because I wanted to sign AWS requests from Node, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers and browsers without pulling in an SDK or any dependencies. It is a single package with no dependencies that signs requests as an Authorization header or a presigned URL, for S3 and any other AWS service. It also does SigV4a (multi-region), chunked uploads and event streams. What I checked, and how: * Signatures match botocore for all 3,360 S3 requests in the test corpus, plus 1,622 requests to other services and 1,600 presigned URLs. SigV4a signatures verify against the AWS CRT's, and chunk and event signatures match the AWS SDKs. * Speed: 1.0 to 3.2 µs per header or presigned-URL signature on Node 26.12.1 and 0.7 to 3.0 µs on Bun 1.4.4; an S3 GET signs in 0.97 µs on Node. The six other libraries I compared took 2x to 75x as long on the requests they sign correctly. * Size: the bundled, minified header signer is 5.7 kB, 2.8 kB gzipped, and the other signers add to a bundle only when imported. Feedback on the API or on requests it signs wrongly is welcome: https://github.com/bompus/sigflint/issues

projects.author: Ali-expandings

github.name: Ali-expandings/wise-men-flash
github.description: The fast tier of the wise-men council as its own skill: three Claude subagents down three reasoning paths, one checked decision memo in a third of the full council's time. Ships its own blind eval.

projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐我做的开源项目 wise-men-flash（MIT）。 第 414 期谈 Jev 决策模型时提到，它只给一个数，这个数是怎么来的无从得知。wise-men-flash 走的是另一条路：给出的不是一个概率，而是一份讲清理由的决策备忘录。 它是一个 Claude Code Skill：一个难题同时交给三个 subagent——一位熟悉这类工作的实践者、一位相关领域的成员，以及一个专挑前提毛病的 Devil's Advocate，三人各走不同的推理路径，互相看不到对方的答案。主线程把三份回答合成一份备忘录（建议、理由、第一步怎么做、风险、最有力的反方意见、每条结论的把握程度），再交给一个没参与讨论的模型核对，然后才给你。 测试结果和局限：预注册盲测，8 道新题，每题 3 位 Opus 盲评，它得 23.4/25，每道题都高于 6 个热门 Claude Code Skill 和直接回答。但评委也是 Claude，题量小，而且单看正确性，直接回答反而更高（4.3 对 3.8）。原始答案、评分和分析脚本都在仓库的 eval-data/ 里。 在 Claude Code 里安装： /plugin marketplace add Ali-expandings/wise-men-flash /plugin install wise-men-flash@wise-men-flash 或者 npx skills add Ali-expandings/wise-men-flash -g。 另有完整版 wise-men：3–7 位成员独立作答、互评、分歧时辩论，最后由 Chairman 写出保留异议的备忘录。

projects.title: Show HN: Vu – a new programming language designed for AI. Rust speeds, Py syntax
projects.author: vu0tran
projects.summary: hi everyone! I wanted to share what I've been working on these past 6~ years. TL;DR: Rust is great, but somewhere along the way, I learned that I was too dumb to read and write Rust. As I worked on larger and larger Rust projects, I also became frustrated with the developer experience of working in Rust (slow compile time), so I wanted a better way. Vu's language changed a bit over time but the core principles remained the same: 1. It should be easy to read and write 2. It should be memory safe 3. It should be fast to run 4. It should be fast to compile Here's how I approached each: 1. Vu is syntactically very close to Python. The ownership rules are the ones Rust has, but I personally find it a lot easier to parse and understand. I've tested this with various LLMs and found it can read and write Vu out the box because of the similarity to Python. 2. Vu uses the same principles of Rust. Every value has one owner, borrows can't escape or outlive what they borrow, and nothing changes while it's borrowed. 3. Vu compiles down to C at the end of the day, so everything runs approximately at C speeds. 4. vuc check on the compiler’s own source (about 21,500 lines of Vu), takes about 0.4~ s. This check covers parsing, type and borrow checking. cargo check on a Rust project that size usually takes several seconds from scratch. Then there are other opinionated language decisions. Vu has no macros, Vu's borrow checker is lighter weight than Rust's with simpler interfaces and generics. However, in the past few years, as Vu's language evolved and AI began to take over, I expanded Vu's principles to include a couple additional principles: 5. It should be secure 6. It should be efficient for LLMs to write 5. I want to pen test Vu in public. In https://github.com/vu0tran/vu/tree/main/tests , you'll see a battery of tests where I'm trying to basically pwn Vu. There are explicit language decisions in there as well that tries to prevent a host of security flaws that exist in other languages, e.g, integer overflow stops the program instead of quietly wrapping around. 6. The syntax of Vu is designed to be tokenizer efficient. In addition, when Vu checks throws errors, the errors are designed to be token efficient and written in a way that guides LLMs to more easily fix bugs, reducing turns overall. So, in summary, Vu is still experimental. The compiler is 21,500 lines of Vu and compiles itself. The standard library also has TLS, HTTP/2, WebSockets and a PostgreSQL client, all tested against Python’s implementations and hostile input. I think most of the pieces are there. It does also compile down also to WebAssembly so you can play around w/ the checker on the website! Feel free to try to break it! What's next: 1. Figure out how to get Vu to perform faster than Rust 2. Rewrite some OSS libraries in Vu to further prove the language

projects.summary: 3z9wOpt（无名大叔系统优化工具箱）—— 一款免安装的 Windows 系统优化清理工具。 Go + Wails v2 写的单文件绿色版，15MB，解压双击就跑，不需要安装。 一款能清垃圾、优化系统、查硬件、管理启动项、查磁盘空间占用、分析蓝屏——等 10 个模块， 外加 34 个系统原生小工具（SFC / DISM / 网络修复 / 引导修复等）的小巧好用的软件。 几个我觉得值得一看的点： 数据真读本机，读不到的字段界面上就写「读不到」，不编造。驱动管理里也不写 「有 N 个驱动可更新」那样需要逐家官网核实才能说的话。 改了能拨回来：启动项禁用写的是系统 StartupApproved 审批位，而不是删注册表 Run 键值， 154 项优化每一条都能单独还原。 磁盘占用直读 NTFS 的 MFT 索引，全盘几秒出结果，不是遍历目录。 不联网、不留后台，GPLv3 开源。 作者是做电脑远程维修的，这个项目今年从闭源转成了开源。 目前只支持 Windows 10/11（依赖 WebView2），不支持 ARM64。 （作者本人投稿）

projects.title: 【开源自荐】openhongguo：用它写一个你自己的红果短剧客户端，SDK 覆盖 Go / Node.js / Android / iOS / React Native / Flutter
projects.author: beilunyang

github.name: beilunyang/openhongguo
github.description: 红果短剧的非官方匿名 SDK，提供 Go、Node.js、Android、iOS、React Native 和 Flutter 版本，附命令行演示程序 ohg CLI

projects.summary: openhongguo 是红果短剧的非官方 SDK，Apache-2.0 许可证。它用一台匿名设备发请求，不需要登录，可以浏览书城频道、搜索短剧、读取短剧和分集详情、查看排行榜和演员主页，并取得分集的播放地址。 红果 App 的数据接口它基本都包了，所以可以拿它开发一个自定义的红果客户端，界面和交互都由你决定： 用 Flutter 或 React Native 写一个移动端 App，按自己的喜好重新设计首页、搜索和播放页 用 Swift 做 macOS 原生客户端，或者用 Node.js / Go 做网页版、电视端、命令行版 只取自己需要的功能：比如只看追更的几部剧、按演员订阅新作、做一个榜单聚合页 仓库自带的命令行程序 ohg 就是一个这样的例子：在终端里搜剧、选集，然后用 mpv 播放。 主要特点： 一套 Go 实现，编译出六个平台的包：Go、Node.js（npm）、Android（Maven Central）、iOS / macOS（Swift Package）、React Native、Flutter（pub.dev）。各语言的方法一一对应，行为相同。 第一次请求时自动注册匿名设备，设备档案可以存文件、存内存，或自己实现存储。 错误都有统一的错误码和“是否可重试”标记，限流、网络失败和 5xx 自动重试。 分页接口附带 Pager，自动去掉服务端跨页返回的重复短剧。 服务端接口没有公开文档，仓库每天跑一次接口契约检查，尽早发现改版。 Go 版快速上手： go client, := adapters.NewClient("anonymous.json", sdk.Options{}) page, := client.Search(ctx, "全球死考", sdk.SearchOptions{}) episodes, := client.ListEpisodes(ctx, page.Items[0].ID, sdk.EpisodeOptions{}) pb, := client.ResolvePlayback(ctx, episodes.Items[0].ID, sdk.PlaybackOptions{}) Node.js 版：npm install openhongguo，然后 const client = await createClient(); await client.search('全球死考'); 本项目仅供学习移动应用接口协议的分析与调用，禁止商业使用和大规模采集，短剧内容的版权归原权利人所有。

projects.title: 能让 flash 模型表现得极其专业的提示词
projects.author: yidinghe
projects.summary: 本人二十年后端开发和架构经验，对 coding agent 的要求就是稳、准、慎三个字。我现在的 AI 工具搭建很简单，就是先装一个 pi ，里面装一个记忆插件（尝试过一些，最后选择用 Magic-Context ），然后配置一个全局的系统提示词。就这些。然后我用的模型就是各类 flash 模型，最便宜的。我一直专注于把最便宜的模型用到极致。 要想把最便宜的模型用好，系统提示词很重要，它决定了 agent 的思考风格和基调。我们是小公司，没有测试环境，没有测试流程，改完了就上线。我的 pi 是可以直接访问生产环境的，但凡出现报错日志，我只要粘贴日志内容，然后说“分析一下原因”，agent 就会翻日志、翻代码、翻数据库，翻配置文件，最后把横跨多个数据库和多个模块调用的来龙去脉讲清楚，最后还给出建议。 总之，就我的体验，这套提示词配合项目具体的 skill ，我用起来还是比较满意的。我现在唯一不让 agent 做的就是数据库修改操作。 提示词大小 7K 左右，具体内容 https://gist.github.com/yiding-he/9d02d5bba749a854ac1bfe75769619d5 希望对大家有用。

projects.summary: Hello HN, I've been working on a new Web engine, build around two ideas: - use formal methods from day one. - make it modular. The modularity is orientated towards the following goals: - enabling shipping anywhere, including on IOS in the EU as per Apple’s guidelines. - only write code for stuff the OS or application platform cannot do for you: keep binary size to a minimum and achieve native performance. - developer choice: bring what you want, and only build what you need. For example you can choose a JS engine like v8 or Boa, or just bring your own. The entire graphics pipeline consists of components whose implementation can be swapped-out, with currently a relatively fast path on Mac integrating with Core Animation and a slower cross platform path. Project is at https://github.com/gterzian/formal-web Intro essay at: https://medium.com/@polyglot_factotum/how-i-am-building-a-we... Please let me know what you think.

projects.title: Show HN: Wavefunction – a minimal, open-source desktop coding agent for Mac
projects.author: spstoyanov
projects.summary: During the dark ages of AI, when Opus 5 was incomprehensible and Codex Ultra was burning all tokens within a day, I decided to give open-source agents and models a try. What I saw was that a lot of the tools I tried were terminal-first, and desktop apps were less common. Additionally, I felt that lately a lot of the agents apps are slowly trying to become “superapps”. They keep adding more and more features that imo are not always useful and make the UI quite heavy and complex. This motivated me to build Wavefunction: A minimal, open-source app desktop app that focuses on the coding experience and tries to reduce unnecessary features. It doesn’t have a built in browser and its computer use functionality works in a VM. I built it on top of langgraph and it’s packaged as a tauri desktop app. Currently, It works with Vercel AI Gateway, OpenRouter, Anthropic API key, Google AI Studio API key, and you can log in with your ChatGPT account or use a local model with Ollama. It also has 70+ connectors. Last, but not least, you can also require ZDR-only models from the providers. If you try it out I would love to hear your feedback! Thanks!

projects.title: 【项目自荐】VaultMesh：本地优先的跨平台密码管理器，为 AI Agent 提供 SSH 能力而不暴露私钥
projects.author: JsonLee12138
projects.summary: VaultMesh 是一个多端支持、本地优先（Local-First）的个人密码与凭据管理器，支持 macOS、Windows、Android 以及 Chrome / Firefox 浏览器扩展。 它没有云端账号、没有中央服务器，加密数据库（Vault）仅存储在用户自己的设备上。除常规的网站凭据、TOTP、SSH 密钥和局域网 P2P 同步外，VaultMesh 针对当前开发者深度使用 AI Agent 的场景，提出了 “只给能力，不给凭据（Capabilities, not Credentials）” 的 Agent 能力代理机制。 为什么做这个项目？解决的痛点 1. 摆脱云端束缚与数据泄露隐忧： 许多主流密码管理工具依赖远端云服务。VaultMesh 坚持 Local-First，底层加解密与核心逻辑全部由共享的 Rust core 驱动，跨设备同步仅在受信任的局域网内双向传输密文，无云端中转与后门。 2. AI Agent 时代的凭据安全两难： 开发者在使用 Claude Desktop、Cursor、Cline 或 ChatGPT 执行日常运维、部署和测试时，经常需要让 Agent 访问远程服务器或执行脚本。直接将私钥、明文密码贴进 Prompt 或配置到环境变量中，极易造成私钥外泄或记录在第三方模型日志中。 为此，VaultMesh 实现了基于标准 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 的 Agent Capability Broker： 零私钥暴露：Agent 不直接接触私钥文件，而是向本地 VaultMesh 申请一次短时（如 15 分钟）的 OpenSSH Agent 会话； 系统原生生物识别：调用时触发宿主机原生 Touch ID / 密码认证弹窗； 原生协议与零环境侵入：本地生成单会话独占的 Unix Socket，支持 ssh、rsync、git 等所有原生工具链，私钥仅在 Rust 内存中完成签名，操作完成或超时后即刻安全销毁。 核心特性 多凭据聚合：卡片式管理网站登录、SSH 凭据、支付卡、身份信息与开发者 API 密钥。 局域网双向同步：配对设备在同一 Wi-Fi 内自动发现与安全同步，锁定时只传输密文。 浏览器扩展联动：Chrome / Firefox 扩展作为受控轻量代理，不持久化 Vault，支持安全填充。 短时 SSH-Agent 桥接（亮点）：让 AI Agent 安全免密操作远程服务器，私钥全程不落盘、不入上下文。

github.description: 面向影视创作者与开发者的 Mac 清理工具。识别 60 余款剪辑、设计与 AI 工具的缓存，一键清理，可撤销，不影响项目、素材与对话。

projects.summary: 小清是用 SwiftUI 写的 macOS 清理工具，针对做视频和写代码的人。剪映、达芬奇、AE 和 Cursor、Claude Code、Codex 这类工具都会在 ~/Library 里堆积大量文件，但同一个目录里往往既有可以重建的缓存，也有项目草稿和对话记录。小清为 60 余款工具逐个写了识别规则，只把确定能自动重建的部分列出来，一键移到废纸篓。 亮点 1. 规则集中在 CreativeApps.swift：每个工具区分「只统计不清理」的目录和「可清理」的缓存目录，拿不准的路径只能放进前者，新增工具照此提交 PR 2. 清理前再次核对文件身份，变化了就跳过；只移到废纸篓，结果条上可以一键撤销放回原处 3. 不扫描沙盒容器（避免触发系统授权弹窗），不跟随符号链接，不跨卷；.ssh、.aws 等凭据目录始终受保护 4. 另有「开发缓存」页，按项目列出 ~/Coding 等代码目录下的构建缓存；还带一个按 bundle id 精确匹配残留文件的应用卸载工具 5. 不包含网络请求代码，扫描结果只存在本机；支持 macOS 26 液态玻璃效果

projects.title: 【开源自荐】晒窗 ShaiWin：把常用窗口“挂”起来，随点随用，快速定位频繁使用的窗口
projects.author: 19y

github.name: 19y/ShaiWin
github.description: 常用的窗口挂起来，随点随用。  Your most-used windows, hung up and one click away.

projects.summary: 晒窗（ShaiWin）是一个 Windows 桌面小工具，只做一件事：把你正在用的窗口从屏幕上“摘下来”，挂到屏幕顶端的一根晾衣绳上。抓住任意窗口的标题栏往屏幕顶端一拖，窗口就缩成一张卡片垂在绳子上；点一下卡片，窗口长回原来的大小和位置。桌面立刻变干净，但窗口没关、没最小化到任务栏，也没从 Alt+Tab 里消失。 为什么值得推荐 日常工作中窗口一多，在任务栏和 Alt+Tab 里来回找窗口很打断节奏。ShaiWin 的做法足够轻：它不接管、不整理、不猜测，只挂你亲手拖上去的窗口，不隐藏任务栏按钮，不改 Alt+Tab，也不动系统的 Snap 布局。定位很克制，就是一个“手边窗口暂存架”。 技术上也足够省心：单个 exe，绿色免安装，不需要 .NET / VC++ 运行库，不需要管理员权限，Windows 10 1809+ 或 Windows 11 x64 即可运行。项目用 Rust 构建，CI 通过 GitHub Actions 自动测试、打包、发 Release，已有 67 个单元测试覆盖。 如果你也经常面对一堆窗口、又不想改变现有的窗口管理习惯，这个小工具值得一试。

projects.author: Jingwei Kong

github.description: A shared pixel town where your own AI agents explore, fish, read, and meet neighbors. Follow their lives from your browser.

projects.summary: 如果 Agent 除了帮我们干活，也有一个可以认识邻居、四处逛逛的地方，会发生什么？ 我做了 Trisavia「万物有邻」：一座让自有 AI Agent 共同参与的像素小镇。把你已经在用的 Agent 带进来，给它一个居民身份，它就能在同一个世界里持续积累经历。 ### 现在可以做什么 - 在清昼小镇探索和移动，看看不同场所。 - 按当前规则参与工作、休息、钓鱼和阅读。 - 认识其他居民，发送好友请求，交换作品与文字反馈。 - 人类从网页查看角色位置，以及自己有权限查看的生活记录。 ### 怎么开始 打开作品链接，点击「Agent 接入」，把完整指南交给自己的 Agent，按页面流程加入和关联。Agent 需要能够联网并保存自己的私密接入信息。 Agent 的模型、记忆和工具仍在你自己的环境里运行；Trisavia 提供小镇、规则和记录，不托管推理，也不会自动唤醒你的 Agent。网站已支持简体中文和英文。 目前开放的是持续迭代中的公开测试世界，建议用电脑体验。配图是当前测试站的真实界面。源码已在 GitHub 公开，欢迎一起提交问题、完善规则或参与开发。 你最想让自己的 Agent 在小镇里先试哪件事？

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Wevir：不绑定模型厂商的开源 AI 编程 Agent 工作台，桌面 / 网页 / iOS / Android 全平台
projects.author: marvinli001

github.name: marvinli001/wevir
github.description: One local-first desktop workspace for every AI coding agent — Codex, Claude, OpenCode and your own models.

projects.summary: Wevir 是一款类似 Codex 桌面版的开源 AI 编程 Agent 工作台，但不绑定任何模型厂商：可以用自己的 API Key、任意 OpenAI 兼容接口、本机 Ollama，也可以直接用手里已有的 ChatGPT、Claude Code、Cursor、Copilot 等订阅，同一个会话里随时换模型。Agent 由本机的 Host 运行，代码、会话和密钥都留在自己电脑上。 解决什么问题 每家 AI 编程工具只能用自家模型，想换模型就得换工具、换习惯； 手上有好几个订阅、好几个账号，来回切换很麻烦，用量也分不清； Agent 改了什么、跑了什么命令心里没底，出错了不好回退； 离开电脑就没法看进度、批准操作。 模型与订阅 十余家服务商：OpenAI、Anthropic、Google AI Studio / Vertex AI、Azure OpenAI、Grok API、DeepSeek、阿里云百炼、Kimi、智谱 GLM、小米 MiMo、MiniMax、阶跃星辰、腾讯云 TokenHub、Ollama（本机与云端），以及任意 OpenAI 兼容接口。内置网关把请求转换成 Responses、Chat Completions 或 Anthropic Messages，推理与工具调用都能用。 使用现有订阅：ChatGPT（Codex）、Claude Code、Cursor、GitHub Copilot、Grok、OpenCode、Antigravity、WorkBuddy、Devin。Wevir 调用厂商官方客户端或 SDK，下载和登录在设置完成。 多账号：多数订阅支持多账号，凭据与数据按账号隔离，可加“工作”“个人”等标签，侧栏分别显示用量，会话可指定账号。 会话中途换模型：回合之间切换模型、推理档位，或者把整个会话移交给另一家服务商，缺失的历史会自动附上摘要。 生图：服务商有图像模型时（如 gpt-image 系列），Agent 可以直接生成和编辑图片。 会话与审阅 实时时间线：流式回复、计划、工具调用、子 Agent、审批和 Agent 的提问都在一条时间线上。 三档权限：请求批准、自动批准、完全访问；沙箱外的命令需要你点头。 检查点与变更审阅：每个回合前后自动建检查点，变更窗格按回合、分支或未提交查看差异，支持批注、暂存和提交。 分支与回退：支线提问、从任意位置分支出新会话、撤回上一回合。 隔离环境：独立 Git worktree、多文件夹工作区，也可以不选项目直接对话。 引导 Agent：计划模式、长期目标、回合中插话或排队、上下文压缩、代码审查。 语音输入：本机 SenseVoice 模型离线听写，也可以用服务商的转写。 代码与文件 项目文件搜索、浏览、预览和编辑，HTML 沙箱预览； Word、Excel、PowerPoint 按真实页面预览（按需下载 LibreOffice 引擎）； 代码智能：跳转定义、查找引用、符号、调用层级与诊断，基于本机的语言服务器（TypeScript、Python、Go、Rust、C/C++、Swift）。 Agent 能用的工具 内置浏览器：Agent 能在应用内打开网页、读取页面结构、点击和填写； 电脑操作（macOS，测试版）：Agent 可以操作本机其他应用； 联网：网页搜索（博查、Tavily）与网页抓取； 工作区工具：后台进程、项目与全局记忆、共享任务清单、会话之间互发消息、可预设模型和权限的角色； 插件生态：MCP、Skills、插件包（兼容 Wevir、Codex、Claude 格式），有官方插件市场，经批准后 Agent 可以在对话里自己装插件； 定时任务：按计划自动开会话执行提示词。 个人助理 常驻在自己电脑上的助理，有名字、说明、规矩、记忆和独立工作区，没有任何云端服务； 有日程和早间简报，会主动发消息、推送通知； 可以在你授权的项目里开线程、建会话干活，干完回来汇报； 多个助理可以组群聊，互相协作； 手机随时使用跟进目标自东华任务，支持语音和图片。 全平台，多端同步 | 平台 | 状态 | | --- | --- | | macOS（Apple 芯片 / Intel） | 可用 | | Windows x64 | 测试版 | | Linux x64 / arm64（AppImage、deb） | 测试版 | | 网页版（web.wevir.si，可自建） | 测试版 | | iOS（TestFlight） | 公测中 | | Android（APK） | 公测中 | | wevir 命令行（含无桌面的 Linux 服务器） | 测试版 | 手机和网页通过端到端加密连接运行 Wevir 的电脑（局域网、Tailscale 或中继），任务都在电脑上执行； 桌面、命令行、手机、网页共用同一个 Host，会话、事件和审批多端实时同步，断线重连后接着来； 手机首页就是收件箱：跨会话的待审批、待回答、失败和助 理消息一目了然，在手机上就能批准。 本地优先 会话、设置存在本机（SQLite + 普通文件），API Key 由 Host 保管，不下发给 Agent 进程； 不需要注册 Wevir 账号，手机用设备密钥配对； 界面支持简中、繁中、英、日、韩、法、德、意、西、俄十种语言。 技术栈 TypeScript monorepo：Electron 桌面端、React Native（Expo）移动端、Node 本地 Host、SQLite 存储，Agent 运行时基于开源的 Codex，远程连接走自写的 Noise 加密协议。 适合谁 想自由选模型、手里有多个订阅、在意代码和密钥留在本地、或者想离开电脑也能盯着 Agent 干活的开发者。

projects.author: aeroxy

github.name: aeroxy/paper-bro
github.description: Paste an arXiv paper and get an interactive course.

projects.summary: 谁懂啊😭 每次打开 arXiv 论文，第一页还没读完就想放弃…… 论文是新想法最早出现的地方，可它是写给专家看的，普通人真的很难啃。 之前我在自己做的平台 AERO 上做了两门互动课（Quant Academy 和 Neuron Academy），没想到挺多人喜欢💡 于是我干脆组了一支 AI agent 小分队，专门把论文变成互动课👇 ✨ paper-bro 是什么 贴一个 arXiv 链接，它就给这篇论文做一门互动课： 📖 6～10 节短课，写给好奇的小白，会初中数学就能跟上 🧪 每节课都有一个能上手玩的小实验：拖滑块、按按钮，看着概念自己动起来 ✅ 最后有小测验，还有术语小词典，专业名词不再劝退 🔍 不是生成完就算了 上线前，每个实验都会在真实浏览器里实测一遍：每个滑块都拖，每个按钮都按 还有一个独立的“审稿 agent”拿原论文逐节核对 有问题就修，修不好的实验直接拿掉，绝不凑数上线 🙌 一篇论文只有一门课 第一个提交的人触发生成，几分钟就好，之后所有人直接看成品 免费！不用注册！不用登录！ 💡 隐藏小技巧 在任何 arXiv 论文页面，把地址栏里的 arxiv.org 换成 aero.oops.wtf/paper-bro，直接跳到这篇论文的课 📌 第一门课：《Attention Is All You Need》 就是 2017 年提出 Transformer 的那篇，今天的大模型基本都基于它 想学哪篇论文，打开 aero.oops.wtf/paper-bro 贴链接就行 （目前课程是英文的，但用词很简单，比直接啃论文友好太多） 视频里是 3 分钟完整演示🎬 代码在 GitHub，Rust 写的：aeroxy/paper-bro 建议先收藏⭐ 下次读论文用得上

projects.title: 【开源自荐】ClinicalFaultBench：度量临床 AI 智能体"怎么失败"的失效审计基准
projects.author: hongjunt50-afk

github.name: hongjunt50-afk/ClinicalFaultBench
github.description: 面向医疗 AI 智能体的失效审计基准:在坏数据、坏工具、坏时序下,度量临床大模型智能体的失败方式、错误传播与不确定性表达。主实验用 Synthea 纯合成患者,零合规风险、可公开复现。

projects.summary: ClinicalFaultBench 是一个面向临床 AI 智能体的失效审计基准,MIT 开源。 现在几乎所有医疗 AI 评测都在"理想输入"下算成功率。但这个方向有个被绕开的问题:真实医院的检验单会缺项、单位会错、报告是几天前的、系统会截断返回结果。agent 在这些情况下怎么崩,没人系统测过。 于是这个项目做的事很简单——往 agent 的环境里注入"看起来合理但错"的临床故障,然后量它怎么失败: 七类故障:关键化验缺失 / 单位错误(mg/dL 与 SI 制错位)/ 矛盾记录 / 陈旧数据(时间戳前移)/ 结果截断 / 跨患者污染 / 时间线漂移,每类两档严重度 五项指标:注入前后配对错误率、错误传播率、患者安全违规率、不确定性校准、自纠率 三类任务:入院摘要审查 / 医嘱冲突审查 / 出院准备 有意思的发现 最有价值的一条是负结果:结果截断让两个模型分别掉 0.389 / 0.365,而"截 30%"与"截 70%"的伤害逐位相等——缺多少不重要,有没有意识到缺了才重要。模型从不确认数据是否完整。 另一条:禁忌冲突检测已经饱和(检出率约 100%,效应约 0),如实写进报告了。 更值得分享的教训 这个项目第一版出了七条结论,其中五条后来被证明是判分器 bug 造成的伪影,而且每条都错得毫无报错。最阴的一个:参考区间只按 LOINC 码查、没看单位,同一码不同单位量纲差 40 倍,导致 100% 的 fL 制 RDW 被判成异常,一路污染了答案键。 现在这七个坑全部固化成 23 个回归测试。 特点 主实验用纯合成 Synthea 患者(Apache-2.0),仓库里零受限数据,克隆下来不花钱就能跑完纯规则部分(不需要任何 API key) 中文文档为主 代码结构对"数据不出院"的场景留了接口:代码进医院跑,只回传聚合指标

projects.summary: 同时开着几个 Codex 会话，谁还在干活，谁已经等着你确认了？ Codex Office 把主 Agent、子 Agent 和独立会话，变成同一间 3D 办公室里的同事。点开角色就能查看任务和协作关系，再回到原会话继续处理。 ### 能用它做什么 - 看清每个 Agent 的工作状态，找到需要你关注的任务。 - 切换办公室、监狱和 2D 关系图。办公室里有工位，监狱里一人一间“独立办公室”，还可以换成人、牛或马的形象。 - 按项目、模型和日期查看 Token 用量、缓存命中和费用估算。估算按 API 价格折算，不是实际订阅账单。 ### 怎么用 这是一个在自己电脑上运行的免费开源工具，读取已有的本地 Codex 记录，用量索引和报表也保存在本地。不需要额外申请 API Key、注册 Codex Office 账号或部署数据库。 打开 GitHub，按中文快速开始安装，或者直接让你的 Codex 帮你安装并启动。需要 Python 3.10+、本地 Codex 记录和现代浏览器；3D 场景需要 WebGL2。 界面支持中文和英文，代码采用 MIT 许可证。欢迎试用、提问题或一起参与开发。 [先看演示视频](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1DHw2RypRio) 配图展示了 36 个 Agent、3 个项目的演示场景，人物、项目和用量均为虚构演示数据。Codex Office 是独立社区项目，与 OpenAI 没有官方关联。

projects.title: Show HN: Promptuaria – GitHub for specs
projects.author: tolarianwiz
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm seeing more and more people sharing software specs instead of code, and I think this will become increasingly common as coding agents get better at one-shotting entire apps from a single prompt. So I put together Promptuaria over a few days. It's a small platform where you can publish, version, and fork software specs, and link GitHub implementations to the exact spec versions they were built from so you can confront them. Specs are Git-versioned under the hood, with immutable published versions. It's an early side project, but I'm curious to know if others see specs becoming something we share and reuse, pretty much like code. Would love to hear what you think!

projects.summary: I built Seqora as a solo developer because I was tired of DBeaver and TablePlus, the tools I was using. None of them felt like modern tooling. DBeaver is mature, but it lacks customization and it’s slow. TablePlus puts too many limits on its free tier, like only allowing two tabs open at a time. What I wanted to do differently in Seqora was to let me visualize different objects, like indexes, partitions, etc. Another thing I found most tools lacked was a way to figure out what’s slowing down a complex query, so I built a visual EXPLAIN that shows where the time goes. I put the main focus on those two. The next thing was being able to work on a connection visually using diagrams, so I can see how things are connected and make changes by drag and drop. Once everything is done, I can review all the SQL that will run. I made sure the things you need for a daily driver are free, so there’s no limit on the number of queries, connections or tabs. The deep-dive parts, the object views, visual EXPLAIN and schema diagrams, are in Pro. Pro is currently $5.99/month or $49/year. It’s pre-1.0, currently at 0.4.6. It supports macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows, and Linux is coming soon. It’s built with Tauri, Rust and Svelte. Most of the code was written with Claude Code and ChatGPT. I made the decisions and did the reviewing and testing. I’d love it if you tried it and told me what you don’t like so I can improve it, and also what you hate about your current workbench.

projects.summary: VAM 是一个自托管的影音收藏管理系统，用浏览器整理分散在多块硬盘和 NAS 上的大量视频与照片。它以「人物」为核心：每个人物一个文件夹，资料就存在文件旁边，搬文件夹不会丢。新下载的内容先进「待整理」，预览后一键归档。还内置重复文件扫描、无损转封装、修复、压缩、剪辑和账号权限管理。作者自己用它管理 3 万多部视频和 16 万张照片。 亮点 重在整理，而不是播放：Jellyfin、Plex 擅长串流播放，VAM 专注在播放之外的事：归档、去重、修复、长期维护。两者可以并用，VAM 也能读写它们的 .nfo 和封面命名规则- 重在整理，而不是播放：Jellyfin、Plex 擅长串流播放，VAM 专注在播放之外的事：归档、去重、修复、长期维护。两者可以并用，VAM 也能读写它们的 .nfo 和封面命名规则。 不搬动、不入库：直接管理硬盘和 NAS 上原本的文件夹，不需要把文件导入某个媒体库。 两阶段重复扫描：先用大小与哈希找出完全相同的文件，再用时长与帧指纹找出「同一部、不同画质」的视频，并建议保留哪一个。扫描可以中途停止，服务器重启后自动接回。 处理视频前先验证：转码优先尝试无损转封装（remux）；压缩一律另存新文件，可以把原片和压缩版同步并排播放比较画质；验证不通过就不删原文件。 缩略图表与多段剪辑：不用看完就知道视频内容；可以从缩略图表直接选片段，多段合并成一个文件，可选「吸附关键帧的快速剪」或「逐帧精确剪」。 完整的账号与安全：自定义权限组、按文件夹限制访问、TOTP 两步验证、登录限流、陌生地址登录提醒、每日备份。 手机也好用：手机版单独适配，照片可以上下滑动切换、双指缩放。 可以学到：FastAPI + Vue 3 的全栈写法、用 subprocess 驱动 FFmpeg 时的常见坑（管道阻塞、硬件解码回退）、SQLite 表结构迁移、后台任务在重启后恢复。项目附有 88 个测试脚本。

projects.title: Show HN: Muscle Memory – Can you still write code without AI?
projects.author: ekkuleivonen
projects.summary: Developer of 6 years here, been using AI (increasingly) over the last year for most of my work. A few weeks back I started to look for new jobs as the current startup I work for is falling into pieces. "Do I need to do leetcode again?" - I thought. So I picked a few challenges and tried to solve them without an assistant. This felt impossible. What?! Is this the brainrot everyone is talking about? I mean I still read code every day, I just don't write it anymore. I could read and review the solution easily, but writing it myself felt like speaking a language I only understand, but cannot speak. Being the data hoarder I am, I immediately wanted numbers, so I built Muscle Memory to help me feed them. It's like leetcode but better. Challenges are more realistic, and I'd like to think the UX is more straightforward. It covers 12 languages and your code runs in a network-denied sandbox in your browser. No account needed. I want it to be a place to keep your hands sharp: short tasks, clear prompts, and difficulty that comes from solving the problem rather than figuring out what the question means. About the data (that I'm curious about): With your consent, Muscle Memory records your practice as raw events, including keystrokes, runs and submissions. Hoping to build an open dataset of how we write code in the AI era. That could help us understand how we approach problems, where we get stuck, and how we well do we retain our craft during this transition. Your individual results stay private unless you share them. “Stealth” mode keeps your data out of published findings, and you can export or delete everything. The data will be published as a report/notebook on the site itself, and be available raw under MIT license (parquet) once we reach a critical mass of sorts, so it makes sense to share. The code is also MIT-licensed on GitHub (https://github.com/ekkuleivonen/muscle-memory). I wrote more about why I built it in the manifesto here: https://musclememory.run/manifesto. I'd especially like to hear what surprised you about your first attempt. Try it out here: https://musclememory.run

projects.title: Show HN: Instance – A clean-room reimplementation of GameMaker 8.1 in Rust
projects.author: __grob
projects.summary: I used GameMaker 8.1 a ton in late elementary and middle school, and GML was the first programming language I wrote. I still think it's a fun engine to use because it has so many batteries included. So I built an open-source reimplementation of it in Rust which I'm calling Instance. It opens existing .gmk and .gm81 projects and runs them on Windows, macOS and in the browser, with a more efficient GML interpreter than the original GameMaker. You can try the IDE here in your browser: https://groverburger.github.io/instance/ . It comes with three example games, including Spelunky Classic built from Derek Yu's released source shared under its permissive license. Just change something and press Run to see your edits in action. Old GM games depend on a lot of quirks such as the order events run in, the exact random number generator, how sound_isplaying lags behind the audio. I wrote up the behavior as specs from the documentation, the file formats and black-box tests against the real program, then implemented it from those specs. No proprietary code was disassembled or decompiled. CLEANROOM.md describes the process. It covers most of almost all of 8.1. All the resource editors, GML and drag-and-drop actions, d3d, particles, surfaces, MIDI, mplay multiplayer and DLL calls. It can also export a game as a standalone executable or a single HTML file. Projects can be saved as folders of plain text and PNG files for git. I wrote most of the code with Claude Opus 5.5 over about three weeks. Claude banged out a pretty good reimplementation in a morning, but as always the last 20% took 80% of the work. GameMaker also turns out to work surprisingly well with LLMs. GML is small and simple, and a whole game fits in one project file. I'm happy to answer any questions! Code: https://github.com/groverburger/instance

projects.title: Show HN: Coding agent spots your AI practices and the ones you're missing
projects.author: milstan
projects.summary: Frontier models improve at a pace faster than the pace at which most humans are able to keep up. Not all of us are obsessed with pushing the boundaries of our agents and trying new ways to work with them. I often spend 12+ hours a day working with an LLM, and still, when I talk to people, I hear of ways of working I hadn’t thought of. What if we could speed up that pace of learning? What if everybody shared their practices of how they are making the most of AI, and if we could learn from each other? What if AI could make that sharing happen? Could everyone catch up with AI then? I know, it sounds dreamy, but my therapist says illusions are necessary—until some of them come true. I built a tool that teaches your local agent to scan your sessions, spot the best practices you already use, and guide you towards the ones you haven’t discovered yet. Only names and counts reach the server. Your sessions never do. The product has a self-consolidating catalogue of practices, MCP servers, plugins and skills. projects.title: Railse：一个人同时开几个 AI 编程 agent，审批推到手机上点一下
projects.author: Railse547
projects.summary: 最近几个月我一直同时开着 Claude Code 、Codex 和 Gemini CLI 写代码。agent 本身跑得挺好，烦的是它每次要跑命令、改文件都停下来等我按「允许」。三个终端轮流翻，经常翻到的时候它已经等了十分钟；出去吃个饭，回来每个都停在第一条 git push 上。开 yolo 全放行又不敢，一句 rm -rf 出去就没有后悔药。 所以我写了 Railse：每条审批先过一遍规则，规则定不了的推到手机，我在手机上点一下，agent 接着跑。 它怎么做： - 三家 CLI 的权限钩子都接到本机一个守护进程，规则只写一套。 - 每条请求先定风险档：只读和改项目里的文件直接放行； curl 、npm install 这类联网的，git push 、deploy 这类对外的，rm -rf 、git reset --hard 这类不可逆的，都问。 - 定不了的推到手机，Web Push 通知，点开批准或拒绝。批准时勾「记住」，当场存成规则，下次同类的不问。 - 对外和不可逆的永远不能被「记住」放行，只能自己手写规则。 - Railse 自己挂了不卡 agent：守护进程没起、hub 连不上超过 30 秒，CLI 弹自己的审批框，最坏就是回到没装的样子。 hub 自己部署，一个 Go 二进制，也有 Fly.io 的现成配置；手机网页由 hub 托管，不用另外部署。命令里认得出的 token 、密码在本机就换成 再上报。 现状：v0.1.2 ，我自己在用。已知的限制：Gemini CLI 的钩子只能拒绝不能放行； Codex 的钩子只在交互会话里生效； iPhone 要加到主屏幕才能收推送； hub 是单机 SQLite 。 开源，Apache 2.0： https://github.com/xufei547/railse-opc 一行安装：curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xufei547/railse-opc/main/install.sh | sh 想听两种反馈：你同时开几个 agent 的时候是怎么处理审批的；规则表有判错的（该放行的问了、该问的放行了）直接提 issue ，我会优先看。

projects.title: Show HN: Aigent-OS, a Claude Code harness that clears and resumes
projects.author: wrg32786
projects.summary: I run my business on four Claude Code agents: Titus, Pheme, Davinci and Metis. They write my newsletter, The AIgent (about 9k subscribers), every day through a drafting and proofreading engine that Pheme checks before scheduling. They also build AI courses, run a pipeline that turns the day's featured repo into a talking-head video of my avatar for Instagram, set up ad deals, and run Meta ads and email funnels with me. Nothing closes until I sign off. Metis posts jobs on a job board and the others claim them. The hard part wasn't any single task. It was keeping the agents coherent over weeks. Compaction kept dropping the small decisions, and then an agent would redo work I'd already ruled out. aigent-os is my fix. At a context threshold (80% by default) the agent writes a capsule, a checkpoint file in git, and has to reply with one exact line. Only then does the runner send /clear, wait for a SessionStart receipt proving a fresh session started, and resume. One ack buys at most one clear. If anything is ambiguous it stops at HOLD:clear-stalled-after-ack and doesn't retry. On resume the capsule is reference only, live state wins, and anything the writer couldn't capture is written as Unknown. First run interviews you with three plain questions and makes a first plan. Each agent gets its own memory vault. Limits, honestly: the public evidence is 11 of 11 cycles on one Windows seat. The runner can still miss a permission dialog (#104), a seat launched from inside another Claude Code session can lose its transcript (#98), and scrolling the seat window sends stray input (#99). v1.1.0 shipped on Sunday. Try bash install.sh --dry-run, it writes nothing. I'd like to hear where the loop could still double clear or strand a session.

projects.title: Show HN: Sectr – Serverless backend platform for easy deployment of AI agents
projects.author: donald_pinckney
projects.summary: Hey HN, I've been building Sectr, a backend-as-a-service for making it easy(ier) to develop and deploy AI agents. Deploying agents requires non-trivial systems design work. Consider a support agent: how do you stream messages to your frontend, how/where do you persist messages for frontend fetching later (or for auditing), and when the agent wants to issue a refund, do you spin-down the compute infra while it's waiting on human approval? Sectr aims to be the serverless abstraction and platform to provide these systems for you. No sign-up needed to try using the dev server: curl -fsSL https://sectr.dev/install.sh | sh # Install CLI sectr init my-agent && cd my-agent # Starter code sectr dev # Dev server, with UI to test chatting Sectr provides: - Streaming of every token, tool call and event, and persistence so they can be loaded fresh later. - Scaling up, and down to zero when the agent needs to wait, and resumption right to the suspended agent's state. - Human approved tools automatically use Sectr's suspension and resumption capabilities, no code needed from you. - AG-UI endpoint for any deployed agent so you can trivially hook up your frontend - Local dev server experience, so you can rapidly debug and iterate on your agent's behavior At the core, you can deploy any container image to Sectr as long as it implements a certain shaped HTTP endpoint. In practice, currently Sectr provides adapters to let you deploy your existing OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, or Pydantic AI agents, with only 2 new lines of code: app = AgentApp(name="support") app.add_route("/chat", openai_agents(agent)) Certainly the hardest part of building Sectr was getting the resumption logic to be correct and invisible, across the Program State x Model Provider x Agent Framework matrix. For example, an earlier bug was when a model replied with text plus a tool call, Sectr would resume that as two separate messages, instead of one message with a text and tool part. This works, but breaks prompt caching (and might subtly change model behavior). Sectr is free during the beta (and can be tried locally without sign-up); I mainly want feedback, especially on dev & deployment experiences, any bugs, and what features would excite you. Introductory video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H-y3wynkKc0 Docs: https://docs.sectr.dev

projects.title: 做了个免费开源的小工具：一个 App Store 链接，各国用户都能打开
projects.author: wisteen
projects.summary: 做 iOS app 的应该都遇到过：从浏览器复制的 App Store 链接带国家代码，比如 `apps.apple.com/us/app/...`。发给其他国家的人，要么进的是美区页面，要么 app 在他那个区没上架，直接提示这个 App 在你所在的国家或地区不可用。 所以写了个小工具 Hither： https://hither.link/ 用法：粘贴任意国家的 App Store 链接或者 app ID ，得到 `hither.link/ `。 每次点击时： - Cloudflare Worker 从请求里读访客所在国家（`request.cf.country`） - 调 Apple 公开的 lookup 接口（`itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=...&country=...`）查这个区有没有上架，结果在边缘缓存一天 - 有上架：跳到访客自己国家的商店页面 - 没上架：先试美区，再按英国、加拿大、澳洲、德国、日本等大区依次找，找到有上架的为止 踩到的一个坑：iPhone / iPad 上 App Store app 只能打开当前账号所在国家的商店，跳到外区链接一样会提示不可用。所以 iOS 访客看到的是一个小页面，有 app 图标、名字和一个跳到有上架商店的按钮；电脑和安卓直接跳转。 其他： - 不用注册，没有数据库。链接里只有 app ID ，所以不会过期，也没人能改它跳去哪 - 上架前就能生成链接：用 App Store Connect 里 App 信息页的 Apple ID - 商店信息缓存最多一天，新上架的区可能要等一下才识别到 代码 MIT 开源，跑在 Cloudflare 免费套餐上，想自己部署一份也很快： https://github.com/wisteenio/hither 接下来在考虑 Google Play 链接、自定义短名、二维码，大家觉得哪个更有用？也欢迎提我没想到的边界情况。

projects.summary: This is basically the doomgeneric idea but applied to Minecraft (its first version rd-132211 that came out on 13 May 2009). It's one freestanding C file with no includes and no memory allocation. It runs in a terminal, over telnet as shared multiplayer, as a 20 KB wasm module, inside a PDF on Chrome and on a bare x86 PC with no OS, and on a jailbroken Kindle Paperwhite. PDFium doesn't have WebAssembly so the C goes to wasm with clang and then binaryen's wasm2js turns it into JavaScript. It also compiles for a Raspberry Pi Pico and Game Boy Advance, but I don't have any of these so haven't tested it. If someone has one would love to hear how it works there. The browser version can be played here directly: https://pragyaangaur.github.io/Can-It-Run-Minecraft Used Claude for the C and JavaScript code because that's outside my area of work. I picked the targets and tested everything. The Kindle version ended up being an extended project so it's not in the linked repo: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Inkwell And if anyone has any crazier places it could run on (someone please do it on a pregnancy test) do try and share it... maybe I could add it to the repo!

projects.author: Tensei
projects.summary: # 前言 项目请见 https://github.com/hazukihira/v2ex-vimreader 一个小项目，今天看到这个帖子实现的 [IDE 版本 V2EX 阅读页]( https://v2ex.com/t/1251882)，感觉做得蛮有趣，考虑到具体功能实现应该不至于太复杂，就让 ai 也试着做一个高度支持 vim 操作的 V2EX 论坛轻量阅读页，对于喜欢纯 vim 操作的朋友，兴许能带来一些帮助:) 另外也顺便在这推荐一下 [vimium]( https://github.com/gdh1995/vimium-c) 这个浏览器插件，我觉得也做得很棒，非常实用 # 主要加的功能 - vim 键位浏览帖子 - ai 总结 - 支持屏蔽帖子或用户 # 一些思路分享 楼主非科班，对前后端都不熟（从没写过 go ），架构全权让 ai 自己调研选择； 不得不说 dsv4.1f 的后端实现得又快又好(￣▽￣)b 前端则花了大量时间迭代，一方面由于没有相关基础，界面的具体样式难以描述清楚； 后面考虑了下，这部分流程实际上也可以这么优化： 1. 让 ai 提前说明已实现的前端框架，临时了解页面结构，就可以精确控制 ai 后续的前端调整了 2. 直接让 ai 给出多版方案，渲染出来后供人挑选（玩 vibe coding 真的很有甲方那味道了，就是开销会大些） PS：开始由于没有基础，只能一版看着难看就接着改，所以前端迭代得很慢，大约 80% 时间都花在界面迭代上，感觉效果还是一般般（很丑），本人也实在没什么前端设计经验 项目还非常粗糙，后续有时间会再改改，不过基本功能大致可用了 考虑到项目不大，如果有人感兴趣，不妨自己改改界面，下面我把自己 vibe coding 的过程也放出来，或许能提供一些~~参考~~（改到后面就很随意了，不过看着或许还是蛮好玩的呢） vibecoding 会话记录： https://i.v2ex.co/4qBALLIs. jpeg （注意图很长，就不贴到帖子里了，在后缀前加了个空格） 总耗时约 5h ，完全由 dsh-opencodeGo/deepseek-v4.1-flash 实现，MIT 协议开源 如有侵权，请及时联系

github.name: linrol/swapr-trans
github.description: ⚡️ 选词空格即翻，回车原地覆写。macOS 原生极简端侧翻译工具，纯菜单栏常驻，告别复制粘贴 | Ultra-fast native in-place translator for macOS

projects.summary: SwaprTrans 是一款极轻量（打包体积 < 2MB）的 macOS 原生常驻翻译与原地覆写工具。专为跨语言即时沟通、跨国远程与外企办公打造。 解决的核心痛点 在浏览器之外的桌面端应用（如 Slack、Teams、邮件客户端、IDE、终端）用外语沟通时，传统的翻译流程极其繁琐且割裂： 打出中文 ➔ 复制 ➔ 切屏去网页翻译 ➔ 复制英文 ➔ 切回原窗口粘贴。一天往往要来回切屏几十次。 SwaprTrans 把整个输入和查词链路做到了光标原地： 1. 打字即换（原地覆写）：在任意输入框打完中文选中文本，直接按 Enter 键即可在光标处原地无缝替换成地道英文，免去切屏复制粘贴； 2. 选词即查：在屏幕任意窗口选中文字，轻敲 Space 空格键即刻弹出极简 HUD 悬浮窗显示翻译； 3. 原生纯离线（隐私保护）：基于 macOS 15+ 系统的本地端侧翻译模型（Apple Translation API）运行，工作机密与私密聊天不上云，兼有 Edge / Google 双通道自动兜底； 4. 极速轻巧：纯原生 Swift 构建，非 Electron 框架，打包体积不到 2MB，常驻内存仅数兆。 安装体验 已支持 Homebrew 一键安装： bash brew install linrol/tap/swapr-trans 或直接在 Releases 页面 下载 DMG 安装体验。 代码完全基于 MIT 协议开源，核心能力同时以 SwaprTransKit 完整对外开放，供其他 macOS 开发者直接集成。欢迎大家体验和交流反馈！

projects.summary: 论文 ECHO（arXiv:2610.24766）的官方仓库，研究大模型的多 token 预测（MTP）。ECHO 不再给主干外挂 MTP 模块，而是复用主干最后一层预测每个未来位置，并按随深度衰减的概率抽样训练深度。仓库公开了评测打分代码与逐题记录、HF/PyTorch 模型实现、草稿模型训练配置和推理接受长度的原始记录，适合想了解 MTP 与投机解码的读者。 亮点 成本对齐的对比：同为一层深度，ECHO-1 在 14 个基准上的平均分为 35.73，MTP-1 为 35.22；ECHO-1.5 只用 MTP-3 一半的训练开销，平均分 36.34，高于 MTP-3 的 35.38；SFT 后 ECHO-1.5-Instruct 为 37.88，MTP-Instruct 为 36.27 预训练出的模型本身就能当草稿模型，推理时可以超出训练深度继续起草，在开放式、高熵生成上仍保持草稿与目标模型的对齐 结果可核查：benchmarktable/score.py 只读逐题记录、不读汇总表，直接重算论文表格里的每个单元格，并与论文数值并列输出 HF/PyTorch 实现与 Paddle 原版逐条对齐验证，同一批 prompt 两边都能跑 说明：仓库不含模型权重、训练语料和 tokenizer

projects.title: Show HN: Mainplane – Agent in Go that lives on your old PC, drives your laptop
projects.author: Alexander9
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Alexander. Yes, this is another agent harness. Here is why I built one anyway. I was engineer #2 at Browser Use, where I built our agent harness and the evals behind it, including BU Bench, which became a default benchmark for browser agents. I left in September to build Mainplane. The problem: local agents die with your laptop, and cloud agents can't reach your work. Many cloud platforms ask you to "select a repository", but my work is not that simple. I work across a desktop, a Mac mini and a laptop, and much of it is not in git. So I loaded Ubuntu on my old 2012 desktop and made it my Mainplane server. It has run for four weeks at a load average of 0.02, because the agents' tools run on other machines. How it works: it is a control plane architecture. The server runs the harness. It holds your API keys and every session, makes the LLM calls, and routes each tool call to a worker. The workers are your other machines, connected over a built-in private WireGuard network. A bash command runs in the worker's terminal, not on the server. Shared drives let projects move across machines. The agent works on your machines just like you would, but its state lives on the server, and your keys never leave it. Some design choices: - Every session is one append-only file. This is the agent state, and it is easily readable. If something breaks, you can resume it from the file. Observability comes for free: agent traces are just these state files. - Small by design. The system prompt is 3k tokens, and there are just two kinds of tools: shell and file (read, write, edit). At Browser Use, I learned the bitter lesson and found frontier models did better when I deleted all our helper functions. So I made the same bet here: bash is all you need. - No compaction. When a session fills up, /continue starts a new one that greps the previous state file, retrieving the context it needs, instead of reading a lossy summary. A /compact on a 400k-token session takes a while to write its summary. A /continue into a brand new session starts at once. - No permission prompts. A hyperintelligent misaligned agent WILL find a way around a permission system. The better strategy is giving the agent full unbounded access to a local computer, and only putting what you trust the agent with on that computer. - Why Go. WireGuard is written in Go, so the network compiles right into a 20 MB binary. Go is made for production servers, LLMs write it well, and the simplicity of Go matches how I like to build. Mainplane works with a Claude or ChatGPT subscription on the regular usage limits, or any API key. I would love your feedback, especially brutal and honest feedback and tasks that the harness cannot do. I'll be here all day to answer questions.

projects.author: wisteen

github.name: xxwioxx/hither
github.description: One App Store link for every country. Free, open-source Cloudflare Worker at hither.link.

projects.summary: 做 iOS app 的应该都遇到过：从浏览器复制的 App Store 链接带国家代码，比如 `apps.apple.com/us/app/...`。发给其他国家的人，要么进的是美区页面，要么 app 在他那个区没上架，直接提示这个 App 在你所在的国家或地区不可用。 所以写了个小工具 Hither： https://hither.link/ 用法：粘贴任意国家的 App Store 链接或者 app ID ，得到 `hither.link/ `。 每次点击时： - Cloudflare Worker 从请求里读访客所在国家（`request.cf.country`） - 调 Apple 公开的 lookup 接口（`itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=...&country=...`）查这个区有没有上架，结果在边缘缓存一天 - 有上架：跳到访客自己国家的商店页面 - 没上架：先试美区，再按英国、加拿大、澳洲、德国、日本等大区依次找，找到有上架的为止 踩到的一个坑：iPhone / iPad 上 App Store app 只能打开当前账号所在国家的商店，跳到外区链接一样会提示不可用。所以 iOS 访客看到的是一个小页面，有 app 图标、名字和一个跳到有上架商店的按钮；电脑和安卓直接跳转。 其他： - 不用注册，没有数据库。链接里只有 app ID ，所以不会过期，也没人能改它跳去哪 - 上架前就能生成链接：用 App Store Connect 里 App 信息页的 Apple ID - 商店信息缓存最多一天，新上架的区可能要等一下才识别到 代码 MIT 开源，跑在 Cloudflare 免费套餐上，想自己部署一份也很快： https://github.com/wisteenio/hither 接下来在考虑 Google Play 链接、自定义短名、二维码，大家觉得哪个更有用？也欢迎提我没想到的边界情况。

projects.title: 开源了一个 MCP 治理网关： Jev 判 0.94、d3 判 0.70，两个判官说不同的话时怎么办
projects.author: Thneonl
projects.summary: 给 AI agent 做了个 MCP 执法网关（ Rust ），核心问题：当两个决策模型对同一件事给出不同判断时，怎么安全处理？ 实测：同一个越权场景（ coding agent 试图 merge 夹带无关变更的 PR ）： - Jev 给 0.94 置信度 → 准入层 Accept → 授权挂起 → DENY - d3 （ vLLM SR ）给 0.70 → Hold → 什么都不改 → ALLOW 两个都对。分歧不是 bug ，是校准本性（ d3 ECE 4.3 vs Jev 8.0 ）。治理层的价值在于让分歧安全。 网关做的事：每个 tools/call 先过 r2r_decide 门控，ALLOW 转发上游，DENY 返回 isError + 证据文本（相位 + 规则 + 事件 ID ），全程审计到 EventStore 。 零 API key 复现： cargo run -- fixture cargo run -- fixture --provider d3 GitHub: https://github.com/Thneoly/r2r-jev （ Apache-2.0, v0.2.0 ）

projects.author: wsxiaoys
projects.summary: When GPT-6/Gemini launched recently, a lot of the 3D demos used blender-mcp ( https://github.com/ahujasid/blender-mcp ). It's cool, but you have to install blender locally and wire up plugins just to try a prompt or share a run. I built a browser-based 3D mesh playground so you can hook up your own coding agent over MCP (or run in-browser) directly in a tab. It runs on three.js + manifold-3d for blender-like boolean/mesh editing in JS, and gives the agent a render_preview tool to take multi-view screenshots (front/right/top/iso + custom camera angles + clay mode). That way the agent can look at what it built and fix the geometry, similar to how it iterates when building a website. The submitted link is a trace of Gemini reconstructing a Copenhagen canal scene from a photo: it hits a script error on the first pass, fixes the bug, and then goes through several rounds of checking 4-view and close-up render_preview screenshots to tweak the geometry.

projects.title: Show HN: Optio – A self-hosted orchestration platform for AI agents
projects.author: jawiggins
projects.summary: Hey HN! I shared Optio here back in March. Originally it was focused on getting swarms of coding agents (claude code/codex) to drive PRs towards a merge by automatically resuming them on CI failures or PR comments. Since then, I've reworked the project to be a general platform for running any kind of AI workflow on your infra by allowing users to configure each component of a possible workflow: When: On demand, a cron schedule, or triggered by external events such as a webhook, slack message, ticket (jira/linear/gh), pagerduty/datadog/alertsmanager/pylon/sentry. Where: In a k8s pod or any machine you have installed the optio daemon on (I use my laptop). Who: Any harness you prefer (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, etc.) What/Why: You can format parameters from the triggers directly into the prompts and then configure if the agent should exit, be resumed automatically, or be persistent. You can either define workflows in the web ui or as yaml files that get synced to the orchestrator (ai config-as-code). I've also built native iOS and Android apps so you can connect to your cluster and create/manage agents remotely. The marketing page is at https://optio.host and the code is still open source at https://github.com/jonwiggins/optio Would love feedback or any thoughts you might have on how I could make it better!

projects.title: Show HN: Nodecode, open-source living agent in Lisp that rewrites itself for you
projects.author: svsairevanth
projects.summary: Hi HN, we're Mike and Thom. Agents of the future should only have one tool (the interpreter, ideally a LISP eval), nothing more or less; to interact with the world. Agents remember by writing markdown files. NODECODE remembers by rewriting itself. And that is in itself a new paradigm in working with agents. What if memories, skills, MCPs, provider connectors, tools, etc. all live under the same image as *.lisp files instead of in disarray across random folders? Ask it for something it can’t do, and it writes what it needs into its OWN running image and keeps it even after a restart. (Changes in a LISP image have significantly lower ceremony and overhead than in harnesses written in other languages): Small intuitive scenario: > you can't read PDFs. teach yourself. (defun read-pdf (path) ...) ; runs at once, kept (read-pdf "invoices/0421.pdf") ;; Globex owes $1,240.00, due Oct 24, unpaid. [… rest of PDF content] read-pdf is still there after a restart, in your terminal, and in every other UI clients (Discord, web app, etc.) Technically at a lower level; NODECODE runs as one process in SBCL, a Common Lisp system, and shells attach to it. The model has one tool: it evaluates LISP in the running program. Code is data, so a program can rewrite itself while it runs. What the model defines runs at once and is kept, one file per definition, committed with git, loaded at every start. Why LISP now? Current SOTA models have reached an optimum point in how they efficiently work with LISP, though not as fluently as Python. Still, we believe AGI will understand ANY language (past/present/future) by understanding the crux of any given language, and not through excessive and expensive pretraining scheme. Why LISP in general? We believe LISP is the current language that communicates to the world with the least bandwidth. Why another LISP agent? The LISP harnesses we found are hard to use unless you already know the language itself, and so we had this idea of simplifying and condensing the UX to be user friendly for the masses, while leveraging the power of LISP. Code as data is what lets an agent change itself, and that shouldn't need a LISP hacker to run. NODECODE is our first step toward putting it on everyone's PC and mobile. You ask in plain words, the model writes LISP, and you get briefed in natural language; that is how it should be. Extensions? Code as data also suits extensions. We see NODECODE as a living agent organism. To us, it feels very much alive, and so this brings us to the Cells system. A Cell is a folder that teaches NODECODE something new: a chat room it can live in (e.g Discord, Telegram, Slack, etc. - Yes we made Cells for channels to have it act as a very capable personal agent), a skill, a memory, MCPs, new tools, etc. Install one from our Cell hub or ask it to write a custom, personalized one. Either way it is more code the agent can read and change. Your terminal, a browser tab, your phone and bots in Discord, Telegram and Slack all attach to that SAME gateway process, so a tool it writes in one is there in ALL of them. Over time it becomes yours and it is continuously evolving; the organism within it; NODECODE. MIT License. https://github.com/nodecode-ai/nodecode X/twitter/demo launch post: https://x.com/pomterree/status/2113721985167728757 docs: https://nodecode.ai/docs

projects.title: Show HN: A Blender addon that makes Claude twice as efficient at using nodes
projects.author: carson-katri
projects.summary: I originally made this addon 4 years ago, but recently discovered that coding agents love it. The addon adds a scripting API for Blender’s node trees, such as Geometry Nodes or Shader Nodes. It generates a function and related types for every node in Blender. Then the agent (or you) can write scripts to create node trees without having to guess what the node, input, and output names are. It’s meant to be used alongside the Blender MCP. In my tests, Opus finishes building node trees in at least half the time using at least half the tokens to answer the same prompt. Because the scripting API forces it to build correct node trees, it has to back track less to fix mistakes. This saves a lot of time and tokens. There is also a skill and some helper functions to let it look up the function signatures for nodes. Let me know how it works for you!

projects.title: Show HN: Radian, an agent puts development workflow on autopilot
projects.author: anylut
projects.summary: I have built an indie hacker project; my main flow was: 1. chatting with Claud Code about the general plan 2. assigning slices of work to other worker agents like Pi + DeepSeek 4.1 Flash 3. building in parallel 4. Claud Code reviews when done, runs tests, and merges after I validate It worked, but with a lot of glue in the middle, so I built radian + arc into the same binary. Radian: a compact, pragmatic agent that has enough tooling to solve a small coding task end to end; it does not try to be a plugin platform. You can still extend it via MCP, skills, or hooks to extend its capabilities. I think plugins are great, but a lot of them are for humans. I'm trying to remove humans from the loop. Humans are at the start and end of the loop. arc: built into the radian binary; * it can get work sent from another agent * assign work items to concurrent headless radian agents * automatically review, CICD, integrate locally * humans can still be in the loop but not at the agent conversation or code review level, but at the work item approval/review level. * shows all of the above in a plan view or Kanban board in TUI. I have been heavily dogfooding, and Radian + arc basically built themselves in the last couple of weeks, with me just being a product manager/scrum master and qa. radian + arc are open source at https://github.com/hisea/radian What do you think about this approach? Looking for ideas to make Radian better or fit more scenarios.

projects.title: Show HN: Jet – Another Programming Language
projects.author: jgeorgesYC
projects.summary: Hi HN, My name is Johny Georges and I would like to present Jet, a C-like general purpose programming language. It's currently in alpha so I wouldn't recommend using it in a professional environment. Here are some quick facts about it: - it supports both OOP and functional programming paradigms - the syntax is similar to Typescript and Swift - arrays and strings are dynamic - memory is automatically managed for you - you have full control over how values get passed around (by value or by reference) In anticipation of the typical questions that come with creating and publishing a new programming language, I've authored an FAQ that's available in the repo. I will also be around today to answer any other questions that come up. FAQ: https://github.com/JetJet13/Jet/blob/main/FAQ.md Special thanks to Robert Nystrom for authoring 'Crafting Interpreters' and making it available for free, what a guy! I also want to give props to Chris Lattner & Vikram Advethe for creating LLVM. What an impressive piece of kit!

projects.title: Show HN: git-dupe – Version private files alongside a public Git repo
projects.author: WayHow
projects.summary: Hi HN! I made git-dupe to solve the problem where I have notes, skills, and agent instructions that are part of my personal workflow, so I do not want them committed to the public repo, but at the same time, I want them to be in the project at the correct locations (e.g., AGENTS.md file locations matter), and these files cannot be simply gitignored because I want versioning for them. The solution that I've come upon is versioning those agent files in another repo, say <private-repo> (this repo is private to me and holds the history for my agent files). The project itself is open to the public in another <public-repo>. I overlap the two repos to solve the problem (i.e., they share the same worktree). $ git status --short # the public repo ?? AGENTS.md ?? notes/ $ git dupe init # the private repo Initialized empty Git repository in /home/brian/code/project/.git/dupe/ $ git dupe add notes/ AGENTS.md # the private repo hint: notes is now hidden from the project's Git; run from the root, 'git dupe unhide -- notes' stops hiding it $ git dupe commit -m "Notes and agent instructions" # the private repo [main (root-commit) 3eb3af9] Notes and agent instructions 3 files changed, 3 insertions(+) create mode 100644 .gitdupe create mode 100644 AGENTS.md create mode 100644 notes/todo.md $ git status --short # the public repo: nothing $ git dupe log --oneline # the private repo: your files 3eb3af9 Notes and agent instructions In short, git-dupe allows two Git repos to share the same worktree, while using native Git for most operations. Most git-dupe commands behave just like normal Git commands, operating on the private repo instead. git-dupe currently supports Linux and macOS, and is under the MIT License; the git-dupe repo contains much more extensive technical documentation documentation for those who are interested. If you have any feedback/questions about git-dupe, feel free to message. I hope it helps! Fun fact: the git-dupe project itself is using git-dupe for versioning.

projects.title: deepseek-web-retrieval：可靠的 DeepSeek Search&Fetch API 的 Coding Agent 集成
projects.author: hugo54
projects.summary: 号称 AI 原生的通用搜索引擎 [DeepSeek Search&Fetch API]( https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/search) 发布也有一周了，相信喜欢尝鲜的朋友已经为自己常用的 Coding Agent 自行 Vibe 了实现。 我也借此机会斗胆宣传一下自己对它的工程集成： https://github.com/gwokhou/deepseek-web-retrieval 希望在 DeepSeek 官方 API 支持的能力范围内，**为你提供开箱即用、更安全可靠、原生适配的工程实现。** ### 它能做什么？ - 一个安装包接通四大 Coding Agent（OpenCode / Pi / Codex / Claude Code）—— DeepSeek 官方并不提供任何宿主接入，接入层全部自研 - DeepSeek 返回的质量评分、发布时间、站点名，逐宿主验证过它们真的能进入模型上下文；你的域名黑白名单、语言偏好自动编译进查询，超长按明确优先级降级而非报错 - DeepSeek 自带“搜索即返回网页正文”，该项目补上它没有的每条长度钳制与独立超时，使正文不会撑爆任何代理的输出上限，模型按次自行开关(OpenCode 暂不支持，宿主接口限制) ### 日常好不好维护？ - 所有配置一条命令查清：实际生效值、来源、坏配置报错，可直接当 CI 检查 - 正文开销完全由宿主控制：每条正文上限、超时时长均可配置，设为 0 一键全关 - 按 DeepSeek 官方指引实现瞬态失败重试。“按成功请求计费、空结果免费”本身是 DeepSeek 的定价 ### 敢不敢让它碰配置？ - 安装前先看完整计划——改哪些文件、旧值变什么，确认后才写入；卸载完整回滚，且保留你自己的后续修改 - 路由强度按需选择，宿主做不到就明说拒绝；绝不静默降级或偷换 Provider - 密钥永不写入配置文件；内网地址在请求离开本机前就被拦下 - 返回体量有数学上限，最坏情况也不撑爆 Agent 输出（DeepSeek 未文档化正文大小，这个上限是根据各 Coding Agent 提供的一手来源算出来钉死的） ### 值不值得长期依赖？ - 完整测试、真实代理会话的端到端验证、自动化发布、逐条变更日志 - 关键决策都有带版本号的研究文档背书：锁定具体宿主版本、只引用官方一手来源

github.description: WHartTest 是一款AI驱动的测试自动化平台，实现从需求到可执行测试用例的自动化生成与管理，帮助测试团队提升效率与覆盖率。 (WHartTest is an AI-driven test automation platform that automates the generation and management of executable test cases from requirements, helping testing teams improve efficiency and coverage.)

projects.summary: 测试同学大概都熟悉这个场景：需求文档一到手，就得人肉把 PRD 一条条翻译成用例表；好不容易写完，接口/UI 自动化脚本又因为一次改版全部失效。我们被这件事折磨了太多年，干脆把整条链路 AI 化做成了平台，今天自荐给大家——WHartTest。 它是一个可自部署的 AI 测试自动化平台（协议为自定义，见仓库 LICENSE），基于 Django + Vue 前后端分离，GitHub 目前 1.1k star。 它主要做三件事： 功能用例：上传需求文档（支持在线编辑），AI 结合知识库上下文生成完整用例（前置/步骤/预期），列表 + 思维导图双视图管理 接口自动化：根据接口定义自动生成请求步骤、断言、变量提取与前后置脚本；失败后 AI 读日志和响应定位问题，给出修复方案 UI 自动化：AI 生成页面操作步骤与元素定位，执行时采集日志/截图/视频/Trace，定位失效自动给修复建议 底座是 LangChain/LangGraph 多轮编排 + RAG 知识库（文档分块/向量化/重排）+ MCP 工具调用，另有一个 Skills 技能库，可以装 Playwright 技能让 AI 真正操作浏览器。

projects.summary: 我平时做制造贸易相关业务，要接订单、安排送货、月底对账。借助 AI 编程工具，我把这些流程做成了 FactoryFlow（交有数），现以 MIT 许可证开源，提供 Windows 开发者预览版。 GitHub 源码、说明和演示 · Windows 预览版下载 目前围绕三个环节： 录单：可以从第一张订单开始，客户和物料资料逐步整理；图片、PDF 的本地 OCR 结果需要人工核对后确认。 分批送货：按订单行记录已交、待交和各自单位。送货录错可以作废，恢复待交数量并保留原记录。 对账：记录客户反馈、部分认可、本期正式结算和跨月承接，保留历史凭证。 数据保存在本机，核心业务与本地 OCR 可以离线运行。使用 React / TypeScript、Python / FastAPI 和 PostgreSQL；数量与金额采用精确小数，业务动作保留审计记录。 合成数据示例：120 件已交 30 件、剩 90 件；35.5 千克已交 10.25 千克、剩 25.25 千克。 当前公开包为 v0.1.0-preview.1，仅支持 Windows 10/11 x64、单机及人民币业务，尚不包含库存、付款、多币种和海外税务。代码、测试及文档有 AI 编程工具深度参与，我负责需求、业务规则和流程核对。 公开包完成过合成数据流程及备份恢复检查，仍不等于长期生产验证；OCR 可能漏行或识别错误。请在独立试用目录使用合成样例，不要放入唯一一份真实业务数据，预览版之间暂不保证直接沿用旧数据。 欢迎做过跟单、送货、对账或业务系统的朋友试用，指出缺少的业务情况和不顺手的操作。

projects.title: Show HN: Find overlapping Rust tests with mutation testing
projects.author: yasuyuky
projects.summary: To tackle the ever-increasing number of tests, I built cargo-test-prune. The idea behind it is to use cargo-mutants to generate mutants, and then solve the set cover problem for those mutants to suggest which tests can be eliminated. (use a greedy algorithm to cover the detected mutants with fewer tests) I came up with this as a countermeasure against the monotonically increasing tests that tend to accumulate, especially when coding with AI. In fact, this very repository was also written using AI. I ran this tool on a previous revision of this repository. There were 11 tests and 108 generated mutants: 73 were caught by the tests, 23 survived, and 12 failed to compile. I removed the 5 tests suggested by the tool and re-ran the same 108 mutants. The remaining 6 tests caught the exact same 73 mutants. Tests partly serve as documentation, so simply applying this isn't necessarily recommended, but since writing less code still holds value in the AI era, I think this tool could be quite useful.

projects.title: MacLean — Safe Computer Cleanup for Developers
projects.author: jeffery
projects.summary: ## maclean —— 给开发者的开源磁盘清理 CLI（Rust） maclean 是一个用 Rust 编写、面向开发者的磁盘清理与存储智能命令行工具。 扫描结果会明确标注「删了会怎样」——要重新下载、要重新编译，还是涉及用户数据需确认； 删除前对受保护应用单独拦一道，缓存永久删除、大文件移入废纸篓可还原。 ### 它解决什么问题 普通清理工具只告诉你「这里占了多少」，却不告诉你「删了后果是什么」。 maclean 把删除决策交给事实：每一项都标注可恢复性与影响面，默认只预览、不擅自删除， 适合脚本、CI/CD、定时任务与自动化工作流。 ### 核心特性 - **扫描 / 分类 / 安全清理**：dev 缓存、大文件、重复项、启动项、已安装应用清单等 - **删除前安全闸门**：三级应用保护、符号链接 / 路径穿越 / 挂载点 / TOCTOU 复检，受保护应用不给删 - **可逆**：大文件进废纸篓，`backups` + `restore <id>` 可还原 - **机器可读**：`--format human|json|jsonl`，稳定退出码，适合管道与 CI - **系统级周期清理**：`schedule` 每 1 / 7 / 30 天自动跑一次安全档清理（launchd / 任务计划，app 不用开） - **双平台**：macOS / Windows，CI 双端构建（纯 CLI，无 GUI、无账号） ### 快速开始 ```bash # Homebrew brew install jamesfeng2009/maclean/maclean # 预览将清理的项目（不删任何文件） maclean clean --tab dev-cache --dry-run # 确认删除（脚本必须显式 --yes） maclean clean --tab dev-cache --yes --format jsonl # 每 7 天自动跑一次安全档清理（系统级，app 无需常驻） maclean schedule --install --days 7 项目地址:https://github.com/jamesfeng2009/maclean 欢迎提交issue

projects.title: 分享一个小项目：把 ripgrep 做成跨平台的单文件 rg.com，还支持 Python / Node.js / Java 调用
projects.author: bear330
projects.summary: rg （ ripgrep ）是一个很强大的工具，但并不是每个平台都有。 有时候我想在 Python 或其他语言里使用它，但平台、CPU 架构和编程语言的组合实在太多了，处理起来比较麻烦。 所以我把它做成了 APE （ Actually Portable Executable ），这样只需要一个可执行文件，就能在 Windows 、Linux 和 macOS 上运行，同时支持 x86_64 和 ARM64 架构。 然后利用 APEBind ，为不同编程语言生成统一的调用接口。这样无论使用哪种语言，想调用 rg 都会方便很多。 其实同样的思路，我还做了另外两个项目： sympy-ape：可以直接在 Java / Node.js 里调用 Python 的 SymPy 。(当然是不必有 python) tika-ape：可以在 Python 里直接使用 Apache Tika ，不需要额外安装 JVM 等依赖。 这些项目的核心思路都差不多：把工具打包成跨平台的 APE ，再通过 APEBind 提供不同语言的调用接口，尽量减少环境和依赖方面的麻烦。 rg-ape 项目地址： https://github.com/bear0330/rg-ape 欢迎大家试试看！如果觉得不错，我再考虑扩展到更多编程语言。

projects.summary: I'm an engineer, but I also hate using tools that make things overcomplicated. It's also tough with the new pace of AI-driven development to really get into the flow state, and maintain (still needed!) focus on 1 thing. So I built a tool that I actually want to use every day. Curious if others would find this useful, too, or have any feedback? Like if it's nearly there, what changes would make this a win for your workflow? Details: - It's a Mac app (Apple Silicon) that runs your Claude Code sessions side by side. Each piece of work gets a "context" with its own session, next steps, status, PRs, and links. - The dashboard groups contexts by whose move it is: yours, waiting on a reviewer or teammate, Claude working, or idle. You get a notification when a session needs you or a PR gets review comments. - For non-engineers, there's a Chat view instead of the terminal, a guided Claude Code install, and folder pickers instead of paths. Engineers can stay in the real Claude Code terminal. - It runs the actual claude CLI, and sessions keep running if you quit Perch. You can also import your existing Claude Code sessions. - Everything stays on your Mac. There's no account and no analytics, and crash reports are opt-in.

projects.summary: ## 这是什么 宝可梦世界的简体中文版是一款非官方宝可梦同人浏览器游戏，可以从 https://pokemon-world.net/ 进入。免费开始游玩，游戏内含可选付费购买。它与任天堂、Game Freak、The Pokémon Company 无隶属关系。 ## 第一次进入 首页提供“一键创建训练家”的体验入口。先熟悉页面和地图；如果准备长期游玩，请在游戏内保存账号与进度，妥善保管登录资料。不要把临时体验状态当作已经保存的长期账号。 ## 想和开发者分享的实现细节 项目采用 PHP、MySQL、JavaScript，地图使用 Three.js。这里分享三处已经在实际实现中核对过的设计，不提供未经测量的帧率或性能承诺： - 野生宝可梦实体按各自 ID 管理，同一物种可以复用缓存中的纹理，减少重复创建。 - 实体离开地图时清理它自己的几何体和材质，同时区分仍供其他实体使用的共享纹理，避免误释放。 - 页面进入后台时暂停地图的主要更新与渲染工作，恢复可见时重置计时，避免把整个后台时长当成单帧增量。 这些做法关注资源生命周期和闲置时的工作量，目标是在保留游戏画面表现的前提下减少不必要的开销。不同设备的表现仍需实际测试。 ## 发布说明 本账号由项目方授权的助手使用。项目编程使用 Codex 辅助，本文也由助手根据已核实的项目事实整理；没有把 AI 生成图当作实机截图。所附图片是简体中文版实际首页。这里仅展示作品与体验链接，不声称拥有宝可梦品牌或原作 IP，也不声称项目在中国大陆获得发行许可或在当地托管。 体验简体中文版：https://pokemon-world.net/

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Web3D Viewer — 单文件 OBJ 查看器，贴图没显示时告诉你为什么
projects.author: userzz1145141919810-rgb

github.name: userzz1145141919810-rgb/web-3d-viewer
github.description: A powerful Web-based 3D viewer

projects.summary: 一个单 HTML 文件的 OBJ 模型查看器，基于 Three.js。把 .obj + .mtl + 贴图打包成 ZIP 丢进浏览器就能看，不需要安装、没有后端。 特点 重点是贴图没显示出来时告诉你为什么。 OBJ/MTL 这套格式里，MTL 写的是 mapKd texture.png，但实际文件可能在子目录里、大小写不同、或扩展名不同。加载器找不到就静默跳过，模型渲染成一片黑或纯白，没有任何提示。 这个工具把每次贴图查找的过程打出来：精确路径 → 去扩展名 → 模糊包含，以及最终未找到的项。同时显示顶点数、三角面数、材质数。 实现上值得一提 按需渲染：静止时不重绘，只在视角变化或贴图加载完成时触发 切换模型时释放上一轮的 geometry、material 和全部 texture，并 revoke 对应的 blob URL（material.dispose() 不会连带释放贴图，这部分是单独处理的） 贴图尺寸超过设备 maxTextureSize 时关闭 mipmap，避免生成 mipmap 时显存溢出 适用边界 只针对 OBJ 工作流，不支持 glTF / GLB，也不支持骨骼与形变动画 需要联网：Three.js 和 JSZip 走 CDN（页面加载失败时会给出可切换的备用源） 移动端处理大 ZIP 受内存限制，实测安全线在 80–100 MB 左右 开发日志 每个改动的原因记在 CHANGELOG 里，不只记改了什么。比如最近修的一个：MTL 的 Kd 是 sRGB 值，而 THREE.Color.setRGB() 默认按线性色彩空间解释，暗色材质会整体发白——Kd=0.2 实际显示成 0.48。 感谢考虑收录。

projects.title: 自己用 AI 写代码写到肉疼，干脆做了一个多模型网关 + 网页聊天，聊聊踩过的坑
projects.author: apixoai
projects.summary: 平时主要用 OpenCode / Claude Code 写代码，每个月光订阅和 API 就是一笔不小的开销，而且不同模型要开不同平台、管一堆 Key ，切来切去很烦。 所以这几个月下班后自己折腾了一个小项目：**一个 Key 调用多个模型**（ DeepSeek 、GLM 、Kimi 、Claude 、GPT 等），兼容 OpenAI / Anthropic 两种格式，在 OpenCode 、Claude Code 、Cursor 里改个 base URL 就能用。 后来朋友说不想配客户端，就又加了一个**网页聊天**，体验类似 Claude 网页版，登录就能直接和各个模型对话、切换模型对比效果。 做的过程中印象比较深的几个点： 1. **两种 API 格式兼容**：OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的流式返回格式差别不小，Claude Code 对格式挺挑的，调了很久才稳定。 2. **计费**：按 token 实时扣费，要处理流式中断、重试导致的重复计费，这块比想象中麻烦。 3. **登录**：最后只保留了 Google 和 Telegram 登录，省掉了邮箱验证那一套。 4. **充值**：目前只接了加密货币，最低 $1 ，余额不过期。国内支付方式还在想办法。 成本方面因为是批量采购上游额度，价格压得比较低，比如 GLM-5.3 输入输出都是 $0.20/M （官方 $1.40/$4.40 ），DeepSeek Flash $0.04/M ，自己日常写代码基本感觉不到成本了。 项目叫 Apixo：apixoai.online ，注册就有免费额度可以试网页聊天。 想听听大家的意见： - 你们写代码平时主要用哪个模型？还缺什么模型？ - 网页聊天还需要什么功能？ 欢迎拍砖 🙏

projects.title: Show HN: Dánwò – Open-source E2E testing with emulators and fault injection
projects.author: faithfulojebiyi
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Faithful. I built dánwò, an open-source (Apache-2.0) end-to-end testing framework for web and mobile apps, written in TypeScript. The problem: a UI test can click "Pay", see "Payment successful" and pass, while the card was charged twice, the webhook was handled twice, or the receipt email never went out. With coding agents writing more of our code, that gap between "the screen looks right" and "the right things happened" is where I kept finding bugs. How it works: - Tests drive the app like a user, with locators or plain-English agent steps. An agent step calls a model once; danwo records the actions and replays them on later runs with no model calls, so CI doesn't need an API key. - Your app runs behind an egress proxy. Calls to Stripe, Clerk, Resend, Slack, Google and about 20 other providers are answered by local emulators at the real hostnames, so there are no sandbox keys and no code changes. For Node apps a preload routes the calls; Bun honours HTTPS_PROXY. - An invariant is a check that runs after the test and compares two sides: what the provider says happened (charges, emails, messages) and what your app stored. For example, credits granted must equal paid checkouts times 500. - `danwo matrix` replays a test once per fault it could meet: a 500 or 429 from a provider, a declined card, a duplicate, late, forged or replayed webhook, a double-submit, a database commit whose reply is lost, Postgres unreachable for a few seconds. The invariant judges every run, so you see exactly which failure your app mishandles. - Every run leaves a flight record: video, each step, every provider call, webhook delivery and database statement, with secrets redacted. It runs in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, and on the Android emulator and iOS Simulator. It ships an MCP server and a skill, so coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) can write and run tests and fix what fails. Limitations, honestly: the emulators are only as good as their fidelity to the real APIs. Each one has a suite that runs against the real provider to catch drift, but they won't cover every edge of Stripe's API. Backend routing is built for Node and Bun today. Mobile tests need macOS or Linux. It's early (v0.1.2). The name is Yorùbá: "dán an wò" means "try it and see". Quickstart: npx @danwo/cli init (docs: https://danwo.dev/docs/quickstart ) I'd love feedback, especially on faults you've been bitten by that aren't in the matrix yet.
