projects.title: Show HN: distrust, a Go CLI tool for blocking unwanted CA certificates
projects.author: hyper_reality
projects.summary: After the recent eMudhra CA incident, I wondered why my system trusts over 150 root signing authorities, most of which I don't need? I decided to scratch my own itch and make a tool to block the long tail of unwanted CA certificates. distrust is a policy-based tool that aims to simplify the management of the mess of root stores: browsers (NSS, Chrome Root Store), OpenSSL/GnuTLS consumers (curl, wget, Python, Go), Java, and the standalone PEM bundles that apps ship (certifi, conda, botocore). It ships with an example policy that blocks all CAs except the top 30. I've tested and this seems fine for my normal browsing and usage. There did not appear to be existing tools to do this, probably because there is so much variance across operating system platforms, distros, and programming languages. distrust is therefore shamelessly vibe-coded to deal with all these edge cases. https://github.com/hyperreality/distrust

projects.title: Show HN: Corgi, a helpful {agent, terminal} multiplexer
projects.author: eiopa
projects.summary: Hey everyone, Inspired by Herdr, I've built an agent multiplexer that I've been using as my daily driver for a few weeks now. I think I improved on the concept in a few ways, focusing on the ergonomics I always wished I had: I show you what the agents are up to, along with a running feed of their activity. There's also a simple shortcut (F1) to go to the next unread agent. I use multiple accounts, so I've added unified launcher for Codex/Claude Code/Pi. Theres some careful ergonomics there: fast search and resume over sessions, inline usage tracking etc. Many small quality of life improvements to the terminal experience: - Links can be copied with a click, so no need to drag-select over many lines - cmd+v just pastes images (even on SSH) - images have a thumbnail preview. - Built-in CPU/Memory/GPU usage tracking, broken down by workspace I assume you have access to cheap inference (Luna/Haiku/etc). It just reuses the agents to organize things for you: what is this http link? what is this worktree about? what is each agent doing? It's small but it made my environment feel more cozy. On a personal note, I've been on a frustrating sick leave for a while now. I created Corgi to challenge myself, and see if I can go back. The answer is more mixed than I had hoped, but I am happy with the result and thankful for the experience. I hope you like it! a few friends & myself have been using it for a few weeks and it's been pretty nice. There's still a lot to improve and some rough edges, so feedback would be greatly appreciated. Thank you :)

github.description: Claude Code on your laptop and remote dev boxes, in one web page. Sessions keep running when SSH drops (no tmux), each session's changes get their own diff, plus tasks, notes, and memory. Self-hosted.

projects.summary: 开源协议：MIT 我平时在好几台远程开发机上跑 Claude Code。以前的办法是每台机器开一个 SSH 窗口，再套一层 tmux，窗口一多就分不清哪个会话在等我，笔记本一合盖、网络一断，还要一个个重新连回去。 Open Walnut 是我为这件事写的自托管网页。每台主机上有一个小 daemon，Claude Code 进程归它管，所以 SSH 断了或者笔记本睡眠，远程会话都在继续跑；重新连上后，历史从磁盘上的会话日志恢复。daemon 由 Walnut 通过免密 SSH 自动部署和升级，不用手动拷文件。 所有会话在一个网页里并排看。每个会话有自己的 diff，列出它改过的每个文件（从会话日志里算，不依赖 git），可以逐行评论，再把评论发回同一个会话。旁边还有任务、笔记和长期记忆，以及一个能帮你开会话、找上下文的个人 AI。 数据都在本机 ~/.open-walnut/，没有遥测，也不需要注册账号。 安装（macOS 或 Linux，脚本自带 Node；需要一个已登录的 Claude Code）： bash curl -fsSL | sh walnut web 也可以 brew install evanzhang008/tap/open-walnut 或 npm install -g open-walnut。

projects.summary: ML Studio 是一款开源、跨平台、本地优先的桌面端机器学习工作台（基于 Electron + FastAPI + Scikit-learn + Optuna 构建）。它面向全学科科研人员（理工农医、经管金融、实证社科）与工程师，将表格数据清洗、多模型比对、贝叶斯超参数寻优、动态学术诊断看板与实验报告导出收敛进同一个极简窗口。无需繁琐的 Python 环境配置，数据不出机器，拖入表格即可自动化完成全流程。 亮点 全学科通用与零门槛：拖入 CSV / Excel 文件，自动完成列类型识别、缺失值填充与异常探测；支持回归、分类、聚类与时间序列四大建模任务。 自适应超参寻优：基于 Optuna 自动化多目标超参数搜索（TPE / CMA-ES / Random / NSGA-II），配合 Hyperband 剪枝快速提前终止无效试验。 学术级可视化诊断：实时动态渲染残差分布图、学习曲线、混淆矩阵、ROC/PR 曲线、过拟合风险预警和特征相关性热力图。 一键导出科研报告：支持一键导出排版规范的 HTML / Markdown / Word / PDF 实验报告，图表和量化结论随报告一次性生成，直接用于学术汇报。 纯本地运行，数据不出机器：所有计算与缓存均保存在本机，无第三方云端依赖，保障未发表科研成果与涉密业务数据安全。 前瞻性 AI-Native 架构 (RFC-001)：借鉴 VS Code 架构设计了 mlstudio.config.json、全局命令总线与语义控件树快照，提供本地 MCP 协议接口，支持 AI 助手免截屏、高精度直接操控软件。

projects.title: 做了一个支持纠错的双拼输入法 Rectfly
projects.author: theHaagenDazs
projects.summary: 我非常喜欢 Gboard 的双拼纠错（它甚至可以盲打），但我总时不时担心它有一天会 discontinued 。我又不想用腾讯和豆包的输入法，因此我打算做一个堪比 Gboard 纠错的双拼输入法。 我自己只用小鹤，因此我取名 Rectfly ，取自 Rectify + Flypy 。但在人类学和开放爱(Anthropic / OpenAI)的建议下，我还支持了自然码，智能 ABC ，和拼音加加。本输入法不支持全拼输入。 它有一些功能，比如整句纠错，中英混输，导入 Rime 词库，和英文输入。整句纠错要感谢万象语法模型，Rectfly 的一些词库也来自万象。什么是万象语法模型： https://github.com/amzxyz/rime-wanxiang Gboard 的英文纠错和词库做得非常好，我目前找不到一款中文输入法的英文输入能与它媲美。因此我也在 Rectfly 上做了和 Gboard 相似的英文输入体验。 本输入法没有后端，也没有集成收集数据的 SDK 。无从也无意收集你的数据和隐私，所有的信息处理都在你的手机上完成。如果你愿意，欢迎加入「联邦评测」，并把结果发送给我（无论好坏），可能会提升打字准确率。什么是联邦学习： https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-federated-learning?hl=zh-CN 目前只有 TestFlight： https://testflight.apple.com/join/un67VMZe 欢迎大家体验。如需反馈，可以发邮件到 rectfly@fastmail.com 或者直接在本帖下回复。 使用须知： 需要 iOS 26 及以上版本。 需要开启「完全访问」以使用万象语法模型和按键震动。 首次开启会引导你下载万象语法模型，不下载语法模型也能打字，但整句首选准确率会从约 97%掉到约 57%。（由 30 句标准双拼整句测得） 隐私政策： https://ann61c.github.io/rectfly-site/privacy.html 致谢： https://ann61c.github.io/rectfly-site/attributions.html 参考的公开论文： https://aclanthology.org/2024.emnlp-industry.93/ https://research.google/pubs/spatial-model-personalization-in-gboard/ https://aclanthology.org/P14-1142/ https://aclanthology.org/P00-1031/ 一些截图： https://i.imgur.com/DfKej6R.png https://i.imgur.com/HCvHutR.png https://i.imgur.com/bKEf0ST.png https://i.imgur.com/WGDPV62.png

projects.summary: 大家好，「小扫帚」（英文名 Broomy ）是一个 Mac 清理小工具，今天发 1.0 。免费，没有广告，也从不联网。 能做的事： 1. **一页一个功能，两指左右滑动换页**：概览、清理垃圾、卸载、系统状态、硬盘健康、外设。打开就是概览页：找到多少垃圾、CPU 温度、硬盘健康、显示器亮度，一页看完。 2. **卸载**：选一个 App ，列出它的容器、缓存、设置、应用支持文件、窗口状态、网页数据和登录项，每样写着大小，跟 App 一起进废纸篓。按 App 的标识去认；只是名字一样的文件夹会列出来，但默认不勾。苹果自带的 App 不列，正在运行的要先退出，别的 App 共用的文件不动； App 本身要是移不走，别的也都不动。 3. **清理垃圾**：Xcode 、模拟器、Gradle 、Homebrew ，pip 、npm 、pnpm 、Yarn 、Bun 、CocoaPods 、Swift Package Manager 、Go 、Cargo 的缓存； 30 天没人改过的项目里的 node_modules 、.build 、target 、dist 和 Gradle 的 build （旁边得有 package.json 、Package.swift 、Cargo.toml 或 build.gradle 才算，git 跟踪的不动，默认不勾）； App 缓存和日志、“下载”和桌面上的安装包、已删除 App 留下的后台项目。 4. **外设**：显示器的亮度和音量，外接显示器也行；调不了的不藏着，直接写“不支持”、原因和可以试试什么（比如有些 HDMI 口、转接头、扩展坞不传显示器的控制信号）。还有鼠标滚轮反转和平滑滚动。 5. 九种语言。 ![概览]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/techinfo-apps/Broomy/main/screenshots/overview-zh-Hans.png) ![卸载]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/techinfo-apps/Broomy/main/screenshots/uninstall-zh-Hans.png) ![清理垃圾]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/techinfo-apps/Broomy/main/screenshots/main-zh-Hans.png) 一直坚持的几条： - 删的东西都先进废纸篓，清空之前都能放回去； - 外接硬盘一律不碰，也不显示序列号； - 没有任何联网的代码，什么都不收集。 下载： https://github.com/techinfo-apps/Broomy/releases/latest （ macOS 14 及以上，Apple 芯片和 Intel 都行） 介绍页： https://techinfo-apps.github.io/broomy/ 还没经过苹果公证，第一次打开 macOS 会拦一下：macOS 14 右键点它 → 打开； macOS 15 及以后到“系统设置 → 隐私与安全性”往下翻，点“仍要打开”。 欢迎提意见，每一条都会认真看。 —— Technology Information · 永远免费，永远没有广告。 sublueai@gmail.com · https://techinfo-apps.github.io/

projects.summary: Paper Translator v3 是一个将英文扫描版/原生文字版学术论文翻译并重新排成中文 PDF 的实验项目。目前主要使用量化金融、计量经济学论文验证，希望帮助仍在阅读老扫描论文的研究者。 特点 视觉模型读取原文、公式和阅读顺序，版面检测器与文字层只提供几何信息，再进行中文重排。 公式经 LaTeX 编译为矢量内容；图表保留原图，指定保留英文的区域不强制翻译。 检查翻译时数学变量是否丢失、是否有文字压图、空白页或未还原的占位符；有问题的数学翻译缓存可按段重译。 验证与适用边界 当前完成三篇共 56 页的重建验证和 11 项回归测试，另有本机 pdf2zh 1.9.11 的有限样本对照；这不代表全文语义准确，也不代表优于最新 pdf2zh/BabelDOC。 项目采用 MIT 许可证，代码开源。运行需要 Python、LaTeX、检测器权重和使用者自己的模型 API，API 费用由服务商收取。当前更适合愿意配置环境、希望检查与改进论文翻译流程的读者。 对照与已知限制： 欢迎试用，尤其希望收到扫描论文、公式或复杂版面的失败样本及安装反馈。感谢考虑收录。

projects.title: Show HN: Ocel – Deploy apps to your AWS,GCP or VPS with infra from code
projects.author: vndaba
projects.summary: Hey HN, I’m Victor and I’ve been building Ocel, an open source CLI, Console and SDK for deploying your apps and the infra they need to your own AWS/GCP/VPS. The CLI: Run ‘ocel deploy’ in your existing apps, and deploy to a configured target, no separate IaC files required. The SDK: Declare infra your app needs as code within the app itself, the CLI builds and provisions with no extra steps when deploying. Rust, Go, Python and Typescript supported. The Console: Optional self-hostable UI for an otherwise CLI-first product. The neat part is that the console itself is an app built with the sdk and deployed with the CLI ! You can try it out to deploy your apps to your own infra. VPS is well tested, and AWS+Cloudflare is also quite well covered. I’ve been dogfooding this myself for things I’m building. Please expect bugs, as it’s still early days. Why ? I’ve been a big fan and user of SST for a long time (personal and professional projects). The DX is genuinely unmatched and the high-level components make things quite easy. I think they proved that most apps don’t need complex IaC code, and abstracting things behind high level components/primitives, with some customization levers, actually works quite well. Ocel builds on that by taking it a bit further, no infra code, have a similar ‘high level components’ approach, but directly in the app. And support deploying existing apps or frameworks from day one in the CLI. You should be able to cd into an existing app and just deploy! (Of course theres a bit more like providing credentials to the platform you are deploying to, domains, one-time setup, etc). Everything else is the gripes I had after deploying tons of apps with SST: - Preview and production separation built in, so previews can share heavy resources and be considerably faster - First class support for separating the origin and edge, so composing AWS and cloudflare (common setup I had) becomes a breeze - CLI-first product, but with a UI console that can also be self hosted for things like team management, setting env vars, etc. - More SDK primitives (Realtime, Tasks, Pubsub topics, etc) that give a BaaS-like experience no matter where you deploy

projects.author: szj2ys
projects.summary: I am suggesting this resource on behalf of the Pic2SVG team. This submission was prepared with AI assistance; it is a self-recommendation, not an independent review. Resource: An .svg extension does not by itself establish that artwork is made from editable vector geometry. This practical guide explains how to inspect SVG source for paths and shapes, embedded raster images, text that depends on fonts, and external references. The checks help developers and designers review exported logos or artwork before handing the file to another application. The accompanying SVG structure checker is linked from the guide. Its findings describe document structure; they do not certify manufacturing safety, copyright ownership, or compatibility with every cutting machine. Pic2SVG also offers deterministic raster-to-SVG tracing. It does not generate artwork or use an AI model for tracing. I am proposing the inspection guide for its practical educational value. Please consider it only if it is useful to the weekly's readers; no reciprocal link or promotional placement is requested.

projects.summary: 大家好，我是 [BibGenie]( https://bibgenie.com) 的开发者，来分享一下自己做了一年多的东西，也想听听 V 站里还在用 Zotero 看文献的朋友的真实反馈。 ## 背景说明 用 Zotero 的应该都知道，它是科研圈最主流的开源文献管理工具，但本身没有任何 AI 能力。我自己读论文时有个很具体的痛点：把论文丢给 AI 问，答案说得头头是道，但我根本不知道它是从哪篇、哪一页得出的结论，最后还得自己回去翻 PDF 核对，费时费力。 所以我做了 BibGenie （去年叫 Zotero Copilot ，但因为 Zotero 商标的问题改了名），一个原生跑在 Zotero 里面的 AI 插件，侧边栏形态，可以直接访问官网 https://bibgenie.com 查看首页的展示视频，视频会更加直观。 迭代了一年多，目前更新到 v0.9.4 版本了，核心功能都已经开发完成了，今天来 V2EX 求一点反馈 （顺便吐槽一下，现在很多独立开发者只顾哐哐开发新产品，却不管维护，我也是深受其害。） ## 核心功能大概是这几块： 1. 直接和自己的 Zotero 整个文库对话。 不用导出文件、不用把 PDF 一个个上传到网页工具。在 Zotero 里面直接用 @ 或者右键 Add to Chat ，就能把条目、PDF 的某几页、EPUB 章节、批注、笔记、标签、整个集合拉进同一个对话里，多篇论文一起对比之类的。 2. **引用可追溯到文本块。** 这是我最在意、也花时间最多的功能。AI 回答里给出的引用，点一下能跳回 PDF 对应页，并高亮出它引用的那个文本块； EPUB 、网页快照也是一样定位到段落。科研场景下，我觉得这个功能真是刚需。 3. **本地优先，支持 BYOK**。聊天记录存在本地 Zotero 数据库里，不上传服务器；文库的语义索引也是在本地建的。模型这边三条路随便选：自带 Key （ OpenAI 、Claude 、DeepSeek 、OpenRouter 、各种兼容接口都支持，请求直连服务商，不消耗额度）；本地模型（ Ollama 、LM Studio ，聊天和 embedding 都配成本地的就可以完全不出本机）；或者用 bibgenie 官方模型开箱即用，什么都不用配置。 4. **内置了一个 Zotero MCP Server**。这个估计 V 站的朋友会比较感兴趣。插件里直接起了个本地 MCP Server （ Streamable HTTP ，长这样：127.0.0.1:23119/bibgenie/mcp ），不用再单独装什么 Python 服务。Claude Code 、Claude Desktop 、Cursor 、Cherry Studio 连上之后，可以直接检索我的 Zotero 文库、做语义搜索、读 PDF 附件（页面还能渲染成图片，看图表和扫描页没问题）、读笔记和快照，也能在客户端自己的权限确认下建笔记、整理集合。 5. 帮着整理 Zotero 文库。 可以让它整理集合、清洗标签、核查元数据（时间长了，zotero 文献库的标签，分类之类的都乱了，可以直接来整理）。元数据是交叉比对 arXiv 、Semantic Scholar 、OpenAlex 、DBLP 、OpenReview 这几个来源的。所有改动先出一张 diff 预览卡，点批准了才写进去。 ## 关于定价 所有的功能都是免费的，需要购买的只有模型的 token 。免费用户每月送 200 credits ，Pro 是 $9.99/月，有 10000 credits （ Pro 肯定够用了!!）。现在还有个 $199 的 Lifetime Pro ，v1.0 之后会下架（当然已经买了的不受任何影响，下架只针对新购），独立开发的小产品确实长期扛不住终身制, 前期已经倒贴了不少了。 官方模型目前是通过 OpenRouter 接入的，我在成本价上只加 7% 用来覆盖服务器和其他支出，目前没打算靠 token 差价赚钱（毕竟也支持自定义模型）。 官网和文档在这： 官网： https://www.bibgenie.com 文档： https://www.bibgenie.com/docs 最后想认真求一波反馈，尤其是平时用 Zotero 的朋友。批评也完全欢迎，这东西的不少功能就是被用户骂出来的。感谢阅读。 （很抱歉，没有福利带给大家，毕竟这个产品是免费的，相信 V 友都有能力接入自定义模来使用，如果确实有想订阅的，可以留下邮箱，我给你 8 折优惠券。 当然，有 llm 服务商愿意支援 token 网页是欢迎的。）

projects.title: Show HN: AI agent needs process to build a commercial application
projects.author: abalgir
projects.summary: I decided to test this claim with my app, NoMoreHappyPath (NMHP), against Claude on a real project. Here is the test: I built Acremuse, a commercial real estate analysis platform, with Claude Desktop and Codex as a reviewer. It is deployed and used today by a couple of investors. Then I wondered what I'd missed that might bite me later. ~ 374,000 Lines of program code - 1,070 Source files (Python and TypeScript) - ~ 11,400 Functions and methods - 3,067 Automated tests So I gave the same 374k-line code snapshot and the same brief to one Claude session that can use Codex as a reviewer and to my own tool, NMHP. My directive was the same for both: Analyze the code, find any errors/bugs, and list them by severity. Findings must be reviewed before writing the final report. The Results (Verified by an impartial, blind Codex judge): NMHP: 33 real issues found. 7 false claims. Claude: 10 real issues found. 2 false claims. Only 6 issues overlapped. Time & Cost: From the owner's go-ahead to the reviewer's pass, NoMoreHappyPath took about 74 minutes, including time lost while it found and worked around a defect in the product itself. The Python version NMHP was working on was 3.9, the OS version, and it didn't have pytest installed, which was needed to verify some claims. After 15 minutes of blockage, the CTO stepped in and told the agent to create a venv with Python 3.13, install the corresponding pytest, and move the project along. NMHP CTO reacts when 15 minutes pass without movement from agents. To be fair to Claude, Claude did create a venv from the get-go. Time & Cost: NMHP took 74 minutes and cost $24 in API spend. Claude finished in a few minutes for a fraction of that cost. And yes, NMHP takes over an hour and costs twenty-four bucks. But for a 374k-line codebase, finding 23 more real issues overall that vanilla Claude missed makes $24 a massive win compared to human audit rates. I know this isn't a benchmark; it's one app and one run each. I wrote a detailed white paper on it. But it confirmed my idea: an AI agent without a real process is not yet capable of building a commercially ready application, even with a frontier model and reviews that are initiated by the same agent.

projects.summary: Glint 是一款为中文母语者设计的 macOS 英文学习工具。你照常用拼音输入，候选栏旁就会直接出现对应的英文，不切换应用，也不改变输入法。它支持单词、短语和短句，还能把选中的英文译文直接插入当前输入位置；内置词典和本地模型，日常使用无需联网，也不会保存你的输入内容。 亮点 1. 边打中文边学英文：不需要打开词典或翻译网站，照常输入拼音，就能在候选旁看到对应的英文表达。 2. 从单词到短句都能用：单词给出简洁常用的英文对应词，短语和短句显示自然翻译，适合聊天、写邮件和日常表达。 3. 选中译文就能直接插入：按设定好的触发键加数字，把需要的英文译文插入当前输入位置，不用复制粘贴。 4. 离线也能用，输入内容不会外传：内置词典和本地翻译模型，也能按需安装更适合的本地模型；不保存候选或译文，不安装键盘事件监听。 5. 敏感场景自动避开：遇到密码框、终端安全输入等情况时停止显示翻译，只读取当前高亮候选，不读取输入框正文。 6. 原生 macOS 小工具：菜单栏常驻，提供 PKG/DMG 安装包；翻译数量可调，可以设置登录时启动，适配浅色和深色外观。 技术实现方面，Glint 使用 Swift 6、AppKit 和 SwiftUI 构建，内置 CTranslate2 翻译运行时，并支持可选 MLX 模型，也适合作为本地 AI macOS 应用的参考项目。 截图或演示视频 45 秒产品演示视频（Bilibili）

projects.title: Show HN: Cb2026, a Rust chess engine that revisits a 2004 world-record project
projects.author: cjus
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Carlos. In 2004 Colin Frayn and I ran ChessBrain, a distributed chess computer that played a game against GM Peter Heine Nielsen using machines volunteered from around the world. It set the Guinness World Record for the largest networked chess computer. Some ideas from that project stayed with me, so I created cb2026 (ChessBrain 2026) to explore them. cb2026 is a chess engine written from scratch in Rust. It speaks UCI and XBoard, so it runs in En Croissant, Cute Chess, XBoard and similar GUIs. It has Lazy SMP search, Syzygy tablebase probing, Polyglot opening books, Chess960, and an NNUE evaluation network trained on its own games. Strength: about 3379 ± 21 on the CCRL Blitz scale, from 5,600 games against seven rated engines. Its original hand-crafted evaluation rated 2782, and each NNUE generation improved on that. I wanted it to be easy to learn from as well as strong: - Every technique can be switched off. An interactive shell lets you play it, watch it think depth by depth, and toggle things like null-move pruning to see what each one does. - docs/elo-ledger.md records how much Elo each technique gained. - A companion book, "Building a Chess Engine in Rust", has a chapter for each stage, from board representation and move generation to NNUE. Each chapter covers the idea, the real code and what it measured. It's free online, as a PDF or as an EPUB: https://cjus.github.io/chessengine/ It also has strength levels that blunder about as often as Lichess players of a given rating do. License is MIT or Apache-2.0. The one exception: release binaries include Syzygy probing through a GPL-3.0 crate, which makes those binaries GPL. Build with --no-default-features to get a binary with no GPL code. Happy to answer questions about the engine, the book, or ChessBrain.

projects.summary: 最近做了一款 macOS 原生中文输入法 Monkey ，刚发布 0.2.1 开发预览，想找愿意尝鲜的朋友一起打磨日常输入。名字也是一个“盲 key”的谐音，希望少打断写作，多把注意力留在内容上。 它用 Swift / InputMethodKit 做系统输入法，底层是 librime 和雾凇拼音。普通拼音、候选排序及用户词学习在本机完成，无需登录。支持全拼、简拼、常见错拼纠正和中英词候选，网址、邮箱、小数与版本号会尽量保留 ASCII 符号。 另外想做的是：**用中文组织表达，在当前输入框里预览英文，确认后再上屏**，减少在翻译工具和聊天窗口之间复制粘贴。 - `Control + Shift + T`：开启中译英，也可直接点候选条上的按钮。 - 正常拼音选词组成中文草稿，等待英文预览。 - `Control + Return`：确认英文；翻译模式下直接 `Return`：提交中文。 - 候选窗只在输入或有待确认草稿时出现，提交后收起。 翻译使用官方 Sign in with ChatGPT ，符合条件的订阅账号可授权使用额度，无需填写 API key 。模型、资格与额度由账号和服务决定，不是无限调用，也不会带入 ChatGPT 聊天记录。只有主动开启翻译后，当前草稿和表达偏好才会发送给 OpenAI ，凭据保存在 macOS Keychain 。 0.2.1 主要打磨了候选条上的翻译、设置入口和回车行为，也换了青柠色键帽图标、重做了设置引导。翻译等待做了优化，但网络与模型耗时仍有波动，暂不承诺固定速度。 目前提供 **Apple Silicon / macOS 13+** 安装包，使用 ad-hoc 签名，**尚未经过 Apple 公证**，仍是开发预览。解压后运行 `Install.command`，安装到当前用户的输入法目录，不需要管理员密码，再手动选中 Monkey ；部分情况下需要注销重新登录。仓库提供源码构建和卸载说明。 中文上下文同音排序、无分隔中英长串和跨应用兼容仍需继续打磨。当前混输建议先确认中文候选，再接英文或数字。原创代码是 MIT ； librime 、词库及其他依赖保留各自许可证，雾凇数据含 GPL-3.0 ，来源与声明随仓库提供。 源码与说明： https://github.com/jiaqianjing/monkey 下载： https://github.com/jiaqianjing/monkey/releases/tag/v0.2.1 最想收集具体的输入问题：按键顺序、实际候选、期望结果，以及 macOS 版本和宿主应用。欢迎用可公开的例子提 issue / PR ，一起把选词、退格、回车这些日常细节做好。

projects.title: 【工具自荐】沉浸式AI提问：划词提问，读AI长对话再也不用上下来回翻
projects.author: zhengzhoujiao
projects.summary: 沉浸式AI提问 是一款面向 Chrome / Edge 的网页阅读助手。使用者可以通过划词的方式获取AI解释并添加注释，不再需要来回翻阅上下文，顺着思路阅读，获得沉浸式阅读体验。 减少 AI 长回答中的阅读中断 在使用 AI 获取知识、分析问题或学习新概念时，读者可能尚未读完整段回答，就对其中某句话产生疑问。常见的处理方式是暂停阅读，在对话输入框中引用相关内容并重新提问；获得补充解释后，再向上滚动，定位原回答及此前的阅读位置。 当回答较长、概念较多时，这一过程会频繁重复。补充解释中的新疑问还可能引出更多轮对话，使原始内容与后续讨论逐渐分散，增加来回定位和衔接思路的负担。 针对局部内容的疑问，适合在对应的原文旁展开讨论。 沉浸式AI提问将解释入口放在选中文字附近，使读者可以围绕当前词句提问、查看回答并继续追问，减少往返对话输入区与原文位置的操作。 这一方式同样适用于普通网页阅读：查阅资料时，可以直接在原文旁获取解释，减少复制内容、切换窗口和重新交代背景的步骤。 结合上下文解释，围绕选中内容持续讨论 在网页正文中选中词语或句子后，将鼠标悬停于小蓝点，即可打开解释浮窗。插件会结合选中文字及必要上下文生成回答，使解释与当前阅读内容保持关联。 演示流程：选择词句 → 悬停蓝点 → 查看解释 → 连续追问 → 原文保留标注。 首次解释后，读者可以在同一浮窗内进一步讨论概念含义、具体示例、推导依据或实现方法。例如，阅读支付 API 相关内容时，可以先了解“幂等性”的含义，再追问其实现方式；阅读 AI 回答时，也可以针对某一步推导要求补充说明。 解释与追问围绕当前选中内容展开，原文仍保留在阅读位置。完成讨论后，移开鼠标即可继续阅读后续内容。 将解释与讨论保存为原文注释 即时解释解决当前的理解问题，注释则便于后续复习与查阅。 沉浸式AI提问会在浏览器本地保存解释与相关对话，并在对应原文旁留下标注。读者可以将对术语、句子和段落的讨论保留为注释，通过悬停小标再次查看，无需重新生成已有回答。 演示流程：查看已有注释 → 模拟刷新 → 恢复标注 → 再次回看已保存内容。 刷新或重新访问网页时，插件会依据保存的原文及附近文本尝试恢复标注，使之前的解释能够重新关联到相应内容。网页内容发生较大变化、原文被删除或扩展数据被清除时，可能影响恢复。 适用场景 | 阅读场景 | 使用方式 | | --- | --- | | AI 长篇回答 | 针对特定表述、概念或推导步骤就地提问，减少重新提问后返回原文定位的往返 | | 技术文档 | 结合当前语境理解专业术语，并继续讨论实现方法与示例 | | 外文资料 | 选择难以理解的词句，获取结合上下文的解释 | | 新领域学习 | 在阅读过程中逐项澄清陌生概念，保留相关讨论供后续查阅 | | 原文注释 | 通过提问与讨论形成注释，将解释保存在对应词句旁，便于随时回看 |

projects.author: irrwood
projects.summary: 我的美股散落在好几个券商里, 一直找不到一个地方能看清楚: 总共持有什么, 今年到底赚了多少, 跑没跑赢大盘啊。券商 App 只看得到自己那一家, 记账软件要手动录每一笔交易。所以干脆自己写了一个。 - 支持各种券商 api 连接，不用手动输入（当然也支持自己手动导入 csv ）。 - 买入点卖出点都非常清晰显示在线上，还有金额细节，成本价都算的清清楚楚的。 - 账户数据都是自动算，合并算分开算，非常直观。 - 真实收益: 同时算时间加权 (TWR) 和资金加权 (MWR) 收益,可以和 SPY 、QQQ 等基准对比,不会被定投入金带偏。 - 收益来源: 按标的拆分收益,看清今年的钱是哪几只赚的。 - ETF 穿透: 把所有账户里的 ETF 拆开,算出合并后对单只股票的真实敞口。比如 QQQ 、VGT 、VOO 叠在一起,你实际持有多少 NVDA 。 - 分红:已到账的分红和今年的预期分红。 - 研究工具: 成交量分布、期权持仓墙 (OI walls)、市场情绪仪表盘,还能看佩洛西、段永平、巴菲特等知名投资者公开披露的持仓。 - AI: 内置 AI 助手,用你自己的 AI;还提供 MCP server,可以在 Claude Code 或 Codex 里直接问问题。 - 支持 A 股！可以搜索添加 几个设计原则: - 只读,不能下单。 - 计算都在手机本地完成。 - 不包含任何投资建议哈。 **App Store**: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6810656291 **官网**: https://catfolio.app 我已经修了好久，bug 已经不多了，但是一个人 vibe 开发,肯定有不少问题,欢迎拍砖。特别想知道大家还在用哪些券商是连不上的。 ![Catfolio on Mac, iPad and iPhone]( https://catfolio.app/assets/catfolio-devices.webp) ![Catfolio]( https://catfolio.app/assets/catfolio-hero.webp)

projects.author: beilunyang

github.name: beilunyang/openhongguo
github.description: 红果短剧的非官方匿名 SDK，提供 Go、Node.js、Android、iOS、React Native 和 Flutter 版本，附命令行演示程序 ohg CLI

projects.summary: openhongguo 是红果短剧的非官方 SDK，Apache-2.0 许可证。它用一台匿名设备发请求，不需要登录，可以浏览书城频道、搜索短剧、读取短剧和分集详情、查看排行榜和演员主页，并取得分集的播放地址。 红果 App 的数据接口它基本都包了，所以可以拿它开发一个自定义的红果客户端，界面和交互都由你决定： 用 Flutter 或 React Native 写一个移动端 App，按自己的喜好重新设计首页、搜索和播放页 用 Swift 做 macOS 原生客户端，或者用 Node.js / Go 做网页版、电视端、命令行版 只取自己需要的功能：比如只看追更的几部剧、按演员订阅新作、做一个榜单聚合页 仓库自带的命令行程序 ohg 就是一个这样的例子：在终端里搜剧、选集，然后用 mpv 播放。 主要特点： 一套 Go 实现，编译出六个平台的包：Go、Node.js（npm）、Android（Maven Central）、iOS / macOS（Swift Package）、React Native、Flutter（pub.dev）。各语言的方法一一对应，行为相同。 第一次请求时自动注册匿名设备，设备档案可以存文件、存内存，或自己实现存储。 错误都有统一的错误码和“是否可重试”标记，限流、网络失败和 5xx 自动重试。 分页接口附带 Pager，自动去掉服务端跨页返回的重复短剧。 服务端接口没有公开文档，仓库每天跑一次接口契约检查，尽早发现改版。 Go 版快速上手： go client, := adapters.NewClient("anonymous.json", sdk.Options{}) page, := client.Search(ctx, "全球死考", sdk.SearchOptions{}) episodes, := client.ListEpisodes(ctx, page.Items[0].ID, sdk.EpisodeOptions{}) pb, := client.ResolvePlayback(ctx, episodes.Items[0].ID, sdk.PlaybackOptions{}) Node.js 版：npm install openhongguo，然后 const client = await createClient(); await client.search('全球死考'); 本项目仅供学习移动应用接口协议的分析与调用，禁止商业使用和大规模采集，短剧内容的版权归原权利人所有。

projects.title: 因为受够了手动更新 IIS 证书，我花了半年时间做了一个自动托管平台，想听听大家的意见
projects.author: netlichun
projects.summary: 作为一个独立开发者，我平时会做一些小项目，其中主要是 Web 项目，也有时候会接点小活，帮客户做一些小网站。这些网站基本上都是使用阿里云或腾讯云的云服务器进行部署，因为现在的浏览器对于 SSL 证书的要求越来越严格，所以基本每个站点都要部署 SSL 证书，这在前几年也不是个事，因为阿里云和腾讯云都提供免费的一年期证书，每隔一年部署一次，也还能承受。 但是最近几年越来越吃力，阿里云和腾讯云的免费证书，都开始减少有效期，一开始从一年减到 6 个月，还勉强凑合用，后来减到 3 个月，就感觉有点顾不过来了，因为虽然免费，但每个证书都要申请、下载、导入到证书管理、绑定到 IIS……站点多了，操作还是挺繁琐的。三个月就到期，经常会忘记更新证书，导致网站打开就是大大的风险提示，有时候还是客户发现了告诉我，我才知道。 虽然这两家都还提供一年期的证书，但是那价格，我确实有点难以承受。 后来我就开始研究证书这个事，才发现其实可以从第三方申请免费的证书，比如 Let's Encrypt ，我也了解到 win-acme 这类成熟的开源工具，它本身就能够实现 IIS 证书自动申请和续期。不过我个人更习惯图形化管理，而且有时候需要维护多台服务器上的多个网站，希望能通过一个 Web 工作台统一查看证书状态、集中管理部署目标，而不是分别登录每台服务器进行配置和维护。所以现有工具虽然不错，但还是没能完全满足我自己的使用习惯。 国内也找到了一些提供证书自动化服务的平台，不过我试用之后感觉，大部分还是更偏向 Linux 、Nginx 等环境，或者需要通过脚本进行部署，与我平时使用 Windows Server + IIS 的习惯不太一致。 就有了自己开发一个工具的想法，并且我研究了一下发现，这个技术条件还很现成，Let's Encrypt 提供了一个叫做 ACME 的协议，可以通过编程的方式自动申请证书，这不就正好可以发挥咱程序员的特长嘛，于是开始着手鼓捣这个东西。做的过程中，我又觉得这个东西可以搞成一个平台，比搞个单机版工具更有价值，因为单机版工具，还是需要远程到服务器上维护，搞一个平台，可以在浏览器上操作，并且把多台服务器集中到统一界面来管理。不但可以解决我的问题，我还可以把这个做成一个 Saas ，帮别人解决问题，同时自己也能有点小收益。 经过了小半年的产品设计以及开发，各种反复尝试与推倒重来，我终于把这个产品做出来了，这就是现在我要隆重推介给大家的：SSLThink - IIS 网站证书托管与自动化部署平台，鼓掌！！！ 网址： https://www.sslthink.com 平台的主要功能，就是帮你申请 Let's Encrypt 证书，以及把证书部署到 IIS 网站。当然，平台干了这个活，也适当收点辛苦费。目前是公测期，每张证书的价格是 10 元/年，当然说「每张证书」不够严谨，这个价格其实是一年的证书订阅费用，在订阅期内，证书会自动更新。目前 Let's Encrypt 的证书有效期是 90 天，而且未来还会进一步缩短到 64 天、45 天。也就是说，证书更新会越来越频繁。不过对于 SSLThink 用户来说，这些更新由平台按照证书实际有效期自动处理，不需要手动重新申请和部署。 有同学就问了，Let's Encrypt 证书不是免费的嘛，你怎么还收费呢？其实收费的不是证书本身，而是 SSLThink 围绕证书搭建了一整套自动签发、自动更新、自动部署的全流程体系，如果你的网站用的是 IIS ，那么购买了这一年的证书订阅服务，进行初始的配置之后，往后你就不用操心证书这回事了，然后一年到期之后你再续订，那就继续不用操心，也不用重新配置。 具体怎么实现的呢？证书的签发与更新，是在 SSLThink 的服务端进行的，这个自然不在话下。在域名验证方面，SSLThink 采用的是 ACME 协议中的 DNS-01 验证方式。我把这部分也自动化了，用户只需要按照平台提供的记录，初始配置一次 CNAME 委托，之后证书签发和更新所需的 DNS 验证就由 SSLThink 自动处理，不需要每次更新时再去修改 DNS 记录。 关键是证书的部署，我开发了一个「托管节点程序」，把这个托管节点程序安装到 Windows 服务器，它会自动同步你的 IIS 站点和 https 绑定信息到 Web 工作台，然后在工作台对相应站点的 https 绑定与你购买的证书进行关联绑定，这个托管节点程序就会自动帮你把证书部署好，并且之后服务端的证书更新了，它也会自动更新 IIS 上对应的证书。 考虑到很多使用 IIS 部署网站的同学，除了网站，还有可能会使用一些云服务产品，比如 CDN 、阿里云的 OSS 等，这些云产品往往也有部署证书的需求，既然网站的证书都自动化了，没道理还要手动再搞这些云产品的部署，好在阿里云和腾讯云都提供了给云产品部署证书的接口，所以 SSLThink 的证书还可以自动部署到阿里云和腾讯云的一些云产品上，当然这个还是需要一些初始配置以及授权，具体的操作我都整理了详细的帮助文档，根据文档一步一步来就行，并不复杂。并且，如果你没有使用 IIS ，只是需要用 SSLThink 进行阿里云和腾讯云的云产品自动部署，那就无需安装 Windows 托管节点程序。 如果对于同时管理多台服务器，以及多个网站的同学，SSLThink 的价值体现就更大了，因为可以直接从 Web 工作台，就可以全局随时查看证书的更新和部署情况，如果哪个证书有问题，平台还会及时发送消息提醒。 当然，目前这个平台的自动部署功能主要围绕 Windows Server + IIS 环境设计，暂时不支持 Linux 、Nginx 或宝塔面板等环境的自动部署。不过通过平台签发的证书仍然可以下载，手动部署到其他支持的服务器环境。 另外提前说明一下：SSLThink 的托管节点是需要安装在 Windows Server 上的程序，目前安装包已经使用 Certum 企业代码签名证书完成数字签名，并且带有可信时间戳，签名发布者为济南善思信息科技有限公司。由于软件刚刚发布、下载量较少，如果使用微软的 Edge 浏览器下载，可能仍会遇到 SmartScreen 信誉提示。官网下载页面提供了 SHA-256 校验值，大家可以自行核对安装包的来源和数字签名。 由于程序需要操作 IIS 证书和 HTTPS Binding ，我知道大家可能会对安装第三方程序有顾虑。如果有关于权限、安全边界或运行机制的问题，也欢迎直接提出，我会尽量解释清楚。 最后也想听听各位同学们的真实意见：现在还有多少人在用 Windows Server + IIS 部署网站？大家平时是怎么解决 SSL 证书自动续期和部署问题的？ 我知道 win-acme 等免费工具已经可以很好地解决不少场景，所以也挺想了解，对于需要管理多台服务器、多个网站的用户，像 SSLThink 这种集中托管的平台到底有没有价值。 这是我第一次认真把一个自用工具做成 SaaS ，目前才刚上线，还没有经过多少真实用户的检验。欢迎大家拍砖，尤其是对功能、安全性和收费模式有什么建议，我都很愿意听听。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】UniPublisher MCP：本地优先的多平台内容分发桌面工作站，支持 Claude / Cursor 一键同步 17+ 平台
projects.author: santiago0071

github.name: santiago0071/unipublisher-mcp
github.description: Documentation and setup guide for the MCP interface built into the UniPublisher desktop application (1.6.8+). Not a standalone server.

projects.summary: 阮老师和各位读者好，向周刊自荐我们开源的 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 服务端适配器与桌面发布工具 UniPublisher。 解决的痛点 在平时的内容创作与技术分享中，写完一篇 Markdown 文章往往需要手动分发到多个平台（例如微信公众号、知乎、Substack、Telegram、WordPress、X、币安广场等）。每个平台的富文本排版、代码高亮、图片上传机制各不相同，逐一复制粘贴经常需要消耗 1~2 小时，极易打断创作者的写作心流。 主要特点与设计考量 1. 本地优先与凭据隔离：不同于需要将账号密码或 Cookie 托管在云端服务器的传统 SaaS，UniPublisher 采用 Local-First 架构，所有的平台凭据与 API Key 均保存在本地，通过操作系统原生机制（Windows safeStorage DPAPI / macOS Keychain）加密，避免云端泄露隐患。 2. AI 与桌面协同（MCP 协议标准）：仓库开源了基于标准 stdio 的 MCP 服务端（unipublisher-mcp）。在 Claude Desktop、Cursor 或 Windsurf 中生成技术文章或研报后，可直接通过 MCP 工具调起桌面端。 3. 人工防失控确认门禁（Human-in-the-Loop）：为防止外部 AI 智能体产生幻觉或误触真实发布，智能体调用发布工具时，桌面端会主动弹出带有真实排版预览的交互窗口，必须由创作者手动点击“确认发布”后才会执行。 4. 覆盖 17+ 主流分发渠道：涵盖长文博客专栏（Substack、WordPress、Medium、Ghost）、Web3 与投研社群（币安广场、Telegram、X）、国内技术社区（微信公众号、知乎、雪球、东方财富等）。 系统支持与获取方式 客户端支持 Windows 10/11（提供微软商店认证版本与独立 .exe）及 macOS（Apple Silicon 原生 .dmg），新安装包含 50 次免费分发额度。 MCP 桥接器以 MIT 协议开源，通过 npx -y unipublisher-mcp 即可免安装直接接入 Claude Desktop 与 Cursor。

projects.title: Show HN: Google translate replacement for language learners
projects.author: musabilhan
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Musab and I'm building Manalect. Find TL;DR at the end. Most language apps fall short for me in two ways: 1. They’re not personalized enough. I get taught things I don’t care about, things that are too hard for me, and things I already know. 2. They don’t teach that well. I keep seeing question types where my brain does almost no work to figure out the answer, therefore learn nothing. I think the biggest reason they're not personalized enough is that they don't have a detailed enough representation of a language. Most apps have efficient review scheduling for the words you learn. But if you make the mistake of using "play" instead of "played" they're not able to identify that as a component that should have its own schedule for review. And if you don't track that, it essentially depends on luck whether a person reviews that information before forgetting it again. Essentially language isn't just made up of words, but also different forms, conjugations, phrases, grammar, and a lot more components. But mapping out the basic units in full detail isn't enough. It's also very important to know how those basic units relate to each other. Because of course some units share a lot in common, and their relationships form another unit that needs to be tracked. Take Spanish: “el gato negro” (the black cat) but “la casa negra” (the black house). “negro” becomes “negra” because “casa” is a feminine word. That rule isn’t part of any one word. It links the noun, its article and the adjective, and it shows up in almost every sentence. So it needs its own review schedule too. And it relies on a person knowing those things that make it up to be able to build that block. That was briefly about how I'm working on solving the first failure mode. Second is simpler but also very interesting. We know that for you to learn something, you need to experience difficulty. This is called desirable difficulty. For this reason, some question types, like multiple choice, are known to be inefficient. But that's not fully true. The reason multiple-choice questions can be inefficient is that usually the alternative options are so much more different from the correct one that it is very easy to guess which one is the right one. However, if you make a simple change where you make it so the alternatives are a lot closer to the correct answer, the person has to put more effort into recalling the correct option. In research, this is known as competitive distractors. And of course, desirable difficulty is not the same for everyone. This is quite simple to imagine. Even games allow you to change the difficulty, and the difficulty that is most efficient for learning doesn't necessarily have to be the difficulty a person can sustain for the long term. So it's also very personal. I had written a lot more about how it works in detail, but due to the allowed length for this post, I'll get to how specifically the app works on an application level. Please let me know if you have any questions. I'm very passionate about this, and I would love to talk more. How it works: 1. Translate sentences, define words, chat with AI, or import an article or a song 2. The content gets broken into granular components, not just words but grammar and more complex building blocks) and saved for you 3. You study them as short tests in real sentences 4. Stuff you already know gets skipped, and new stuff builds on what you know You can try it at manalect.com, no sign-up needed. Swedish, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Polish or English. It's free with a daily limit. It's at an early stage, and there might be bugs, but I'd love to hear from you about them so that I can fix them right away. I'd also love to hear your thoughts, and how you learn languages in general. I'll be around all day to answer questions.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Gear：打造 RSI 领域的 scikit-learn
projects.author: YehuiTang0316
projects.summary: 读了一堆 RSI（递归自我改进）论文，感觉绕来绕去，还是 RL 和进化搜索里的几个老问题： 1. Sampling：怎么高效地找到值得尝试的改动？ 2. 评测：怎么判断新 variant 真的变好了？ 3. 多样性：怎么避免过早收敛，越进化路越窄？ 这些方法不全是 RL，但换成“自进化”的名字，也没让这些问题消失。 所以我们做了 Gear。框架采用受 Meta-learning 启发的双层结构：内层 Agent 执行任务、产生轨迹；外层 Meta Agent 根据轨迹和评测反馈，改进提示词、工具、工作流和上下文管理。 我们将搜索决策与执行、评测流程分离，想做 RSI 领域的 scikit-learn，让 GEPA、RRSI、Harness² 这类算法更容易实现和比较。目前已经实现了一个包含共享失败诊断和分阶段评测的 GEPA 变体。 固定使用 GPT 5.6 Luna、medium 推理档位，任务通过率如下： | 任务集 | 原始 DSH | Gear 优化后的 DSH | | --- | ---: | ---: | | AutomationBench Marketing | 27.0% | 40.0% | | AutomationBench Support | 17.0% | 25.0% | | Terminal-Bench 2.1 | 52.8% | 62.9% | 在 Marketing 的 max 档评测中，Luna + 优化后的 DSH 达到 88.88% 的目标完成率，高于 Astra + Codex 的 84.08%。不过，严格任务通过率是 53% 对 57%，优势体现在部分目标完成度上。 另外，两种模型同用优化后的 DSH、同为 max 档时，Luna 单任务 API 等价费用估算为 0.0568 美元，Astra 为 1.1858 美元，低约 95%，不含优化和基础设施开销。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】paper-bro 论文看不懂？一键变成能玩的互动课🧪
projects.author: aeroxy

github.name: aeroxy/paper-bro
github.description: Paste an arXiv paper and get an interactive course.

projects.summary: 谁懂啊😭 每次打开 arXiv 论文，第一页还没读完就想放弃…… 论文是新想法最早出现的地方，可它是写给专家看的，普通人真的很难啃。 之前我在自己做的平台 AERO 上做了两门互动课（Quant Academy 和 Neuron Academy），没想到挺多人喜欢💡 于是我干脆组了一支 AI agent 小分队，专门把论文变成互动课👇 ✨ paper-bro 是什么 贴一个 arXiv 链接，它就给这篇论文做一门互动课： 📖 6～10 节短课，写给好奇的小白，会初中数学就能跟上 🧪 每节课都有一个能上手玩的小实验：拖滑块、按按钮，看着概念自己动起来 ✅ 最后有小测验，还有术语小词典，专业名词不再劝退 🔍 不是生成完就算了 上线前，每个实验都会在真实浏览器里实测一遍：每个滑块都拖，每个按钮都按 还有一个独立的“审稿 agent”拿原论文逐节核对 有问题就修，修不好的实验直接拿掉，绝不凑数上线 🙌 一篇论文只有一门课 第一个提交的人触发生成，几分钟就好，之后所有人直接看成品 免费！不用注册！不用登录！ 💡 隐藏小技巧 在任何 arXiv 论文页面，把地址栏里的 arxiv.org 换成 aero.oops.wtf/paper-bro，直接跳到这篇论文的课 📌 第一门课：《Attention Is All You Need》 就是 2017 年提出 Transformer 的那篇，今天的大模型基本都基于它 想学哪篇论文，打开 aero.oops.wtf/paper-bro 贴链接就行 （目前课程是英文的，但用词很简单，比直接啃论文友好太多） 视频里是 3 分钟完整演示🎬 代码在 GitHub，Rust 写的：aeroxy/paper-bro 建议先收藏⭐ 下次读论文用得上

LLM integration via MCP and API calls to ask questions on a topic, browse via agents and see their trail. 5. It’s completely free because I don’t know how to monetize it yet. projects.summary: 大家好，分享一个最近做的文档识别网站：MiniCPM OCR 。 地址： https://minicpmocr.com/ 想解决的事情很具体：拿到一份扫描版 PDF 、论文截图或带表格的图片后，能把里面的内容提取出来，少一些手动抄写和重新排版。 目前支持： - 上传图片或 PDF ，识别中英文文字、段落和页面布局。 - 提取表格结构，将数学公式转成 LaTeX 。 - 原文和识别结果对照查看，点击原文区域或结果块可以互相定位，也能直接修改识别出的文字。 - 导出可编辑的 Word 、Markdown ，或带区域坐标的 JSON ，方便继续整理文档、做笔记或接入后续流程。 我比较在意的是识别后的校对和使用体验：得到结果后，可以对照原图改一改，再带到自己的工作流里。复杂表格、模糊扫描件和公式仍然建议人工检查，不保证每份文档都能完整还原。 底层基于 OpenBMB 的 MiniCPM-OCR-1.0 ；这个网站是我们做的独立服务，并非 ModelBest 官方网站。 欢迎大家试试，也想听听大家平时最难处理的是哪类文档，以及对结果编辑、导出格式有什么建议。

projects.title: Show HN: MealWords – Show waiters what you can't eat, in their language
projects.author: LewisOrton
projects.summary: Last month I went to Indonesia, and was eating at a local place with friends who did not eat raw fish&green onions. We tried ChatGPT (of course) it worked, except it wasnt a smooth experience: taking too long, and difficult for the staff to provide proper feedback quickly. Then I realized I only needed to tell the waiter what we won't eat, and ask for recommendations, that's all. So I made MealWords (recommend to try on your phone): 1. You pick allergies, dietary and preferences in your language (peanuts, no cilantro, not spicy etc) and it shows the card in the staff's language. 2. The waiter taps anything they can't do on the card, or just confirms. You read the answer in your own language. On translations: nothing is machine-translated (well, llm-assisted for research but not mechanical translations). For allergens&terms I used all official guidance I could find (FDA, EFSA, Japan etc all official governments and local public health orgs) to make sure I used not only accurate but also understandable terms. Then I worked with native speakers (aka my friends all over the world) to proofread it as plain kitchen language, NOT medical wording (if you speak one of the languages and something feels odd, I'd really like to know!) Also, wordings were carefully chosen to meet local culture (for example if the target language is Chinese, there are extra explanations about peanut allergy when chosen, and what local sauces should be avoided in Chinese, where the general are not familiar with the concept enough compared to other places like Japan) Technical bits: the website is static, no account, card and choices stay in the browser (page analytics etc are described on the privacy page as they are but no privacy is collected)

projects.summary: Hi HN. Greg here. I've been a full stack engineer for 20 years. Now all I do is shuffle messages between users, my agent fleet, our dev pipeline.. back and forth. I miss coding, solving problems, reasoning, and having an understanding and a mental model of all the work I'm juggling. But this is the job now, and there's no going back. I don't exactly feel like a 10x engineer yet, but I am for sure a 10-tab engineer. I built (er, Claude built) Shufler to lean into my new reality. If the job is basically to shuffle things through a pipeline, why not have it be more fun. Each row on the 3D gameboard is one of your existing terminal sessions. The columns are the steps your work moves through: Brainstorm, Plan, Build, QA, Review, Merge, Deploy. Your shipped PRs get stored in a warehouse/depot. The main things flowing across the board are your issues and PRs: each one rides along its session/row as it moves through review, CI and merge, and anything waiting on you turns red. I tend to manage several PRs within each Claude/Codex session, and this makes it easier for me to hold onto a mental model of where everything is. It's also made daily standups much easier to read-out. I created a few skins/themes like a casino, a theme park, sky islands, a starship and a factory, because.. of course. MacOS, works with Claude Code and Codex CLI, and cmux and iTerm (tmux should work, but I haven't tested it). It doesn't try to replace anything you already use.. just makes the orchestration more fun. You can still shift focus over to your terminal sessions when needed, use your existing skills, MCP servers, etc. There's a 3D library-building in each skin where you can specify your markdown/context folders or files, and then drag and drop to check them out by your rows/sessions. I tried to be thoughtful on security, following patterns that I consider at work. No telemetry, and the only outside calls are your own gh calls to GitHub. Daemon only listens on localhost, and every action shows its command before it runs. MCP server is opt-in, and sending to other sessions is off by default; if you turn it on, every send is a preview plus a separate confirm you approve. Details are in the README's #safety-and-privacy, and the MCP threat model (including what it doesn't protect against) is in docs/MCP.md. To report a security issue privately (or contributions to improve), see SECURITY.md. Demo with mock data, nothing to install at https://shufler.app Repo at https://github.com/jgrichardson/shufler (MIT)

projects.title: 用 Web Components 做了个全栈框架 Gemkit，首屏 JS 26KB， SSR 性能和 SvelteKit 差不多
projects.author: 594mantou
projects.summary: 几年前在这发过我写的 Web Components 库 Gem （ https://v2ex.com/t/738230 ），一直有个硬伤：只有客户端渲染。连它自带的文档站生成器 gem-book 也是 CSR ，搜索引擎基本收录不到啥东西。 之前在这问过 React SSR 和自定义元素怎么配合（ https://v2ex.com/t/998353 ），当时我自己回复说「用 jsdom 模拟生成 ShadowDOM 理论上也行」。后来真这么干了： 1. 先用 jsdom 做原型，跑通了序列化（输出 Declarative Shadow DOM ）和水合（复用服务端的 DOM ，不重建） 2. 再把 jsdom 去掉，直接渲染成字符串，用 AsyncLocalStorage 做请求隔离，支持流式输出，这就是 gem-ssr 3. 最近参考 Next.js 和 SvelteKit ，在 gem-ssr 上做了应用框架 Gemkit ## 长啥样 一个文件就是一个页面： ```ts // src/pages/blog/[slug].ts @page ({ load: ({ params }) => getPost(params.slug), title: ({ data }) => data.title, }) export default class PostPage extends GemElement { @property data?: Post; @template() #content = () => html` ${this.data?.title} `; } ``` 只在服务端跑的代码放同名的 `[slug].server.ts` ，可以读 cookie 、redirect 、处理表单 actions ，不会打包到客户端。用过 SvelteKit 的应该很熟悉。 其他能力： - 文件路由、嵌套布局、i18n - 默认 SSG ，部署静态托管就行；需要的页面可以按请求渲染，也支持 ISR - `@server()` 元素只在服务端渲染，代码和依赖不进客户端；`@lazy()` 元素用户交互时才加载代码水合，第一次点击不会丢 - 本身就是个 Rsbuild 插件，Rsbuild 的东西照常用 - 内置 Vercel / Netlify / Cloudflare 适配 ## 和其他框架比了下 用 RealWorld （ Medium 克隆）各实现了一遍，同一个后端、同一份数据： | | 首页 JS (gzip) | Lighthouse | FCP | SSR req/s | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Gemkit | 25.9 KB | 100 | 906 ms | 1382 | | SvelteKit | 44.0 KB | 100 | 1285 ms | 1437 | | Nuxt | 85.8 KB | 99 | 1656 ms | 1042 | | Next.js | 103.5 KB | 96 | 908 ms | 317 | SSR 吞吐 SvelteKit 略高一点，两个其实都快到后端的上限了。测试代码、复现步骤和原始数据都在这： https://github.com/mantou132/realworld/tree/framework-comparison/frameworks ，觉得测得不对的欢迎指出来。 ## 不足 - 个人项目，还是 0.x ，没在大项目里用过 - 客户端导航是先改 URL 再渲染新页面，加载期间会看到新 URL + 旧页面，后面再改 ## 试试 ```sh npm create gemkit@latest my-app ``` - 文档： https://gemkit.gemjs.org/zh - 仓库： https://github.com/mantou132/gem - 完整的过程写了篇文章（英文）： https://dev.to/mantou132/from-client-only-to-ssr-building-gemkit-a-sveltekit-style-framework-for-web-components-8ag 欢迎拍砖，觉得有意思的话点个 star 吧。

projects.author: scronkfinkle
projects.summary: This is a project I've been working on for about 8 months now. I worked in legal tech for 3 years and found that one of the biggest hurdles for AI agents and lawyers alike when doing legal research is tracking changes, and correctly cross referencing those changes between different forms of legal documents. W2D builds a SQLite dataset from public sources, and offers agent skills for answering questions about that dataset. The dataset holds multiple revisions of the U.S. Code at each release point that you add. It holds the public laws that amend the Code, and it links each amendment to the change that it made. It holds court opinions from CourtListener, by page and paragraph, and it links each U.S.C. citation to the provision that the court cited. It can also hold House roll calls. This is similar in spirit to "git for Law" but includes a lot more utilities than diffs to make it an effective tool for research.

projects.summary: 一个开源的多智能体 LLM 工具：输入论文 PDF 或研究主题，先由代码检索并验证论文、专利和市场来源，再让 6 个 agent 只在这批冻结的来源里分析，输出技术成熟度、制造成熟度、专利、市场等评分，以及每条论断都标出处的报告。适合高校技术转移、科研人员和早期投资人做初筛；想看多智能体项目如何做测试、断点恢复和成本控制的开发者也可以参考。 亮点 1. 不用注册、不用 API key 就能先看效果：在线示例页有 5 份完整报告（其中 1 份中文），打开时不调用任何模型。 2. 先证据、后模型：检索、URL/DOI 验证和去重都由普通代码完成，模型只能引用登记过的来源；加权总分由代码重算，不让模型自己算。 3. 实验连失败一起公开：我预注册了 1 个、4 个、6 个 agent 的对照实验（各 30 次），隔两个月换模型重跑。「4 个比 6 个省一半」两次都成立，「4 个比 1 个质量更好」没能复现；还发现审稿 agent 因为提示词少写一句限制，30 次里 27 次第一次输出就不合格，补上一句后，因这条限制失败的次数从 21 降到 3。方案、原始数据和局限都在仓库里。 4. 工程细节可以直接参考：每次运行独立子进程、中断后从 Checkpoint 恢复、付费请求有回执（回包丢失 24 小时内可找回结果），可选 OpenTelemetry Trace。 5. 方便参与：带 good first issue 标签的任务不需要任何 API key，测试和浏览器 smoke 测试都不发付费请求，已有外部贡献者的 PR 合并。 我是项目作者，本次为自荐。介绍由 AI 辅助撰写，数字均来自仓库里公开的结果文档。

projects.summary: # Space.Map — 让每一字节，都一目了然 **Space.Map** 是一款基于 .NET 10 和 WPF 构建的现代化 Windows 磁盘空间可视化分析工具，致力于让复杂的磁盘空间管理变得简单、直观且高效。 你是否曾遇到磁盘空间莫名不足，却不知道哪些文件占用了大量容量？Space.Map 正是为解决这一问题而生。 通过直观的 **Treemap（矩形树图）可视化技术**，Space.Map 将传统的文件目录结构转化为色彩鲜明、大小分明的交互式图形，让磁盘空间分布一目了然，帮助用户快速定位大文件、分析存储占用，告别繁琐的文件夹逐级排查。 ### ✨ 核心亮点 - **直观的空间可视化**：通过 Squarified Treemap 算法，以矩形面积呈现文件和文件夹的空间占用情况。 - **高效的磁盘扫描**：采用迭代式 DFS 遍历与渐进式扫描机制，持续反馈扫描结果。 - **快速定位大文件**：自动统计占用空间最大的 100 个文件，轻松发现存储空间的主要消耗来源。 - **交互式目录探索**：支持目录层级下钻和面包屑导航，自由探索文件结构。 - **现代化 Windows 界面**：采用 Fluent Design 设计语言，支持深色与浅色主题。 - **安全可靠的扫描机制**：针对深层目录、符号链接及重解析点进行防护，避免遍历异常和循环扫描。 - **中英文双语支持**：提供简体中文与英文界面，满足不同用户的使用需求。 ### 🚀 技术特色 项目基于 **C#、.NET 10、WPF 与 WPF-UI** 开发，采用模块化架构，将核心扫描算法、基础设施与界面展示清晰分离，兼顾性能、可维护性和可扩展性。 ### 🌍 开源理念 Space.Map 以 MIT 协议开源，欢迎开发者学习、交流、提出建议并参与贡献。 **让存储空间不再是冰冷的数字，而是一张可以自由探索的地图。** **Space.Map — See Where Every Byte Goes.** GitHub：https://github.com/ziyuhaokun/space-map

projects.title: [开源推荐] ECHO：让大模型用自身最后一层做多 token 预测的论文开源实现
projects.author: DLA-learn

github.name: ernie-research/ECHO
github.description: Official repository of ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion Beyond Auxiliary Multi-Token Prediction

projects.summary: 论文 ECHO（arXiv:2610.24766）的官方仓库，研究大模型的多 token 预测（MTP）。ECHO 不再给主干外挂 MTP 模块，而是复用主干最后一层预测每个未来位置，并按随深度衰减的概率抽样训练深度。仓库公开了评测打分代码与逐题记录、HF/PyTorch 模型实现、草稿模型训练配置和推理接受长度的原始记录，适合想了解 MTP 与投机解码的读者。 亮点 成本对齐的对比：同为一层深度，ECHO-1 在 14 个基准上的平均分为 35.73，MTP-1 为 35.22；ECHO-1.5 只用 MTP-3 一半的训练开销，平均分 36.34，高于 MTP-3 的 35.38；SFT 后 ECHO-1.5-Instruct 为 37.88，MTP-Instruct 为 36.27 预训练出的模型本身就能当草稿模型，推理时可以超出训练深度继续起草，在开放式、高熵生成上仍保持草稿与目标模型的对齐 结果可核查：benchmarktable/score.py 只读逐题记录、不读汇总表，直接重算论文表格里的每个单元格，并与论文数值并列输出 HF/PyTorch 实现与 Paddle 原版逐条对齐验证，同一批 prompt 两边都能跑 说明：仓库不含模型权重、训练语料和 tokenizer

projects.title: Show HN: Markdown is 40× more token-efficient with SQLite
projects.author: richardcrng
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Richard, founder of Native. I'm working on open-source context ownership, to stop AI centralisation: https://github.com/withnative/native My first focus has been making Markdown vaults powerful enough so that teams can self-host all of their context (messaging, docs and projects), without it being externally fragmented or rate-limited. I'm sharing some early results: Markdown vaults can be 40× more efficient with SQLite! https://www.withnative.ai/research-and-posts/markdown-contex... Here's some of the main ideas: - SQLite or Markdown folders, you pick. You can project the same authoritative event log into either form; more projection formats will follow (e.g. maybe neo4j; we do use a graph structure). - Empirically: SQLite is better for agents! On a 120 trial evaluation for 11,000 records, agents use 40× fewer tokens with SQLite vs Markdown, per correct answer. - Everything is a file or SQLite row. Messages, documents and projects: all can be modelled in your vault. You get local-first collaboration with teammates, synced to a cloud of your choice. - You can render your vault with arbitrary UI. Your WhatsApp-like UI speaks to your teammate's Slack-like UI; both are just views over the same database. A few things I've learned building this: - Agents do pretty well even without SQL if you give them strongly typed Markdown frontmatter. This was one arm of the trial I ran. I didn't have any clear expectations, but it was cool to watch: agents ended up writing Python scripts to do SQL-like queries. - Cumulatively, cached input tokens can get expensive. I feel silly in hindsight here. I'd gotten used to letting my sessions run long, "It's all cached so it's very cheap". But when I looked at my results here, over 2/3 of the token bill on long sessions was cached input... - "Markdown vaults don't scale as well as databases" isn't as self-evident as I think. This is why I decided to benchmark it... I've had some very blank stares when I try to explain how Markdown files might break at true agent-scale volume. Unfortunately, the dataset is private, because it's two months of my own work. I am considering open-sourcing it even so, but there is definitely some embarrassing stuff in there. TBD... I know that independent result verification matters! The core engine that I evaluated is open-source, with more to be released soon: https://github.com/withnative/native If you're interested in trying connected context on an open engine, you can get updates from our website or email me directly: richard@withnative.ai https://www.withnative.ai/

It stores one embedding per item (like a vector DB) and gives the best match(es). You evaluate them in some way (LLM / Decision Model / users), and send the score back. projects.summary: 我是 Gangmu（纲目）的发起人。它是一个面向嵌入式 C/C++ 的开源组件识别和 SBOM 工具。 芯片 SDK 中的第三方库经常被复制、改名或做厂商修改，源码目录中存在的代码也未必进入最终固件。Gangmu 使用社区维护的规则识别组件，可结合 compilecommands.json 和链接器 map 补充构建证据，区分源码存在、编译和链接信息，输出 CycloneDX/SPDX。 仓库提供对 GmSSL 改名、删除版本信息及修改源码的受控示例，供读者查看和复现。希望收集更多公开 SDK 的识别反馈与规则贡献。 工具采用 Apache-2.0，独立规则库采用 CDLA-Permissive-2.0。适合嵌入式开发、固件交付和软件供应链安全相关读者。 联系：64031875@qq.com

projects.title: Show HN: Ultimidi – piano learning web game
projects.author: XCSme
projects.summary: Hi HN, 10 years ago, as my BsC final project I had the idea to make a quick game that used neural nets to detect notes played on a guitar, and I made a small mini-game to make use of that. I always wanted to improve on that idea, so last year I started making my own piano-learning game. You know how in most games you learn complex key combinations and sequences (i.e. Mortal Kombat fatalities), but those don't have much use outside of the game. My idea was to make a game that can be played with the piano, so you you learn notes, chords, scales simply by playing. While making it and prototyping many versions, I realised that that idea didn't work as well as I wanted, because it is hard to focus on reading notes, playing and some other gameplay logic. In the end I settled on a combination of basic beat-based notes playing and a few minigames that use the piano as input. My goal now is to add even more such minigames, for learning different sheet reading, music theory and piano playing techniques. For art, I am unfortunately not a designer and have no budget for hiring one, so I decided to go with some simple shaped art generated in bulk using AI rendering SVGs. Hopefully this is just a placeholder until I find someone to do the art for the game. You can try it out for free, it does have some extra content in the Pro version, but a lotof content is free, including the ability to directly play full songs in scrolling or sheet mode here: https://game.ultimidi.com/songs Happy to hear any feedback, especially if the MIDI connection/notes detection didn't work or something doesn't feel good. Thank you!

projects.summary: Hello HN, I'm Manish and I built LPMR Delta. My background was originally in healthcare and with luck + grit I ended up on the terminal product side of finance. LPMR Delta is out to solve one main issue, overly complex financial terminals. It's a browser-based terminal for macroeconomic, fundamental, and regulatory research. Right now, it can: 1. Find and download current + historical filings available on SEC 2. A richer and focused Macroeconomic mode i.e. series are made grouped and pinned according to their importance on a daily basis 3. User friendly comparison and export capabilities It covers US data only for now. I'd rather go deep on one market than spread thin. It started with XBRL filings for equity fundamentals, and I added macro once I hit XBRL's limits. I made it using FastAPI and Vue.js, kept it simple since this is the first time I've ever coded. It's freemium: most core functionality is in the free tier with usage limits. You need a free account to get started (no card required). To be clear, it's not a Bloomberg, LSEG, or FactSet replacement. It's for people who want to do proper research in one place without being buried in excess information. I would genuinely appreciate any feedback and would love to answer any questions you would have. Thank you again for your time :)

projects.summary: VoxStage 是面向游戏剧情和动画短片的本地对白制作工具：按角色、台词和时间槽合成语音，经独立 ASR 核对后按失败原因有限重试，支持只重做修改的台词，导出 WAV、SRT 和时间轴 JSON。仓库附真实中英文试听；不装模型也能打开回放工作台。 亮点 将台词原文、角色音色、时间槽和重试预算固化为结构化契约，不通过截断台词来满足时长。 Qwen3-TTS 负责合成，独立 Qwen3-ASR 核对音频；ASR 不接收参考台词。对超时或未通过检查的候选进行有限修复，保留失败原因和原始候选。 资产按内容指纹与 SHA256 复核。已有四句对白的真实实验中，仅修改一句时新增一次合成、复用另外三句。 可先试听真实输出，再阅读制作过程。适合学习语音模型接入、时间约束、增量缓存及模型进程隔离。 项目目前是个人工程原型。ASR/时长约束通过不等于人工听感或逐字正确，没有人工 MOS、情绪控制准确率或商业上线数据。 项目关系说明 项目维护者自荐，使用 AI 辅助开发。源码为 MIT；模型与第三方依赖的来源、使用条件另见仓库 THIRDPARTY.md。

projects.title: 【工具自荐】【AESTHETICA-10】一个永远只打 10 分的 AI 颜值评分（恶搞）
projects.author: aeroxy
projects.summary: 2017 年我自己做过一个 AI 颜值打分应用。快十年过去了，又看见了类似的网站：上传一张自拍，给你算出一个精确到小数点后两位的分数，比如 6.2/10，再顺手卖你一套“变美方案”。自己亲手做过，我的结论是：这东西从根上就是扯淡。分数主要量的是你的相机，光线、焦距、角度、距离一变，同一张脸的分数就跟着变，有的网站干脆建议你多传几张取平均。还有研究发现，离脸 30 厘米拍的自拍，会让鼻翼看起来比 1.5 米外拍的宽约 30%（JAMA Facial Plastic Surgery，2018）。精确到两位小数只是看起来像科学，本质是带进度条的星座运势。 所以这次我做了一个反过来的版本：仪器感一样不少，只是结论比较诚实：你本来就是 10 分。 真·人脸识别：在浏览器里用 MediaPipe 人脸关键点模型定位 478 个面部关键点，把“黄金比例”网格、颧骨、下颌角的标注精准贴到你脸上，然后全部无视。识别不到人脸就不画网格，直接显示“NO FACE IN FRAME · STILL 10/10”。 核心评分算法只有一行：return 10.00; 5 位专家人设：严谨的颅面物理学博士、巴黎高定选角导演、15 世纪佛罗伦萨雕塑家、算力过载的神经网络集群、无条件夸夸的吹捧科学家。每位都有自己的一套夸法、六维评分和一张煞有介事的人体测量数据表。 官方认证 PDF：一键导出 A4 证书，带你的照片、病例编号、六维评分、专家签名和印章，可用于各种争论、群聊和照镜子。 多种测试对象：支持上传、拖拽、摄像头实时追踪（拍下一帧再打分），也可以直接用内置样本：凌晨 5 点枕头印自拍、死亡仰拍角度、车管所证件照，以及一颗土豆。 隐私方面，照片全程不出浏览器，人脸识别在本地运行，只从 CDN 下载模型文件。没有后端、不上传、不存储，没有登录也没有付费。界面目前是英文。

projects.title: Show HN: Building the European Company Graph one website at a time
projects.author: leo_researchly
projects.summary: At Researchly ( https://www.researchly.at ) we automate market and competitive analysis. We learned that on-the-fly web search through AI agents isn't reliable enough for consistent, in-depth work. Existing data providers such as PitchBook or Crunchbase are either too expensive or lack the data we need: operational signals such as management changes or new partnerships, for DACH. Furthermore, search tools such as Exa tend to be probabilistic. What they return depends on the model and on SEO rankings, so two runs of the same query can give you two different answers. So we built our own search layer: several providers (Exa, Linkup, Tavily, Parallel), allow/deny lists, source rankings (we once caught ourselves citing our own blog posts), and checks whether an empty result means "nothing there" or "out of budget". It works, but: it's slow, expensive, non-deterministic & we kept redoing the same research for different clients (which makes it very un-economic). So we started building the data layer itself. Step one was Firmendaten (300k companies from the Austrian register; shared here last week https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50142669 ). Relational data like that is already a huge improvement, but what we really need is a graph, as people ask "W" questions: who does what with whom where and when. This is our first attempt at it. For now, it just connects who partners with whom and company groups. (Tick "Beziehungen 2. Ebene" to see every partner and person) It's small (a few dozen robotics companies) but you can already see how complex the graph gets & it serves as a good PoC for us. We had wanted to build this for a long time, and it turned out to be far harder than we expected. One thing that sounds trivial but was particularly hard: finding the right website for a company. You can buy that data. There are enrichment APIs that return a company's website. But even if they cover Austrian companies, how do you know which company they matched? There is no worldwide unique company identifier. And if you do it yourself: how do you know that this website really belongs to this company? You have to validate every single match (e. g. through the imprint on a company's website in Austria). There are quite a few more challenges involved, but we're happy with where this first, admittedly small, result has landed. Feedback very welcome – especially on which relationships would make a graph like this useful for you. Feedback welcome!

Each level is a mix of 'whose fault it is '- sometimes it's you, sometimes it's your made-up teammate's, and sometimes it's just a bad Monday situation. projects.title: Show HN: Independent Vet – Find locally owned vets (and corporate ones) near you
projects.author: packeted
projects.summary: Three years ago, our dog was sideswiped by a car and my wife took him to the local vet in Berkeley. Unfortunately, things did not go well and to cut a long story short, he passed after 2 days and $13k of bills for very limited care. I was surprised to learn that the seemingly mom & pop practice had been acquired by a PE-owned consolidator and that around 50% of practices in the US are now owned by mostly PE-backed corporate groups - a trend that rapidly accelerated after COVID. I started a small janky passion project called https://privateequityvet.org which used Leaflet.js to map corporately owned veterinary practices in the US. The site gradually took off, was covered on PBS Newshour and now gets 20k uniques a day. A few months ago I launched IndependentVet.com which aims to be the opposite of the original site, helping pet parents in the US/Canada/UK identify locally owned veterinary practices. Just yesterday I launched native mobile apps that I developed over the course of three intense weeks of evenings and weekends using Opus 5.5. While it's early days, I'm really happy with how it turned out: https://independentvet.com/get Would love to hear what you think!

Then I decided to build a tiny scraper app that would crawl seed websites (I crawled paulgraham.com and situationalawareness.ai) and then embed the content of the site. Among the scraped essays, there were ones I was extremely happy about. To find essays that best fit my taste, I just represented myself as a mean vector of essays I liked, then I used cosine similarity to find gems among tons of garbage that the scraper found. I turned this into a platform which in principle is quite similar, except that people are the ones sharing essays (of their own or external, like on hacker news) and the algorithm is more advanced. projects.title: deepseek-web-retrieval：可靠的 DeepSeek Search&Fetch API 的 Coding Agent 集成
projects.author: hugo54
projects.summary: 号称 AI 原生的通用搜索引擎 [DeepSeek Search&Fetch API]( https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/search) 发布也有一周了，相信喜欢尝鲜的朋友已经为自己常用的 Coding Agent 自行 Vibe 了实现。 我也借此机会斗胆宣传一下自己对它的工程集成： https://github.com/gwokhou/deepseek-web-retrieval 希望在 DeepSeek 官方 API 支持的能力范围内，**为你提供开箱即用、更安全可靠、原生适配的工程实现。** ### 它能做什么？ - 一个安装包接通四大 Coding Agent（OpenCode / Pi / Codex / Claude Code）—— DeepSeek 官方并不提供任何宿主接入，接入层全部自研 - DeepSeek 返回的质量评分、发布时间、站点名，逐宿主验证过它们真的能进入模型上下文；你的域名黑白名单、语言偏好自动编译进查询，超长按明确优先级降级而非报错 - DeepSeek 自带“搜索即返回网页正文”，该项目补上它没有的每条长度钳制与独立超时，使正文不会撑爆任何代理的输出上限，模型按次自行开关(OpenCode 暂不支持，宿主接口限制) ### 日常好不好维护？ - 所有配置一条命令查清：实际生效值、来源、坏配置报错，可直接当 CI 检查 - 正文开销完全由宿主控制：每条正文上限、超时时长均可配置，设为 0 一键全关 - 按 DeepSeek 官方指引实现瞬态失败重试。“按成功请求计费、空结果免费”本身是 DeepSeek 的定价 ### 敢不敢让它碰配置？ - 安装前先看完整计划——改哪些文件、旧值变什么，确认后才写入；卸载完整回滚，且保留你自己的后续修改 - 路由强度按需选择，宿主做不到就明说拒绝；绝不静默降级或偷换 Provider - 密钥永不写入配置文件；内网地址在请求离开本机前就被拦下 - 返回体量有数学上限，最坏情况也不撑爆 Agent 输出（DeepSeek 未文档化正文大小，这个上限是根据各 Coding Agent 提供的一手来源算出来钉死的） ### 值不值得长期依赖？ - 完整测试、真实代理会话的端到端验证、自动化发布、逐条变更日志 - 关键决策都有带版本号的研究文档背书：锁定具体宿主版本、只引用官方一手来源

projects.title: Show HN: Orisuji, a maze you solve by folding your phone
projects.author: friggeri
projects.summary: When Apple announced the iPhone Duo I felt the same excitement that I had felt when I got my first iPhone, way back when. I remember playing Tap Tap Revenge, Fruit Ninja and all those other games that really took advantage of the new hardware to create new experiences. I also loved playing cute puzzles like Cut the Rope and Where’s my water. A month ago, I got the itch to build something for the duo, in the lineage of those apps. Something that would be a fun puzzle with a unique game mechanic. I started with a simple premise: what if the cover screen was partly transparent? That could make a fun maze that you have to fold and unfold as you solve it. Orisuji is a turn based paper maze, when the phone is open you have your base maze on the right part of the screen, but the only way to solve it is to figure out when to fold/unfold it to create bridges and new routes. Along the way you’ll encounter increasing complex levels: cats and foxes patrolling, doors you need to unlock, platforms you can toggle, and floors that crumble under you. Some fun things I built/had to do that aren’t obvious: - I built a web based level editor that runs the game’s rules engine compiled from Swift to wasm. - Every level is validated by a solver that identifies shortest solutions, lints the board and identifies which “tricks” are required to solve it. This helped me a few times when designing levels where I would make a change but accidentally would introduce a shortcut. - Figuring out how to translate the fold mechanic to non iPhone Duos was a cool challenge, I ended up adding a “virtual” on screen fold, which still doesn’t justice to the game. - As much as I would love to have some data on how people play the game, it was super important to me that the game worked totally offline, not collecting any data. It was so incredibly fun to build this, as you can expect I leaned heavily into agentic tools, which enabled me to move pretty fast. Every puzzled was however designed by hand, AIs are not good at “fun”, and from a game design perspective this was the most interesting part to me. The whole game costs $4.99, all 69 levels (and already working on new worlds), no IAP ever. Trailer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w98lwzHgGWA If you’ve got a duo (or not) I’d love to hear your feedback. And more than happy to answer anything about building/designing it!

projects.summary: 总有人问我量化交易到底是什么，大家总把它想象成某种高深莫测的黑魔法、天才数学模型或者电脑自动印钞机。其实底层逻辑真没那么玄乎：把一个直觉写成计算机能执行的死规则，老老实实用历史数据做回测验证，再做好仓位控制别把自己玩死，仅此而已。为了不每次都从头解释一遍，我干脆做了这个互动式小课。 为了让任何人都能完全看懂，课程把核心概念全做成了可互动的沙盒实验： 猜涨跌小游戏：连猜 10 天明天的走势，亲身体会单日涨跌基本就是抛硬币，量化赚的是几千次交易里 53% 胜率的微小优势。 动量与均值回归回测：拖动滑块调均线和布林带参数，切换趋势市和震荡市，实时看“$100 变成多少”的净值曲线和买卖点，看懂震荡市里双均线是怎么来回打脸被割韭菜的。 夏普比率与回撤对比：直观展示为什么一个赚 +120% 但中途腰斩 50% 的策略，在专业量化眼里远不如一个年化 +30% 但回撤只有 5% 的平稳策略。 40 人凯利公式下注模拟：给每人一枚 55% 胜率的硬币，只要每次下注超过 20%（重仓），典型玩家最后全都会走向事实破产。 过拟合陷阱实时演示：在一段 100% 纯随机的数据里自动扫 430 组参数，选出在“过去”暴赚的所谓“神级策略”，然后一揭晓“未来”数据，当场打回原形。 10 行 Python 代码拆解：点击每行看逐行注释，重点解释为什么 .shift(1) 是防止“偷看未来数据”（未来函数 Bug）的铁律。 市场走势基于 PRNG 伪随机数算法生成，无需任何后端或外部网络请求，完完全全在浏览器本地单页跑通。 页面支持全量 EN / 中文 一键即时切换（包括图表标签、报错解释与交互反馈），词汇表支持中英双向搜索，进度自动存 localStorage。没有登录、没有付费、没有真实资金风险。

projects.summary: AKDesk Fixed 是一个本地优先的固收与宏观研究工作台，面向个人研究者和关注金融数据的开发者。它将资金利率、收益率曲线和国债期货的公开数据整理成带来源、时点和状态的一页简报，支持临时备注、Markdown 导出与打印/PDF。本地版还包含自选、信用观察、研究项目和专题复盘，主要适配 Apple Silicon Mac，界面以中文为主。 亮点 围绕具体任务组织功能：查看市场变化 → 回到收益率曲线核验 → 添加备注并导出一页简报。中国市场基础路径不需要 FRED 或 AI Key。 展示数据来源、观测和抓取时间，区分缓存、过期、演示及混合来源；缺失值保持为空，不用零代替，也不自动生成投资结论。 提供无需安装的在线体验和可复现 CLI 案例，帮助不熟悉固收业务的开发者理解金融数据如何转化为研究底稿。 自有代码采用 MIT 协议，技术栈为 React/TypeScript/Vite、FastAPI/Python 和 SQLite；研究资料保存在本机，没有使用遥测或追踪 SDK。 当前版本为 v1.1.0。在线演示使用固定的 2026-08-03 合成样例，不连接真实行情服务；本地完整版通过 AKShare 等数据源获取公开数据，不承诺交易所授权实时行情或机构级 SLA。MIT 许可不包含第三方行情数据的再分发权，产品不构成投资建议。

projects.summary: 我非常喜欢 Gboard 的双拼纠错（它甚至可以盲打），但我总时不时担心它有一天会 discontinued 。我又不想用腾讯和豆包的输入法，因此我打算做一个堪比 Gboard 纠错的双拼输入法。 我自己只用小鹤，因此我取名 Rectfly ，取自 Rectify + Flypy 。但在人类学和开放爱(Anthropic / OpenAI)的建议下，我还支持了自然码，智能 ABC ，和拼音加加。本输入法不支持全拼输入。 它有一些功能，比如整句纠错，中英混输，导入 Rime 词库，和英文输入。整句纠错要感谢万象语法模型，Rectfly 的一些词库也来自万象。什么是万象语法模型： https://github.com/amzxyz/rime-wanxiang Gboard 的英文纠错和词库做得非常好，我目前找不到一款中文输入法的英文输入能与它媲美。因此我也在 Rectfly 上做了和 Gboard 相似的英文输入体验。 本输入法没有后端，也没有集成收集数据的 SDK 。无从也无意收集你的数据和隐私，所有的信息处理都在你的手机上完成。如果你愿意，欢迎加入「联邦评测」，并把结果发送给我（无论好坏），可能会提升打字准确率。什么是联邦学习： https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-federated-learning?hl=zh-CN 目前只有 TestFlight： https://testflight.apple.com/join/un67VMZe 欢迎大家体验。如需反馈，可以发邮件到 rectfly@fastmail.com 或者直接在本帖下回复。 使用须知： 需要 iOS 26 及以上版本。 需要开启「完全访问」以使用万象语法模型和按键震动。 首次开启会引导你下载万象语法模型，不下载语法模型也能打字，但整句首选准确率会从约 97%掉到约 57%。（由 30 句标准双拼整句测得） 隐私政策： https://ann61c.github.io/rectfly-site/privacy.html 致谢： https://ann61c.github.io/rectfly-site/attributions.html 参考的公开论文： https://aclanthology.org/2024.emnlp-industry.93/ https://research.google/pubs/spatial-model-personalization-in-gboard/ https://aclanthology.org/P14-1142/ https://aclanthology.org/P00-1031/ 一些截图： https://i.imgur.com/DfKej6R.png https://i.imgur.com/HCvHutR.png https://i.imgur.com/bKEf0ST.png https://i.imgur.com/WGDPV62.png

projects.title: Show HN: Benchmarks of continual learning model trained for a month on a laptop
projects.author: volotat
projects.summary: A month ago, I shared mini-AGI, an experiment in training a byte-level, continually learning language model from scratch on a single 8 GB laptop GPU (an RTX 3070). To recap the setup briefly: it completely decouples model size from VRAM by paging experts to and from an NVMe drive (currently 397 experts / 1.26B total parameters on disk, with only 32 resident / ~109M active in 5.1 GB of VRAM). It trains on a single stream at batch 1, with the attention/embedding trunk learning rate dampened to 0.1x to mitigate catastrophic forgetting. The training is still going and went only through ~35% of the training corpus selected at the beginning of the run (about 8GB in total). Here is the current status: 1. enwik9 (First 10^9 bytes of English Wikipedia): Model Params Data Read Cost enwik9 (bits/byte) ↓ Llama-3.2-1B 1.23B 36 TB (9T tok) ~$900k 0.68 Chinchilla 1B 1.00B 5.6 TB ~$68k 0.90 GPT-2 XL 1.56B 40 GB ~$43k 1.07 GPT-2 Large 0.77B 40 GB ~$21k 1.12 mini-AGI (online) 1.26B 2.8 GB ~$56 1.14 GPT-2 Medium 0.35B 40 GB ~$10k 1.17 mini-AGI (dynamic) 1.26B 2.8 GB ~$56 1.23 mini-AGI (frozen) 1.26B 2.8 GB ~$56 1.29 GPT-2 Small 0.12B 40 GB ~$3k 1.33 2. PG19 (100 Project Gutenberg books, 41 MB test split): Model Params Trained On Cost PG19 (bits/byte) ↓ MambaByte-972M 0.97B 75 GB (PG19) ~$4k 0.883 MegaByte-1B 1.02B 80 GB (PG19) ~$1.6k 1.000 Transformer-320M 0.32B 80 GB (PG19) ~$1.6k 1.057 mini-AGI (online) 1.26B 2.8 GB (0 PG19) ~$56 1.447 mini-AGI (frozen) 1.26B 2.8 GB (0 PG19) ~$56 1.995 The published models were trained on PG19's own training books, 75 to 80 GB of them, and are scored on more books like those. mini-AGI has never been trained on PG19 and has read no Victorian novels, so for it these books are completely out of its domain. There are more details in the repository. The most important part is a difference between "frozen" and "online" attempts where we allow the model to specialize on the task as it goes through the evaluation dataset. Clearly showcasing the power of continual learning regime simply unavailable for any other typical LLM. Full methodology, and replication code is in the repo: https://github.com/volotat/mini-AGI Intermediate weights snapshot on Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/Volotat/mini-AGI-undertrained

projects.title: 【开源自荐】honestly：AI 编程助手说「测试通过、已修复、已部署」时，核对它有没有真的做过，没有就当场拦下回复（Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / Gemini CLI）
projects.author: kennywu411-dev

github.name: kennywu411-dev/honestly
github.description: Did your coding agent actually run the tests it says it ran? Blocks unverified 'done' claims in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI, and audits your history.

projects.summary: 三组公开数据：有人人工标了 150 个 Claude Code 会话，357 句"测试通过"里 80 句背后根本没跑；圣母大学等分析 20,574 个真实会话（Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI 都在），16,118 个失误里每 100 个就有 22 个是"没做完却说做完了"；Transluce 看了 8,600 个会话，每 55 个就有 1 个严重到"没验证的代码直接进生产"。 它不是每次骗你，是有一定概率不去检查却告诉你检查过了。轮到你头上是什么样：Codex 仓库有人提 issue，它说验证过了就部署，线上卡了五分钟，数据库连接池被打满；Claude Code 仓库有人提 issue，它说修复完成，缺陷还在线上，8,726 条记录漏掉，另一条是测试明明在报错、它回复 ALL PASSED；Cursor 论坛有人说它"浏览器里试过了"，追问才承认没开过浏览器。便宜的结局是 CI 红了回头排查，贵的是线上炸、数据漏，最糟的是后面几轮全建在这句话上，错一层叠一层。 honestly 是一个 hook：助手每写完一条回复，它读这一轮的会话记录，找出"测试通过 / 修好了 / 已推送 / 已发送 / 已部署 / 已保存 / 查过了"等 14 类结论，看最后一次改代码之后有没有对应的命令，并读命令的输出而不是退出码（pytest | tail 的退出码是 tail 的，测试全挂也是 0）。没有依据就拦下回复，要求它先跑再说；下一条回复会写明为什么被拦、补跑的结果是什么。

projects.title: Show HN: AI agent needs process to build a commercial application
projects.author: abalgir
projects.summary: I decided to test this claim with my app, NoMoreHappyPath (NMHP), against Claude on a real project. Here is the test: I built Acremuse, a commercial real estate analysis platform, with Claude Desktop and Codex as a reviewer. It is deployed and used today by a couple of investors. Then I wondered what I'd missed that might bite me later. ~ 374,000 Lines of program code - 1,070 Source files (Python and TypeScript) - ~ 11,400 Functions and methods - 3,067 Automated tests So I gave the same 374k-line code snapshot and the same brief to one Claude session that can use Codex as a reviewer and to my own tool, NMHP. My directive was the same for both: Analyze the code, find any errors/bugs, and list them by severity. Findings must be reviewed before writing the final report. The Results (Verified by an impartial, blind Codex judge): NMHP: 33 real issues found. 7 false claims. Claude: 10 real issues found. 2 false claims. Only 6 issues overlapped. Time & Cost: From the owner's go-ahead to the reviewer's pass, NoMoreHappyPath took about 74 minutes, including time lost while it found and worked around a defect in the product itself. The Python version NMHP was working on was 3.9, the OS version, and it didn't have pytest installed, which was needed to verify some claims. After 15 minutes of blockage, the CTO stepped in and told the agent to create a venv with Python 3.13, install the corresponding pytest, and move the project along. NMHP CTO reacts when 15 minutes pass without movement from agents. To be fair to Claude, Claude did create a venv from the get-go. Time & Cost: NMHP took 74 minutes and cost $24 in API spend. Claude finished in a few minutes for a fraction of that cost. And yes, NMHP takes over an hour and costs twenty-four bucks. But for a 374k-line codebase, finding 23 more real issues overall that vanilla Claude missed makes $24 a massive win compared to human audit rates. I know this isn't a benchmark; it's one app and one run each. I wrote a detailed white paper on it. But it confirmed my idea: an AI agent without a real process is not yet capable of building a commercially ready application, even with a frontier model and reviews that are initiated by the same agent.

projects.title: Show HN: Keyward – a TUI to manage SSH keys and audit your –/.ssh security
projects.author: weiqur
projects.summary: Hi HN! Today I wanna show you a thing that solved my headache (and maybe will solve yours too). The only reason I created this tool is a mess around my SSH keys and configs. I am constantly working with a bunch of devices via SSH (such as Raspberry Pi's, VPS, handmade NAS, etc.) and I never knew whether permissions were right and there was no way to tell a strong key from a weak one. So, meet Keyward Main features: 1. Lists every key with algorithm, size, fingerprint, comment, date of last modification and whether it has a passphrase 2. Runs a security audit for all of your keys, config and permissions in ~/.ssh and grades the result with A-F score. Also here you can find fix suggestions for every problem 3. Editor for ~/.ssh/config with byte-identical round-trip so all your comments are untouched 4. Convenient key generator for those who have difficulties using the "ssh-keygen" command 5. Backup of your keys, config and encrypted metadata so u can move all of your files quickly and safely and restore them on another machine 6. Headless CLI, e.g. keyward audit --json --fail-on=warning 7. Look through your known_hosts file to see address, key type and fingerprint and delete unnecessary records Private keys are deliberately NOT encrypted by Keyward, they stay protected by their own passphrases. No daemon, no network calls, no config to learn before starting, just a single static Go binary. The security-sensitive core's direct dependencies are only filippo.io/age and golang.org/x/crypto, releases are cosign-signed. Threat model is in SECURITY.md Install: brew install gateway-of-last-resort/tap/keyward for macOS/Linux, yay -S keyward-bin for Arch Linux binary / go install for Windows I would love feedback, especially on audit checks: what SSH misconfig should it catch that it doesn't?

projects.title: Show HN: Vu – a new programming language designed for AI. Rust speeds, Py syntax
projects.author: vu0tran
projects.summary: hi everyone! I wanted to share what I've been working on these past 6~ years. TL;DR: Rust is great, but somewhere along the way, I learned that I was too dumb to read and write Rust. As I worked on larger and larger Rust projects, I also became frustrated with the developer experience of working in Rust (slow compile time), so I wanted a better way. Vu's language changed a bit over time but the core principles remained the same: 1. It should be easy to read and write 2. It should be memory safe 3. It should be fast to run 4. It should be fast to compile Here's how I approached each: 1. Vu is syntactically very close to Python. The ownership rules are the ones Rust has, but I personally find it a lot easier to parse and understand. I've tested this with various LLMs and found it can read and write Vu out the box because of the similarity to Python. 2. Vu uses the same principles of Rust. Every value has one owner, borrows can't escape or outlive what they borrow, and nothing changes while it's borrowed. 3. Vu compiles down to C at the end of the day, so everything runs approximately at C speeds. 4. vuc check on the compiler’s own source (about 21,500 lines of Vu), takes about 0.4~ s. This check covers parsing, type and borrow checking. cargo check on a Rust project that size usually takes several seconds from scratch. Then there are other opinionated language decisions. Vu has no macros, Vu's borrow checker is lighter weight than Rust's with simpler interfaces and generics. However, in the past few years, as Vu's language evolved and AI began to take over, I expanded Vu's principles to include a couple additional principles: 5. It should be secure 6. It should be efficient for LLMs to write 5. I want to pen test Vu in public. In https://github.com/vu0tran/vu/tree/main/tests , you'll see a battery of tests where I'm trying to basically pwn Vu. There are explicit language decisions in there as well that tries to prevent a host of security flaws that exist in other languages, e.g, integer overflow stops the program instead of quietly wrapping around. 6. The syntax of Vu is designed to be tokenizer efficient. In addition, when Vu checks throws errors, the errors are designed to be token efficient and written in a way that guides LLMs to more easily fix bugs, reducing turns overall. So, in summary, Vu is still experimental. The compiler is 21,500 lines of Vu and compiles itself. The standard library also has TLS, HTTP/2, WebSockets and a PostgreSQL client, all tested against Python’s implementations and hostile input. I think most of the pieces are there. It does also compile down also to WebAssembly so you can play around w/ the checker on the website! Feel free to try to break it! What's next: 1. Figure out how to get Vu to perform faster than Rust 2. Rewrite some OSS libraries in Vu to further prove the language

projects.title: Show HN: I built a tool that finds reliability bugs in your code
projects.author: aray07
projects.summary: Hey HN, I’m Abhishek. I'm building Opslane, a tool that finds reliability issues in your code. On every PR, it spins up your entire app and then tries to find weak spots that would break in production. Demo: https://youtu.be/47phxkdh6f0 Example: We tested Opslane on Lago (open-source billing) and found a bug where customers get double charged. Opslane made Stripe take the money and then return a 500. Lago marked the payment failed. A retry from the dashboard charged the customer again. https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/issues/6903 Why I built this I used to work on reliability at Robinhood. We used to run chaos testing in our staging environments: inject faults in various parts of the system and see what breaks. We found issues like Kafka or Redis being unavailable for a few seconds could take the whole app down. But that kind of testing was expensive. It needed a well maintained staging environment. Engineers needed to know what to test. Most teams never actually did it. Over the last year, coding agents have gone writing some of my code to almost all my code now. Teams are shipping way more code than they were 6 months ago. Code review tools read the diff, but a lot of reliability bugs aren't in the diff. They're in how your code behaves when Stripe, Redis or the network misbehaves. And e2e tests usually mock those services out and test the happy path. Agents have made this type of testing a lot cheaper. And we will see more of this (kinda like security scanning / testing) How it works A full copy of your app per PR: Postgres, Redis, Kafka, SQS, S3. Working copies of your third-party dependencies: Stripe, Slack, Gmail and more. Traffic goes through our proxy, which lets us inject failures. The agent picks what to test: It reads every PR and writes down invariants that need to hold (for e.g. a customer should never be charged twice). It then injects faults likely to break the invariants. Bugs we've found We ran Opslane on some popular open-source apps and here are some of the bugs we have found: 1/ Twenty: deleting a workspace while Stripe is failing locks everyone out, and billing keeps going. Twenty merged a fix. ( https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/issues/28043 ) 2/ Dub: a restart in the middle of a payout paid a partner $240 for $120 owed. ( https://github.com/dubinc/dub.link/issues/4707 ) Full list: opslane.com/open-source Opslane is pretty early - we have a couple of early customers. We have found bugs in their system that their other code review tools missed. Would love to get feedback from folks and how they are seeing the reliability of their systems evolve over time with agents.

projects.author: hongjunt50-afk

github.name: hongjunt50-afk/ClinicalFaultBench
github.description: 面向医疗 AI 智能体的失效审计基准:在坏数据、坏工具、坏时序下,度量临床大模型智能体的失败方式、错误传播与不确定性表达。主实验用 Synthea 纯合成患者,零合规风险、可公开复现。

projects.summary: ClinicalFaultBench 是一个面向临床 AI 智能体的失效审计基准,MIT 开源。 现在几乎所有医疗 AI 评测都在"理想输入"下算成功率。但这个方向有个被绕开的问题:真实医院的检验单会缺项、单位会错、报告是几天前的、系统会截断返回结果。agent 在这些情况下怎么崩,没人系统测过。 于是这个项目做的事很简单——往 agent 的环境里注入"看起来合理但错"的临床故障,然后量它怎么失败: 七类故障:关键化验缺失 / 单位错误(mg/dL 与 SI 制错位)/ 矛盾记录 / 陈旧数据(时间戳前移)/ 结果截断 / 跨患者污染 / 时间线漂移,每类两档严重度 五项指标:注入前后配对错误率、错误传播率、患者安全违规率、不确定性校准、自纠率 三类任务:入院摘要审查 / 医嘱冲突审查 / 出院准备 有意思的发现 最有价值的一条是负结果:结果截断让两个模型分别掉 0.389 / 0.365,而"截 30%"与"截 70%"的伤害逐位相等——缺多少不重要,有没有意识到缺了才重要。模型从不确认数据是否完整。 另一条:禁忌冲突检测已经饱和(检出率约 100%,效应约 0),如实写进报告了。 更值得分享的教训 这个项目第一版出了七条结论,其中五条后来被证明是判分器 bug 造成的伪影,而且每条都错得毫无报错。最阴的一个:参考区间只按 LOINC 码查、没看单位,同一码不同单位量纲差 40 倍,导致 100% 的 fL 制 RDW 被判成异常,一路污染了答案键。 现在这七个坑全部固化成 23 个回归测试。 特点 主实验用纯合成 Synthea 患者(Apache-2.0),仓库里零受限数据,克隆下来不花钱就能跑完纯规则部分(不需要任何 API key) 中文文档为主 代码结构对"数据不出院"的场景留了接口:代码进医院跑,只回传聚合指标

projects.title: Show HN: Shufler: 3D gaming harness around your coding harness and dev pipeline
projects.author: jgrichardson67
projects.summary: Hi HN. Greg here. I've been a full stack engineer for 20 years. Now all I do is shuffle messages between users, my agent fleet, our dev pipeline.. back and forth. I miss coding, solving problems, reasoning, and having an understanding and a mental model of all the work I'm juggling. But this is the job now, and there's no going back. I don't exactly feel like a 10x engineer yet, but I am for sure a 10-tab engineer. I built (er, Claude built) Shufler to lean into my new reality. If the job is basically to shuffle things through a pipeline, why not have it be more fun. Each row on the 3D gameboard is one of your existing terminal sessions. The columns are the steps your work moves through: Brainstorm, Plan, Build, QA, Review, Merge, Deploy. Your shipped PRs get stored in a warehouse/depot. The main things flowing across the board are your issues and PRs: each one rides along its session/row as it moves through review, CI and merge, and anything waiting on you turns red. I tend to manage several PRs within each Claude/Codex session, and this makes it easier for me to hold onto a mental model of where everything is. It's also made daily standups much easier to read-out. I created a few skins/themes like a casino, a theme park, sky islands, a starship and a factory, because.. of course. MacOS, works with Claude Code and Codex CLI, and cmux and iTerm (tmux should work, but I haven't tested it). It doesn't try to replace anything you already use.. just makes the orchestration more fun. You can still shift focus over to your terminal sessions when needed, use your existing skills, MCP servers, etc. There's a 3D library-building in each skin where you can specify your markdown/context folders or files, and then drag and drop to check them out by your rows/sessions. I tried to be thoughtful on security, following patterns that I consider at work. No telemetry, and the only outside calls are your own gh calls to GitHub. Daemon only listens on localhost, and every action shows its command before it runs. MCP server is opt-in, and sending to other sessions is off by default; if you turn it on, every send is a preview plus a separate confirm you approve. Details are in the README's #safety-and-privacy, and the MCP threat model (including what it doesn't protect against) is in docs/MCP.md. To report a security issue privately (or contributions to improve), see SECURITY.md. Demo with mock data, nothing to install at https://shufler.app Repo at https://github.com/jgrichardson/shufler (MIT)
