projects.title: Show HN: Instance – A clean-room reimplementation of GameMaker 8.1 in Rust
projects.author: __grob
projects.summary: I used GameMaker 8.1 a ton in late elementary and middle school, and GML was the first programming language I wrote. I still think it's a fun engine to use because it has so many batteries included. So I built an open-source reimplementation of it in Rust which I'm calling Instance. It opens existing .gmk and .gm81 projects and runs them on Windows, macOS and in the browser, with a more efficient GML interpreter than the original GameMaker. You can try the IDE here in your browser: https://groverburger.github.io/instance/ . It comes with three example games, including Spelunky Classic built from Derek Yu's released source shared under its permissive license. Just change something and press Run to see your edits in action. Old GM games depend on a lot of quirks such as the order events run in, the exact random number generator, how sound_isplaying lags behind the audio. I wrote up the behavior as specs from the documentation, the file formats and black-box tests against the real program, then implemented it from those specs. No proprietary code was disassembled or decompiled. CLEANROOM.md describes the process. It covers most of almost all of 8.1. All the resource editors, GML and drag-and-drop actions, d3d, particles, surfaces, MIDI, mplay multiplayer and DLL calls. It can also export a game as a standalone executable or a single HTML file. Projects can be saved as folders of plain text and PNG files for git. I wrote most of the code with Claude Opus 5.5 over about three weeks. Claude banged out a pretty good reimplementation in a morning, but as always the last 20% took 80% of the work. GameMaker also turns out to work surprisingly well with LLMs. GML is small and simple, and a whole game fits in one project file. I'm happy to answer any questions! Code: https://github.com/groverburger/instance

projects.summary: This is basically the doomgeneric idea but applied to Minecraft (its first version rd-132211 that came out on 13 May 2009). It's one freestanding C file with no includes and no memory allocation. It runs in a terminal, over telnet as shared multiplayer, as a 20 KB wasm module, inside a PDF on Chrome and on a bare x86 PC with no OS, and on a jailbroken Kindle Paperwhite. PDFium doesn't have WebAssembly so the C goes to wasm with clang and then binaryen's wasm2js turns it into JavaScript. It also compiles for a Raspberry Pi Pico and Game Boy Advance, but I don't have any of these so haven't tested it. If someone has one would love to hear how it works there. The browser version can be played here directly: https://pragyaangaur.github.io/Can-It-Run-Minecraft Used Claude for the C and JavaScript code because that's outside my area of work. I picked the targets and tested everything. The Kindle version ended up being an extended project so it's not in the linked repo: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Inkwell And if anyone has any crazier places it could run on (someone please do it on a pregnancy test) do try and share it... maybe I could add it to the repo!

github.description: AI multi-agent tool that turns research papers into cited commercialization and tech-transfer assessments: TRL, patent landscape, market and risks. CrewAI + FastAPI, with a reproducible benchmark.

projects.summary: 一个开源的多智能体 LLM 工具：输入论文 PDF 或研究主题，先由代码检索并验证论文、专利和市场来源，再让 6 个 agent 只在这批冻结的来源里分析，输出技术成熟度、制造成熟度、专利、市场等评分，以及每条论断都标出处的报告。适合高校技术转移、科研人员和早期投资人做初筛；想看多智能体项目如何做测试、断点恢复和成本控制的开发者也可以参考。 亮点 1. 不用注册、不用 API key 就能先看效果：在线示例页有 5 份完整报告（其中 1 份中文），打开时不调用任何模型。 2. 先证据、后模型：检索、URL/DOI 验证和去重都由普通代码完成，模型只能引用登记过的来源；加权总分由代码重算，不让模型自己算。 3. 实验连失败一起公开：我预注册了 1 个、4 个、6 个 agent 的对照实验（各 30 次），隔两个月换模型重跑。「4 个比 6 个省一半」两次都成立，「4 个比 1 个质量更好」没能复现；还发现审稿 agent 因为提示词少写一句限制，30 次里 27 次第一次输出就不合格，补上一句后，因这条限制失败的次数从 21 降到 3。方案、原始数据和局限都在仓库里。 4. 工程细节可以直接参考：每次运行独立子进程、中断后从 Checkpoint 恢复、付费请求有回执（回包丢失 24 小时内可找回结果），可选 OpenTelemetry Trace。 5. 方便参与：带 good first issue 标签的任务不需要任何 API key，测试和浏览器 smoke 测试都不发付费请求，已有外部贡献者的 PR 合并。 我是项目作者，本次为自荐。介绍由 AI 辅助撰写，数字均来自仓库里公开的结果文档。

projects.author: knarykov
projects.summary: This is a variation of chess in which, in addition to the arrangement of the pieces, the rules governing pawn movement are altered, and new rules are introduced: Called Diagonals, Diago, or DiagoChess. Standard 8x8 board. White sets up in the bottom-right corner (King on h1) and moves first; Black sets up in the top-left corner (King on a8). Movement: Kings, Queens, Rooks, Bishops, and Knights move normally. Pawns move 1 square in any direction to empty squares, but capture strictly diagonally. Special Rules: No check, checkmate, castling, pawn promotion, or en passant. Win Conditions: First player to capture the enemy King wins immediately. Attacked King Mechanics: Streak Reset: The attacked turn counter resets to zero as soon as your turn starts with your King safe. You can play this version on the website; I've added full-fledged multiplayer with the ability to create public and private rooms. The multiplayer is powered by NOSTR (nostr relays). The website features a game against a bot at various difficulty levels, single-screen gameplay, online matches against other players, a time limit like in chess, and even a profile (either as a guest by entering just a nickname, or via Nostr).

projects.title: Show HN: ssh zydra.sh, a GPU Linux desktop in your terminal, with Doom
projects.author: teledream
projects.summary: ssh zydra.sh There's no sign-up or anything, and you get a 15-minute demo of a graphical Linux VM drawn entirely in your terminal. It has a browser, an editor, and it runs Doom. It works best in Kitty or Ghostty. WezTerm and Konsole also work, as well as Sixel and iTerm2 terminals, though with less detail. Text-only terminals support non-graphical apps: shells, editors, and other TUIs. Why? For a few months I ran coding agents in tmux on a VPS over SSH, and it sucked. I couldn't paste images, scrolling broke and I didn't wanna figure out why, I had no notifications for when an agent finished, I couldn't see browsers agents opened to smoke-test, logins drifted between my laptop and the server, I couldn't check in from my phone, and to know what an agent had done five minutes ago I had to read through opaque chunks of tool calls. These issues added up and had me in a limbo: They made my setup bad enough to annoy me every day, but not quite bad enough to stop my real work and fix it. How it works: Zydra is a custom (Smithay-based) Wayland compositor in a microVM with an AMD GPU, implementing a series of terminal protocols that solve many issues but are often ignored: Kitty graphics for windows, OSC 52 for the clipboard, images included, OSC 9/99/777 for notifications, SGR mouse for scrolling and clicks. VNC is limited to sending pictures of the screen and diffing frames to find what changed. In Zydra, apps directly tell the compositor what changed, and terminal text is sent as text you can select and copy natively. The browser is a WebKit build that delivers frames to the compositor as DMA-BUFs without a readback, and agents drive it through Playwright. Alt+P is sort of like Raycast: browse apps, linked GitHub, websites, and SSH targets from it. You can watch the desktop at any point in time and rewind to periodic snapshots. To achieve this, the desktop records into a timeline file, a kind of structured video, and the VM takes snapshots along it. You can traverse back like a livestream to see what happened while you were away, then restore or fork the whole machine from that point. Agents can mark points on the timeline and checkpoint the whole machine before risky changes. Other things to try: ssh -t zydra.sh dino # the Chromium dino game via SSH tar -czf - -C ~ .claude .claude.json | ssh -T zydra.sh upload # bring your configs (includes your Claude login) ssh -o ObscureKeystrokeTiming=no -A zydra.sh # lower latency & forward your SSH agent ssh -p 443 zydra.sh # connect from a corporate firewall sshfs zydra.sh: ~/zydra # paid accounts: mount your home Everything runs on one dedicated server with one AMD iGPU, so there are 12 demo slots. When they're full you wait in a queue and can play Chromium's offline dino game. The paid plan is $40/month (+ tax): 8 GB RAM, 4 vCPUs, 80 GB disk, GPU access, with no time limit and a 3-day money-back guarantee. I'll be around all day to answer questions.

projects.title: Show HN: Tabverse – a free, open-source, with self-hostable server Workona clone
projects.author: liyu1981au
projects.summary: Hi, I want to share with you my chrome extension: Tabverse, as it is now passed the reveiw of Chrome Web Store and live at: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/tabverse/lffblcippn... Tabverse is a local first workona like chrome extension for managing tabs, with its source open at https://www.github.com/liyu1981/tabverse . In essential it has the core functions workona has, but can operate totally locally, which means it will not need an account nor subscription. The only limit is your local storage spaces so that you can have as many spaces(I call tabverse) as you can. It is open source, so not just your data stays with you, and the tool itself will stay with you in future. Beyond the normal workona features (persisted workspace, load/reload/import/export, note/bookmark/history tools), there are features does require a server. Features like backup/sync, global search on all tabverses, and future collaboration (not yet done), can only be possible if there is a server. I build this part in open too: the server is free to self host and open source in same repo of Tabverse. The tabverse's idea was with me few years ago while I was using Workona and was frustrated with its limitation on free tier (remember was only 5 workspaces), and the missing features of managing multiple workspaces at the same time. Tabverse takes the idea of Workona, and develop further: each window with a Tabverse tab is a workspace, all stored in local storage, and multi windows can have multi Tabverses same time, and can switch fast. There can even be window without Tabverse, so besides work, personal stuff or entertainment will have place to go. As I build this alone, in the middle, almost give up on this project, and luckily AI agents now is there: not only I have a good helper, but also I have a partner I can discuss a bit. So this time the first version starts with v0.7.2. But AI agent can never replace the real need from human on what should be built and what works better, so I want to share with you and listen to your feedbacks early. Please give it a try, and every feedback to me is a gift. Besides the self-hosted option, I host a server at https://tabverse.liyu1981.xyz (yes, the same website of intro and docs), but is invitation only. If you want to help me to test in this early stage, you can login with Google (the only social login I configured :)), and request an invitation there. I will act as soon as I find your request :). But do not worry at all if you only want to use Tabverse locally without a server -- that is the first thing when I was building it. In current version there are also AI features built in, and again do not worry as the AI features is using Chrome's Prompt API, which is totally local, with Gemini Nano (first time will need to download it automatically), nothing send to a server, and you can always turn this on of off in settings. Morden computers with decent memory should work well, but some older computer may suffer (so please turn off). And it is Chrome only. (Honestly, Tabverse currently only support Google Chrome, but not other Chrome based browsers).

projects.summary: 最近做了一个音乐相关的 Web 工具，ChordFold 。 地址： https://chordfold.com/ 主要功能是：用户选择一段 MP3 或 WAV 音频，AI 自动识别里面的和弦，以及和弦随时间的变化。 和一些需要上传音频到服务器的识别服务不同，我选择了浏览器本地推理的方案。 目前的技术方案： 使用 BTC 系列和弦识别模型 模型转换为 ONNX 格式 通过 ONNX Runtime Web 在浏览器里执行 WASM 推理 对音频进行解码和 CQT 特征提取 模型预测后对结果进行平滑，生成和弦时间轴 用户侧的操作流程也比较简单： 选择本地音频文件 首次使用时下载识别模型 在浏览器本地分析音频 得到按时间排列的和弦结果 点击时间轴上的和弦，可以跳到对应位置回听 可以切换查看支持的吉他和弦指法图、钢琴音符参考 目前限制音频最大 14MB 、最长 10 分钟。 选择本地推理主要有几个考虑： 第一，音频不需要上传服务器，相对更有隐私优势。 第二，不需要为每个用户的识别请求支付云端 GPU 推理费用。 第三，工具本身不需要用户注册账号。 但缺点也很明显。 首先，模型首次下载需要时间。 其次，不同设备上的 WASM 推理性能差异比较大。 还有就是和弦识别的准确率问题。对于干净的钢琴、吉他音频，相对容易分析；复杂编曲、失真、转位和弦以及快速切换的片段，模型仍然可能出现错误。 目前不打算宣传什么 99% 准确率，实际上还没有可靠的统一准确率测试数据。 接下来主要想继续优化识别效果、模型加载和结果交互。 想请教一下 V 友： 有没有做过音乐信息检索（ MIR ）或者音频模型部署的？ 对于浏览器本地音频推理，ONNX Runtime Web + WASM 还有哪些值得优化的方向？ 有更适合浏览器端运行、准确率又比较好的和弦识别模型推荐吗？ 如果你会弹吉他或者钢琴，也欢迎拿一段音频测试一下，看看识别效果怎么样。 技术交流和产品体验方面的建议都欢迎。

projects.title: Show HN: Ultimidi – piano learning web game
projects.author: XCSme
projects.summary: Hi HN, 10 years ago, as my BsC final project I had the idea to make a quick game that used neural nets to detect notes played on a guitar, and I made a small mini-game to make use of that. I always wanted to improve on that idea, so last year I started making my own piano-learning game. You know how in most games you learn complex key combinations and sequences (i.e. Mortal Kombat fatalities), but those don't have much use outside of the game. My idea was to make a game that can be played with the piano, so you you learn notes, chords, scales simply by playing. While making it and prototyping many versions, I realised that that idea didn't work as well as I wanted, because it is hard to focus on reading notes, playing and some other gameplay logic. In the end I settled on a combination of basic beat-based notes playing and a few minigames that use the piano as input. My goal now is to add even more such minigames, for learning different sheet reading, music theory and piano playing techniques. For art, I am unfortunately not a designer and have no budget for hiring one, so I decided to go with some simple shaped art generated in bulk using AI rendering SVGs. Hopefully this is just a placeholder until I find someone to do the art for the game. You can try it out for free, it does have some extra content in the Pro version, but a lotof content is free, including the ability to directly play full songs in scrolling or sheet mode here: https://game.ultimidi.com/songs Happy to hear any feedback, especially if the MIDI connection/notes detection didn't work or something doesn't feel good. Thank you!

github.description: Timed character-dialogue production for games and animation: Qwen TTS, independent ASR checks, bounded repair and incremental audio assets.

projects.summary: VoxStage 是面向游戏剧情和动画短片的本地对白制作工具：按角色、台词和时间槽合成语音，经独立 ASR 核对后按失败原因有限重试，支持只重做修改的台词，导出 WAV、SRT 和时间轴 JSON。仓库附真实中英文试听；不装模型也能打开回放工作台。 亮点 将台词原文、角色音色、时间槽和重试预算固化为结构化契约，不通过截断台词来满足时长。 Qwen3-TTS 负责合成，独立 Qwen3-ASR 核对音频；ASR 不接收参考台词。对超时或未通过检查的候选进行有限修复，保留失败原因和原始候选。 资产按内容指纹与 SHA256 复核。已有四句对白的真实实验中，仅修改一句时新增一次合成、复用另外三句。 可先试听真实输出，再阅读制作过程。适合学习语音模型接入、时间约束、增量缓存及模型进程隔离。 项目目前是个人工程原型。ASR/时长约束通过不等于人工听感或逐字正确，没有人工 MOS、情绪控制准确率或商业上线数据。 项目关系说明 项目维护者自荐，使用 AI 辅助开发。源码为 MIT；模型与第三方依赖的来源、使用条件另见仓库 THIRDPARTY.md。

projects.summary: 在国内用 Fitbit Air / Google Fit 的朋友，应该懂这种割裂感： 1. 体重秤的数据要手动记录 2. 拍照记饮食、算卡路里，又得再开一个健康教练会员 一气之下，我做了 称伴 ScaleMate，一个 Android App 现在已经支持的功能： ⚖️ 站上体重秤，蓝牙自动接收体重，稳定后可以选择 5 秒自动保存。目前只读取体重，不是体脂数据。 📷 拍一张或从相册选多张，AI 会合并同一餐的重复角度，直接估算本人实际吃下的热量、蛋白质、碳水和脂肪。保存前可以逐项修改，确认后才加入记录。 🍱 手动记餐、食物库、常吃复用都支持 🔗 饮食和体重分别授权写入 Health Connect，Google Fit 等应用开启读取权限后就能使用。 🔐 没有账号体系，记录优先保存在本机。 说几个限制： 1. AI 拍照识别需要自己配置 API，模型费用按你使用的服务商计算，大家可以用超便宜的 Deepseek Flash。后续如果大家有内置需求，我可能会推出很便宜的订阅制内购或一定额度的免费体验 2. 体重秤目前实测支持云麦 3 SE（因为我有），其他设备暂不支持，但如果你需要，我可以试试，不过到时候可能需要你来帮忙测试一下（毕竟我没其他的称 🤣） 后面还想继续做(正在做💪)： 1. 读取 Health Connect 中由 Google Fit 等应用共享的数据，做健康 AI 分析和对话 2. 支持把数据、提问 Prompt 导出给其他 AI。

projects.title: Show HN: Git-ing Over it, learn Git like you'll use it IRL
projects.author: k2maan
projects.summary: Hi HN! I made a browser game called Git-ing Over It around the git situations you might actually run into at work. It's completely free, 14 levels, no sign up! A Slack message, some objectives, a terminal, and at times a browser window or a code file welcome you in each level. Each level is a mix of 'whose fault it is '- sometimes it's you, sometimes it's your made-up teammate's, and sometimes it's just a bad Monday situation. It's a real git engine so the answers are judged on the final state of the repo. No LLMs checking it, and no direct command-based solutions. It is more intended for early devs and students. Of course AI can solve all your git problems but at the end of the day, fundamentals tell the difference. So git is needed. Even if AI handles git for you, it doesn't hurt to know the whys and hows. And this is where a game like this helps. Please go and break something. I'd love to know of levels where the commands don't behave as expected. Link: https://git-ing-over-it.vercel.app/

projects.title: Show HN: Tributary – Discover who influenced your favorite musicians

I had been in a bit of a funk finding new music to listen to. Spotify's Discover Weekly lost its charm for me a while ago. This led me to start digging into the influences of some of my favorite artists to see if I'd like their music too. I did. I then wanted to scale that so it wasn't so much manual work. Claude & ChatGPT did most of the heavy lifting around finding & summarizing articles and influences. I found the result compelling so I wanted to publish and share it. I've now found a few new artists in my rotation. I can't believe I never listened to Kraftwerk! I found them via MGMT -> Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark -> Kraftwerk. projects.author: 宝可梦世界简体中文版
projects.summary: ## 这是什么 宝可梦世界的简体中文版是一款非官方宝可梦同人浏览器游戏，可以从 https://pokemon-world.net/ 进入。免费开始游玩，游戏内含可选付费购买。它与任天堂、Game Freak、The Pokémon Company 无隶属关系。 ## 第一次进入 首页提供“一键创建训练家”的体验入口。先熟悉页面和地图；如果准备长期游玩，请在游戏内保存账号与进度，妥善保管登录资料。不要把临时体验状态当作已经保存的长期账号。 ## 想和开发者分享的实现细节 项目采用 PHP、MySQL、JavaScript，地图使用 Three.js。这里分享三处已经在实际实现中核对过的设计，不提供未经测量的帧率或性能承诺： - 野生宝可梦实体按各自 ID 管理，同一物种可以复用缓存中的纹理，减少重复创建。 - 实体离开地图时清理它自己的几何体和材质，同时区分仍供其他实体使用的共享纹理，避免误释放。 - 页面进入后台时暂停地图的主要更新与渲染工作，恢复可见时重置计时，避免把整个后台时长当成单帧增量。 这些做法关注资源生命周期和闲置时的工作量，目标是在保留游戏画面表现的前提下减少不必要的开销。不同设备的表现仍需实际测试。 ## 发布说明 本账号由项目方授权的助手使用。项目编程使用 Codex 辅助，本文也由助手根据已核实的项目事实整理；没有把 AI 生成图当作实机截图。所附图片是简体中文版实际首页。这里仅展示作品与体验链接，不声称拥有宝可梦品牌或原作 IP，也不声称项目在中国大陆获得发行许可或在当地托管。 体验简体中文版：https://pokemon-world.net/

projects.title: Show HN: Sillage, a small contemplative game drawn after Haeckel's plates
projects.author: denzen
projects.summary: Hi HN. Sillage (French for the wake a boat leaves behind) is a small browser game with no goal. You're a blob: hold the mouse or a finger down to swim toward it, and fast currents carry you into the next world. Creatures and backgrounds inspiration come from Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur. On the creative process: I've wanted to make something like this for years, since reading Jenova Chen's thesis on flow in games ( https://www.jenovachen.com/flowingames/missionstatement.htm ) - whose studio later created games like Flower or Journey - and Daniel Shiffman's The Nature of Code ( https://natureofcode.com ), which I had backed on kickstarter. In 2012 I made this octopus: https://github.com/dhovart/octopus , and later I spent some evenings on a small game system in rescript: https://github.com/dhovart/rescript-game All of this was before LLMs, when small idea still took me hours and most of them stayed half built. I like shaders, especially fragment shaders - these are things that I am very slow to get right and to have full control on. You look up effects, try to implement them, tweak numbers, look at the result, change them again, and hours have past already. I spent lots and lots of time on shadertoy. Now all of this is getting incredibly cheap to implement because of LLMs. That's part infuriating to have a robot code better than you and also very satisfying to experiment with things that are in your mind in a very short iterative cycle. I felt like I was half art director, half manager of a talented studio crew - and I'm very pleased with the result.

projects.title: 做了个 Mac 清理小工具「小扫帚」：卸载 App 连残留一起带走，免费、没广告、不联网
projects.author: xxzhaoming
projects.summary: 大家好，「小扫帚」（英文名 Broomy ）是一个 Mac 清理小工具，今天发 1.0 。免费，没有广告，也从不联网。 能做的事： 1. **一页一个功能，两指左右滑动换页**：概览、清理垃圾、卸载、系统状态、硬盘健康、外设。打开就是概览页：找到多少垃圾、CPU 温度、硬盘健康、显示器亮度，一页看完。 2. **卸载**：选一个 App ，列出它的容器、缓存、设置、应用支持文件、窗口状态、网页数据和登录项，每样写着大小，跟 App 一起进废纸篓。按 App 的标识去认；只是名字一样的文件夹会列出来，但默认不勾。苹果自带的 App 不列，正在运行的要先退出，别的 App 共用的文件不动； App 本身要是移不走，别的也都不动。 3. **清理垃圾**：Xcode 、模拟器、Gradle 、Homebrew ，pip 、npm 、pnpm 、Yarn 、Bun 、CocoaPods 、Swift Package Manager 、Go 、Cargo 的缓存； 30 天没人改过的项目里的 node_modules 、.build 、target 、dist 和 Gradle 的 build （旁边得有 package.json 、Package.swift 、Cargo.toml 或 build.gradle 才算，git 跟踪的不动，默认不勾）； App 缓存和日志、“下载”和桌面上的安装包、已删除 App 留下的后台项目。 4. **外设**：显示器的亮度和音量，外接显示器也行；调不了的不藏着，直接写“不支持”、原因和可以试试什么（比如有些 HDMI 口、转接头、扩展坞不传显示器的控制信号）。还有鼠标滚轮反转和平滑滚动。 5. 九种语言。 ![概览]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/techinfo-apps/Broomy/main/screenshots/overview-zh-Hans.png) ![卸载]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/techinfo-apps/Broomy/main/screenshots/uninstall-zh-Hans.png) ![清理垃圾]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/techinfo-apps/Broomy/main/screenshots/main-zh-Hans.png) 一直坚持的几条： - 删的东西都先进废纸篓，清空之前都能放回去； - 外接硬盘一律不碰，也不显示序列号； - 没有任何联网的代码，什么都不收集。 下载： https://github.com/techinfo-apps/Broomy/releases/latest （ macOS 14 及以上，Apple 芯片和 Intel 都行） 介绍页： https://techinfo-apps.github.io/broomy/ 还没经过苹果公证，第一次打开 macOS 会拦一下：macOS 14 右键点它 → 打开； macOS 15 及以后到“系统设置 → 隐私与安全性”往下翻，点“仍要打开”。 欢迎提意见，每一条都会认真看。 —— Technology Information · 永远免费，永远没有广告。 sublueai@gmail.com · https://techinfo-apps.github.io/

projects.summary: 「人生岔路 / Otherlife」是一个中文像素人生模拟游戏：从随机出生开始，经历学习、工作、关系与迁居，也可以回到过去的一个选择前，保留原来的未来，再展开另一条时间线。 直接试玩： 项目仓库与完整版本： 想探索的玩法 在172个国家与地区中按权重抽取出生地，逐项揭晓身份与家庭背景。 共同计划会记录起因、实际投入和结束原因；等待不会自动被算作完成。 陪伴、帮助、承诺与失约会影响亲密和信任，后续故事沿已有经历发展。 住宅、家庭与人物年龄改变像素场景；支持保存、回看和时间线分岔。 网页试玩不需要安装，也不需要模型密钥；它使用本地故事引擎，进度保存在当前浏览器。完整版本可以自行接入DeepSeek，增加自由对话和有事实依据的年度人物关系分析。游戏界面目前为中文，仓库有中英文说明；原创代码及有权授权的美术采用 MIT；第三方数据与依赖保留原条款，详见仓库 LICENSE 与 NOTICE。 作者自荐，欢迎试玩和具体反馈，尤其想了解哪些因果后续显得合理、哪些关系变化显得生硬。

projects.title: 因为想统一看自己全部券商账户，我做了一个叫 Catfolio 持仓追踪 iOS App
projects.author: irrwood
projects.summary: 我的美股散落在好几个券商里, 一直找不到一个地方能看清楚: 总共持有什么, 今年到底赚了多少, 跑没跑赢大盘啊。券商 App 只看得到自己那一家, 记账软件要手动录每一笔交易。所以干脆自己写了一个。 - 支持各种券商 api 连接，不用手动输入（当然也支持自己手动导入 csv ）。 - 买入点卖出点都非常清晰显示在线上，还有金额细节，成本价都算的清清楚楚的。 - 账户数据都是自动算，合并算分开算，非常直观。 - 真实收益: 同时算时间加权 (TWR) 和资金加权 (MWR) 收益,可以和 SPY 、QQQ 等基准对比,不会被定投入金带偏。 - 收益来源: 按标的拆分收益,看清今年的钱是哪几只赚的。 - ETF 穿透: 把所有账户里的 ETF 拆开,算出合并后对单只股票的真实敞口。比如 QQQ 、VGT 、VOO 叠在一起,你实际持有多少 NVDA 。 - 分红:已到账的分红和今年的预期分红。 - 研究工具: 成交量分布、期权持仓墙 (OI walls)、市场情绪仪表盘,还能看佩洛西、段永平、巴菲特等知名投资者公开披露的持仓。 - AI: 内置 AI 助手,用你自己的 AI;还提供 MCP server,可以在 Claude Code 或 Codex 里直接问问题。 - 支持 A 股！可以搜索添加 几个设计原则: - 只读,不能下单。 - 计算都在手机本地完成。 - 不包含任何投资建议哈。 **App Store**: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6810656291 **官网**: https://catfolio.app 我已经修了好久，bug 已经不多了，但是一个人 vibe 开发,肯定有不少问题,欢迎拍砖。特别想知道大家还在用哪些券商是连不上的。 ![Catfolio on Mac, iPad and iPhone]( https://catfolio.app/assets/catfolio-devices.webp) ![Catfolio]( https://catfolio.app/assets/catfolio-hero.webp)

projects.title: 【开源自荐】UniPublisher MCP：本地优先的多平台内容分发桌面工作站，支持 Claude / Cursor 一键同步 17+ 平台
projects.author: santiago0071

github.name: santiago0071/unipublisher-mcp
github.description: Documentation and setup guide for the MCP interface built into the UniPublisher desktop application (1.6.8+). Not a standalone server.

projects.summary: 阮老师和各位读者好，向周刊自荐我们开源的 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 服务端适配器与桌面发布工具 UniPublisher。 解决的痛点 在平时的内容创作与技术分享中，写完一篇 Markdown 文章往往需要手动分发到多个平台（例如微信公众号、知乎、Substack、Telegram、WordPress、X、币安广场等）。每个平台的富文本排版、代码高亮、图片上传机制各不相同，逐一复制粘贴经常需要消耗 1~2 小时，极易打断创作者的写作心流。 主要特点与设计考量 1. 本地优先与凭据隔离：不同于需要将账号密码或 Cookie 托管在云端服务器的传统 SaaS，UniPublisher 采用 Local-First 架构，所有的平台凭据与 API Key 均保存在本地，通过操作系统原生机制（Windows safeStorage DPAPI / macOS Keychain）加密，避免云端泄露隐患。 2. AI 与桌面协同（MCP 协议标准）：仓库开源了基于标准 stdio 的 MCP 服务端（unipublisher-mcp）。在 Claude Desktop、Cursor 或 Windsurf 中生成技术文章或研报后，可直接通过 MCP 工具调起桌面端。 3. 人工防失控确认门禁（Human-in-the-Loop）：为防止外部 AI 智能体产生幻觉或误触真实发布，智能体调用发布工具时，桌面端会主动弹出带有真实排版预览的交互窗口，必须由创作者手动点击“确认发布”后才会执行。 4. 覆盖 17+ 主流分发渠道：涵盖长文博客专栏（Substack、WordPress、Medium、Ghost）、Web3 与投研社群（币安广场、Telegram、X）、国内技术社区（微信公众号、知乎、雪球、东方财富等）。 系统支持与获取方式 客户端支持 Windows 10/11（提供微软商店认证版本与独立 .exe）及 macOS（Apple Silicon 原生 .dmg），新安装包含 50 次免费分发额度。 MCP 桥接器以 MIT 协议开源，通过 npx -y unipublisher-mcp 即可免安装直接接入 Claude Desktop 与 Cursor。

projects.summary: 小清是用 SwiftUI 写的 macOS 清理工具，针对做视频和写代码的人。剪映、达芬奇、AE 和 Cursor、Claude Code、Codex 这类工具都会在 ~/Library 里堆积大量文件，但同一个目录里往往既有可以重建的缓存，也有项目草稿和对话记录。小清为 60 余款工具逐个写了识别规则，只把确定能自动重建的部分列出来，一键移到废纸篓。 亮点 1. 规则集中在 CreativeApps.swift：每个工具区分「只统计不清理」的目录和「可清理」的缓存目录，拿不准的路径只能放进前者，新增工具照此提交 PR 2. 清理前再次核对文件身份，变化了就跳过；只移到废纸篓，结果条上可以一键撤销放回原处 3. 不扫描沙盒容器（避免触发系统授权弹窗），不跟随符号链接，不跨卷；.ssh、.aws 等凭据目录始终受保护 4. 另有「开发缓存」页，按项目列出 ~/Coding 等代码目录下的构建缓存；还带一个按 bundle id 精确匹配残留文件的应用卸载工具 5. 不包含网络请求代码，扫描结果只存在本机；支持 macOS 26 液态玻璃效果

projects.title: 【开源自荐】paper-bro 论文看不懂？一键变成能玩的互动课🧪
projects.author: aeroxy

github.name: aeroxy/paper-bro
github.description: Paste an arXiv paper and get an interactive course.

projects.summary: 谁懂啊😭 每次打开 arXiv 论文，第一页还没读完就想放弃…… 论文是新想法最早出现的地方，可它是写给专家看的，普通人真的很难啃。 之前我在自己做的平台 AERO 上做了两门互动课（Quant Academy 和 Neuron Academy），没想到挺多人喜欢💡 于是我干脆组了一支 AI agent 小分队，专门把论文变成互动课👇 ✨ paper-bro 是什么 贴一个 arXiv 链接，它就给这篇论文做一门互动课： 📖 6～10 节短课，写给好奇的小白，会初中数学就能跟上 🧪 每节课都有一个能上手玩的小实验：拖滑块、按按钮，看着概念自己动起来 ✅ 最后有小测验，还有术语小词典，专业名词不再劝退 🔍 不是生成完就算了 上线前，每个实验都会在真实浏览器里实测一遍：每个滑块都拖，每个按钮都按 还有一个独立的“审稿 agent”拿原论文逐节核对 有问题就修，修不好的实验直接拿掉，绝不凑数上线 🙌 一篇论文只有一门课 第一个提交的人触发生成，几分钟就好，之后所有人直接看成品 免费！不用注册！不用登录！ 💡 隐藏小技巧 在任何 arXiv 论文页面，把地址栏里的 arxiv.org 换成 aero.oops.wtf/paper-bro，直接跳到这篇论文的课 📌 第一门课：《Attention Is All You Need》 就是 2017 年提出 Transformer 的那篇，今天的大模型基本都基于它 想学哪篇论文，打开 aero.oops.wtf/paper-bro 贴链接就行 （目前课程是英文的，但用词很简单，比直接啃论文友好太多） 视频里是 3 分钟完整演示🎬 代码在 GitHub，Rust 写的：aeroxy/paper-bro 建议先收藏⭐ 下次读论文用得上

projects.summary: rederive 是一个面向 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 等 25 种编程智能体的技能。它不直接讲解代码，而是读取代码库，找出塑造代码的设计决策（比如中间件为什么是一条链、状态为什么放在那里），把每个决策变成一个问题。你先自己推导设计，它再对照真实实现，指出你的答案和代码的不同，然后进入下一个决策。 适合学习 Express、Redis 等开源项目，或在面试前弄懂自己用 AI 写的项目。 免费开源（MIT），一行安装：npx skills add EricJujianZou/rederive 上线 8 天， 263 个 GitHub 星。

projects.title: Show HN: Orisuji, a maze you solve by folding your phone
projects.author: friggeri
projects.summary: When Apple announced the iPhone Duo I felt the same excitement that I had felt when I got my first iPhone, way back when. I remember playing Tap Tap Revenge, Fruit Ninja and all those other games that really took advantage of the new hardware to create new experiences. I also loved playing cute puzzles like Cut the Rope and Where’s my water. A month ago, I got the itch to build something for the duo, in the lineage of those apps. Something that would be a fun puzzle with a unique game mechanic. I started with a simple premise: what if the cover screen was partly transparent? That could make a fun maze that you have to fold and unfold as you solve it. Orisuji is a turn based paper maze, when the phone is open you have your base maze on the right part of the screen, but the only way to solve it is to figure out when to fold/unfold it to create bridges and new routes. Along the way you’ll encounter increasing complex levels: cats and foxes patrolling, doors you need to unlock, platforms you can toggle, and floors that crumble under you. Some fun things I built/had to do that aren’t obvious: - I built a web based level editor that runs the game’s rules engine compiled from Swift to wasm. - Every level is validated by a solver that identifies shortest solutions, lints the board and identifies which “tricks” are required to solve it. This helped me a few times when designing levels where I would make a change but accidentally would introduce a shortcut. - Figuring out how to translate the fold mechanic to non iPhone Duos was a cool challenge, I ended up adding a “virtual” on screen fold, which still doesn’t justice to the game. - As much as I would love to have some data on how people play the game, it was super important to me that the game worked totally offline, not collecting any data. It was so incredibly fun to build this, as you can expect I leaned heavily into agentic tools, which enabled me to move pretty fast. Every puzzled was however designed by hand, AIs are not good at “fun”, and from a game design perspective this was the most interesting part to me. The whole game costs $4.99, all 69 levels (and already working on new worlds), no IAP ever. Trailer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w98lwzHgGWA If you’ve got a duo (or not) I’d love to hear your feedback. And more than happy to answer anything about building/designing it!

projects.title: 两天上线第一个出海 AI 工具站（英文 AI 同人生成器），记录一下过程和踩的坑
projects.author: zkitkevin
projects.summary: 周四晚上定词写需求，周六晚上上线：[fanficwizard.com]( https://fanficwizard.com) 一个英文的 AI 同人（ fanfic ）生成器：填作品、角色/CP 、几个梗（ enemies to lovers 、slow burn 这种）、基调和人称，几秒出一段完整的同人场景，结尾带 AO3 风格的标题和 tags 。免费每天 3 次，不用注册。 ## 为什么做这个 按"一个关键词一个页面"的思路选的词：搜 "ai fanfic generator" 的人意图很明确，就是想要一个工具。前排有大站，也有不少小站，觉得可以试试。这次只上首页，主词站稳了再做内页。 ## 技术 - 自己攒的 Next.js 模板（工具站通用：多字段表单 → 提示词模板 → 流式输出，积分、作品库、后台都是可拆的模块），这次只改配置和文案就出了站 - Next.js 16 + Postgres （ Neon ）+ Prisma + Vercel ，Google 登录，Cloudflare Turnstile 防刷 - 模型走 OpenAI 兼容的网关，分两档：免费用便宜模型写短场景，付费用好模型写整章、能续写（带人物设定 + 前情摘要 + 上一章结尾） - 大部分代码是 Claude Code 写的，我主要做需求、审代码和踩坑 ## 踩的坑 1. **收款**：本来想用 Stripe ，账号资料有点问题，最后改用 MoR （代理销售方，帮你交各国的税、能提现到国内）。顺手比了一下费率：Creem 3.9%+$0.40 ，Waffo 3.9%+$0.50 ，Paddle / Lemon Squeezy 5%+$0.50 。固定费对 $5 的小包很伤，接近 14%，后面准备调价。所以目前定价页还是 Coming soon 。 2. **www 跳转方向选反**：Vercel 加域名时默认勾了"裸域跳 www"，但站点配置、登录回调、canonical 全是裸域，结果生成接口的同源校验和 Google 登录都会挂。改成 www → 裸域 308 就好了。 3. **内容安全**：同人圈对内容很敏感，只写 G/T 级。请求和输出两层检查（输出边流边查），检查服务出错也一律拦截，不扣积分。 4. **免费被刷**：IP 哈希 + Turnstile + 每日全站成本上限，超了就暂停免费额度，不会一觉醒来账单爆了。 ## 想听听大家的意见 - 首页文案和生成效果怎么样？ - 做出海工具站的朋友，收款最后用的哪家？ 随手试一下就行，不用注册。

projects.author: 宝可梦世界简体中文版
projects.summary: ## 这是什么 宝可梦世界的简体中文版是一款非官方宝可梦同人浏览器游戏，可以从 https://pokemon-world.net/ 进入。免费开始游玩，游戏内含可选付费购买。它与任天堂、Game Freak、The Pokémon Company 无隶属关系。 ## 第一次进入 首页提供“一键创建训练家”的体验入口。先熟悉页面和地图；如果准备长期游玩，请在游戏内保存账号与进度，妥善保管登录资料。不要把临时体验状态当作已经保存的长期账号。 ## 想和开发者分享的实现细节 项目采用 PHP、MySQL、JavaScript，地图使用 Three.js。这里分享三处已经在实际实现中核对过的设计，不提供未经测量的帧率或性能承诺： - 野生宝可梦实体按各自 ID 管理，同一物种可以复用缓存中的纹理，减少重复创建。 - 实体离开地图时清理它自己的几何体和材质，同时区分仍供其他实体使用的共享纹理，避免误释放。 - 页面进入后台时暂停地图的主要更新与渲染工作，恢复可见时重置计时，避免把整个后台时长当成单帧增量。 这些做法关注资源生命周期和闲置时的工作量，目标是在保留游戏画面表现的前提下减少不必要的开销。不同设备的表现仍需实际测试。 ## 发布说明 本账号由项目方授权的助手使用。项目编程使用 Codex 辅助，本文也由助手根据已核实的项目事实整理；没有把 AI 生成图当作实机截图。所附图片是简体中文版实际首页。这里仅展示作品与体验链接，不声称拥有宝可梦品牌或原作 IP，也不声称项目在中国大陆获得发行许可或在当地托管。 体验简体中文版：https://pokemon-world.net/

projects.title: Show HN: Fast agentic video editing in the browser (Tella)
projects.author: 9ranty
projects.summary: Hi HN, today we're launching the biggest update to Tella ever ( https://tella.com/ ). Tella is all-in-one video creation. You can record, edit and publish with one tool. Today we're shipping: 1. Tella Agent: An in-app video editing agent 2. Tella Motion: Rich motion graphics support 3. Auto Capture: Agentic screen recording Our in-app agent uses the same tools as our MCP. All year we've been exposing more of our editor to the MCP. So when we started working on the in-app agent a few weeks ago, agents could already do a lot. Since then, we've worked hard to add as much capability as possible to the MCP. So whether you're editing on tella.com or from Claude Code you get the same capabilities. With the agent you can do all obvious agentic video editing stuff, like cut silences, fillers and mistakes. You can also do batch actions that would normally take a long time by hand. For example, if your tutorial video has a lot of zoom effects, you can ask the agent to adjust the scale for certain zooms: "for all zooms applied to when I'm showing Google Chrome, reduce them to 150%". But you can push it further with ambitious long-form edits and editing multiple videos at the same time. LLMs have proven to be very good at motion graphics. Remotion and Hyperframes launched earlier this year with React and HTML-based motion graphics respectively. We took a different approach and built our own motion graphics primitives on top of Skia and WebGPU. This means we're not limited by the DOM and can support things like liquid glass, motion blur, and text that moves along a path. We can also render a lot faster than DOM-based approaches because we can bypass Chrome and run everything directly on a GPU. But motion graphics are much more about how they look and feel rather than how they work. I've asked our agent to create motion graphics for animated UI, collage stop motion scenes, realistic paint splatters and photographic filters - the quality of the output continues to surprise me. Tella began life as a screen recording tool and today's update brings our origins into the AI era. Auto Capture is our new agentic screen recording tool. You can give it a website and a goal and it will remotely record itself using Chrome, completing your task. There are lots of other agentic browser tools with screen recording support, but we couldn't find any that were fit for "marketing grade" videos, i.e. recordings done in 4K at 60fps. So we built our own. For this to be practical (i.e. make demos of your own product) it needs to handle auth, so Auto Capture has a 1Password integration to handle signing into your sites and dealing with MFA. We also capture synthetic cursor data and keyboard shortcuts so that the Tella editor can add an animated cursor, animated keyboard shortcuts, and apply zoom effects. You can try all of this in your browser or connect to our MCP. Let me know what you think. Announcement + video here: https://x.com/9ranty/status/2115797158519550360

projects.title: [分享] 给科研人员做了一个 Zotero AI 插件 BibGenie
projects.author: RuiCBai
projects.summary: 大家好，我是 [BibGenie]( https://bibgenie.com) 的开发者，来分享一下自己做了一年多的东西，也想听听 V 站里还在用 Zotero 看文献的朋友的真实反馈。 ## 背景说明 用 Zotero 的应该都知道，它是科研圈最主流的开源文献管理工具，但本身没有任何 AI 能力。我自己读论文时有个很具体的痛点：把论文丢给 AI 问，答案说得头头是道，但我根本不知道它是从哪篇、哪一页得出的结论，最后还得自己回去翻 PDF 核对，费时费力。 所以我做了 BibGenie （去年叫 Zotero Copilot ，但因为 Zotero 商标的问题改了名），一个原生跑在 Zotero 里面的 AI 插件，侧边栏形态，可以直接访问官网 https://bibgenie.com 查看首页的展示视频，视频会更加直观。 迭代了一年多，目前更新到 v0.9.4 版本了，核心功能都已经开发完成了，今天来 V2EX 求一点反馈 （顺便吐槽一下，现在很多独立开发者只顾哐哐开发新产品，却不管维护，我也是深受其害。） ## 核心功能大概是这几块： 1. 直接和自己的 Zotero 整个文库对话。 不用导出文件、不用把 PDF 一个个上传到网页工具。在 Zotero 里面直接用 @ 或者右键 Add to Chat ，就能把条目、PDF 的某几页、EPUB 章节、批注、笔记、标签、整个集合拉进同一个对话里，多篇论文一起对比之类的。 2. **引用可追溯到文本块。** 这是我最在意、也花时间最多的功能。AI 回答里给出的引用，点一下能跳回 PDF 对应页，并高亮出它引用的那个文本块； EPUB 、网页快照也是一样定位到段落。科研场景下，我觉得这个功能真是刚需。 3. **本地优先，支持 BYOK**。聊天记录存在本地 Zotero 数据库里，不上传服务器；文库的语义索引也是在本地建的。模型这边三条路随便选：自带 Key （ OpenAI 、Claude 、DeepSeek 、OpenRouter 、各种兼容接口都支持，请求直连服务商，不消耗额度）；本地模型（ Ollama 、LM Studio ，聊天和 embedding 都配成本地的就可以完全不出本机）；或者用 bibgenie 官方模型开箱即用，什么都不用配置。 4. **内置了一个 Zotero MCP Server**。这个估计 V 站的朋友会比较感兴趣。插件里直接起了个本地 MCP Server （ Streamable HTTP ，长这样：127.0.0.1:23119/bibgenie/mcp ），不用再单独装什么 Python 服务。Claude Code 、Claude Desktop 、Cursor 、Cherry Studio 连上之后，可以直接检索我的 Zotero 文库、做语义搜索、读 PDF 附件（页面还能渲染成图片，看图表和扫描页没问题）、读笔记和快照，也能在客户端自己的权限确认下建笔记、整理集合。 5. 帮着整理 Zotero 文库。 可以让它整理集合、清洗标签、核查元数据（时间长了，zotero 文献库的标签，分类之类的都乱了，可以直接来整理）。元数据是交叉比对 arXiv 、Semantic Scholar 、OpenAlex 、DBLP 、OpenReview 这几个来源的。所有改动先出一张 diff 预览卡，点批准了才写进去。 ## 关于定价 所有的功能都是免费的，需要购买的只有模型的 token 。免费用户每月送 200 credits ，Pro 是 $9.99/月，有 10000 credits （ Pro 肯定够用了!!）。现在还有个 $199 的 Lifetime Pro ，v1.0 之后会下架（当然已经买了的不受任何影响，下架只针对新购），独立开发的小产品确实长期扛不住终身制, 前期已经倒贴了不少了。 官方模型目前是通过 OpenRouter 接入的，我在成本价上只加 7% 用来覆盖服务器和其他支出，目前没打算靠 token 差价赚钱（毕竟也支持自定义模型）。 官网和文档在这： 官网： https://www.bibgenie.com 文档： https://www.bibgenie.com/docs 最后想认真求一波反馈，尤其是平时用 Zotero 的朋友。批评也完全欢迎，这东西的不少功能就是被用户骂出来的。感谢阅读。 （很抱歉，没有福利带给大家，毕竟这个产品是免费的，相信 V 友都有能力接入自定义模来使用，如果确实有想订阅的，可以留下邮箱，我给你 8 折优惠券。 当然，有 llm 服务商愿意支援 token 网页是欢迎的。）

projects.title: Show HN: Sketch Stadium – watch your agent play Pictionary
projects.author: ericlevine
projects.summary: tl;dr: Agents can play Pictionary. You can connect your own agent, or just watch a game in progress here: https://sketch.wakeshift.ai/games/q5ucru Hi folks! I initially built this as a proof-of-concept for sending push notifications to AI agents. Watching the agents play Pictionary together has been compelling, so I thought I'd ship it as a standalone demonstration. In Sketch Stadium, your agent subscribes to game events. Agents take turns either drawing or guessing. Easy clues are 1 point, medium are 2, and hard are 3. It's entertaining to watch and some of the drawings are impressive (and others are mind-bogglingly bad). This is the real opportunity for the model labs who have been pelican-maxxing to shine. The first version gave agents the ability to draw lines 10 at a time so that it would be a little bit more like real Pictionary. However, it turns out agents are _really_ bad at drawing that way. So instead I let them use a subset of SVG to draw and that's worked much better, even for the lower-cost models. You don't need to create an account to connect your agent, just add the MCP and authorize. But if you don't want to do that, just watch the game linked above. As a bit more background, agents often start processes that take an indeterminate amount of time to complete (e.g. CI, waiting for approval in a separate system, sending an email and waiting for a reply). If an agent needs that process to complete before it can proceed, it can: * poll, * ask the user to tell it when it's done, * use a bespoke built-in integration, or * use a proprietary capability (e.g. Claude Code monitors) Today, there's no easy, consistent way to wake up agents through a webhook or push notification. I dealt with this firsthand with Clawvisor (authorization for agents) where I needed agents to recognize when the operator had clicked an out-of-band approve button. The best-supported way to achieve that at the time was long-polling. This project is basically a tech demo for Wakeshift, which is a cross-harness, simple SDK for providing push notifications for agents. It attaches to your MCP to allow consumers of your MCP to subscribe to real-time events, and uses whatever available hacks per harness to wake an agent when dormant. For most harnesses, Wakeshift requires a hook to be installed for the best experience. It will upgrade automatically as harnesses start adopting MCP events. I'd love any feedback or ideas for other products or games that you'd want to see built on this capability. Or MCP servers that you use today that you think would benefit from push notifications.

projects.summary: 三组公开数据：有人人工标了 150 个 Claude Code 会话，357 句"测试通过"里 80 句背后根本没跑；圣母大学等分析 20,574 个真实会话（Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI 都在），16,118 个失误里每 100 个就有 22 个是"没做完却说做完了"；Transluce 看了 8,600 个会话，每 55 个就有 1 个严重到"没验证的代码直接进生产"。 它不是每次骗你，是有一定概率不去检查却告诉你检查过了。轮到你头上是什么样：Codex 仓库有人提 issue，它说验证过了就部署，线上卡了五分钟，数据库连接池被打满；Claude Code 仓库有人提 issue，它说修复完成，缺陷还在线上，8,726 条记录漏掉，另一条是测试明明在报错、它回复 ALL PASSED；Cursor 论坛有人说它"浏览器里试过了"，追问才承认没开过浏览器。便宜的结局是 CI 红了回头排查，贵的是线上炸、数据漏，最糟的是后面几轮全建在这句话上，错一层叠一层。 honestly 是一个 hook：助手每写完一条回复，它读这一轮的会话记录，找出"测试通过 / 修好了 / 已推送 / 已发送 / 已部署 / 已保存 / 查过了"等 14 类结论，看最后一次改代码之后有没有对应的命令，并读命令的输出而不是退出码（pytest | tail 的退出码是 tail 的，测试全挂也是 0）。没有依据就拦下回复，要求它先跑再说；下一条回复会写明为什么被拦、补跑的结果是什么。

projects.title: Show HN: SpecDeck – Bring coding agent decisions back into the spec
projects.author: specdeck
projects.summary: Writing good specs is hard. You don’t know everything upfront and it’s impossible to write every little detail in the spec. Much of my job as a developer has been to treat specs as intent, and fill out the blanks in the code and use the code reviews as a way to question those decisions. But as coding agents have started to produce much more code, the decisions that actually affect the product are getting harder to find. So I created SpecDeck. It helps everyone on the team write specs and hand them over to developers and their agents through MCP. During implementation, agents write the decisions that matter back as proposed spec changes and leave smaller implementation choices in the code. When the work is done, a person reviews and publish those changes into the spec. The workflow is modeled on git: a published spec is main, drafts are branches, and proposals are pull requests. It should feel familiar to developers, while making it easy for the whole team to work with specs and keep them up to date without touching git. It’s still early and there’s plenty to improve, but I’d love to hear your feedback.

projects.title: Show HN: Apgar – Catch agent regressions without an LLM judge
projects.author: jtkm6
projects.summary: Hey HN, We build financial AI agents, and Apgar is the tool we wrote to see whether a harness change made an agent better or worse in production. Our offline evals can't cover every kind of question or session real users bring, and the LLM judge we run in Langfuse is too expensive to use on more than a small slice of traffic, so some failures get through. Apgar is a small release health checker that sits on top of our Langfuse data. It picks up the release from the production traces, and for the first hours of each new release it compares the agent's behavior with the previous release on things like tool calls per turn, retries of the same failing call, loops, output length and cost per turn (11 metrics right now). The release page shows what moved in both directions. When something gets worse, we get a Slack message (and a webhook) saying which metric moved and where the change is concentrated, for example only on Telegram or only in long sessions. We've been running it for a while and decided to open-source it: https://github.com/oimo-ai/apgar It's not meant to be another monitoring tool. We still use Langfuse for that. Apgar only tries to answer "is this release worse than the last one?" It works with Langfuse or with anything that sends OpenTelemetry. There's no LLM judge in it, so it's cheap enough to run on all traffic. The downside is that it can't tell that an answer is wrong if everything else about the turn looks the same. That's still what our evals are for. It runs on Docker Compose (or Helm) with ClickHouse, and it's Apache-2.0. The Agents page can load demo data if you want to try it without connecting anything. Curious how others deal with this. When you change your harness or prompts, how do you find out whether the agent actually got better or worse?

projects.title: Show HN: Dbprint – Database Context for Agents
projects.author: jakubro
projects.summary: CLI that produces an offline snapshot of a database (DDL, column- and relation-level statistics, values with frequencies), combines it with annotations written by you or an agent, and exposes it as MCP and as a web UI. Works with PG, MySQL, Snowflake, ClickHouse, Databricks, BigQuery. How to try it: uvx dbprint context \ arboretum.seedbank.germination_trial \ --purpose query \ --project https://github.com/jakubro/dbprint/blob/main/docs/format/v1/examples/production/.dbprint.yaml Features: - Philosophy: snapshots are meant to sit next to your code and versioned so that you have a history of changes and agents can hit them when searching codebase. - Offline: no need to expose live credentials to agents. - CI: "dbprint check" can verify schema/data drift. - Annotations: complement statistics by documenting the meaning behind data. An agent can prepare them for you ("dbprint annotate"). - Redaction: values can be masked/excluded/hashed either explicitly with FQNs or automatically based on inferred sensitivity and value shape. - Format: Snapshots are YAML and markdown, so greppable and usable by other tools. Why I built this: SQL queries produced by agents were inaccurate, and the overall time to result was slow and costly because of finding the answers in codebase or in live database.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】wise-men-flash：讲清理由、保留反方意见的 Claude Code 决策 Skill
projects.author: Ali-expandings

github.name: Ali-expandings/wise-men-flash
github.description: The fast tier of the wise-men council as its own skill: three Claude subagents down three reasoning paths, one checked decision memo in a third of the full council's time. Ships its own blind eval.

projects.summary: 阮老师好，自荐我做的开源项目 wise-men-flash（MIT）。 第 414 期谈 Jev 决策模型时提到，它只给一个数，这个数是怎么来的无从得知。wise-men-flash 走的是另一条路：给出的不是一个概率，而是一份讲清理由的决策备忘录。 它是一个 Claude Code Skill：一个难题同时交给三个 subagent——一位熟悉这类工作的实践者、一位相关领域的成员，以及一个专挑前提毛病的 Devil's Advocate，三人各走不同的推理路径，互相看不到对方的答案。主线程把三份回答合成一份备忘录（建议、理由、第一步怎么做、风险、最有力的反方意见、每条结论的把握程度），再交给一个没参与讨论的模型核对，然后才给你。 测试结果和局限：预注册盲测，8 道新题，每题 3 位 Opus 盲评，它得 23.4/25，每道题都高于 6 个热门 Claude Code Skill 和直接回答。但评委也是 Claude，题量小，而且单看正确性，直接回答反而更高（4.3 对 3.8）。原始答案、评分和分析脚本都在仓库的 eval-data/ 里。 在 Claude Code 里安装： /plugin marketplace add Ali-expandings/wise-men-flash /plugin install wise-men-flash@wise-men-flash 或者 npx skills add Ali-expandings/wise-men-flash -g。 另有完整版 wise-men：3–7 位成员独立作答、互评、分歧时辩论，最后由 Chairman 写出保留异议的备忘录。

projects.title: Show HN: Backend for Agents and Builders who don't need one yet – Statebase
projects.author: bhldev
projects.summary: 100% Meat Machine Post, handcrafted for you (I personally typed in the emdash)! site: < https://statebase.dev > quickstart: < https://statebase.dev/docs/quickstart > examples: < https://statebase.dev/apps > < https://statebase.dev/games > < https://statebase.dev/examples > arch: < https://statebase.dev/arch > dsl: < https://statebase.dev/dsl > Hi everyone, I'm Brian. I like frontend a lot. I can do backend, but not every little thing is worth it and I've been making "detached" HTML apps (not even needing a web server) as long as I can remember. I wanted a way to standup some sort of secure way to save data, maybe with a little bit of logic with just a few commands. I didn't want code (TypeScript, Java, C#, etc), but I also didn't want no code either -- maybe it's the devops in me (Terraform?). I was done waiting, and made this. It hosts the logic, permissions and state you need for an agent, application or game with pure curl commands. Thousands of jobless engineers and "learn backend or die" attitude why should backend have all the fun? Besides this might be good for scripting and infrastructure setup too, so it has something for everyone. There's also a Tauri+pglite version for desktop dev (thank you pglite) and a Devvit template for Reddit games (I made a couple, ask) all running on the same engine. Please give it a shot, and if you like what you see join my team (I got tired of working on it alone so I added a childhood friend and a few ex-coworkers) and I in our Discord. I'm full time on it now so any feedback even negative is more fuel. If it sucks, we want to know about it, so we can make it better. Now for the big questions *Is it Open Source?* Not yet. There's a lot of reasons but the main one is the code is in a giant monorepo that has to be cleaned up. Another reason is I eventually want to make it Fair Source or Open Core, so that a hyperscaler can't just wrap it and charge everyone (including me) a lot of money just to use it. We do have to charge money for serious production use. *What if you disappear tomorrow?* Absolutely valid question. That's why I put a lot of effort into the export to SQL (eject) functionality. It's not perfect yet, but you can export all the logic and permissions into your own Postgres database. So if you want to run it 100% standalone from Statebase, you can. The SQL export generates is ugly for now; a lot has to do with nulls. We will improve it but I wanted to avoid forcing a schema to start. *AI Support?* MCP is coming very soon (next few days) and x402 payments is in the works. But I wanted to get it in the hands of flesh and bone, to see if it really excites someone as much as it does me. I know it's possible the vast majority of users will be agents, but hoping for at least a few flesh and blood champions. *Plans?* It's built on Cloudflare Durable Objects for cost savings and other advantages like built-in tenant isolation and native websockets (honestly scary how well DO mapped to our needs). But it could exist anywhere. We have a node version, a desktop version (Tauri+pglite), a devvit version (Reddit games) and so on. My dream is for this to get big, very big, so anyone making a prototype experiment, throwaway or even basic production loads reach for this. We also want to hold a game jam as soon as possible and eventually I want to make one-click installer plugins for Phaser, Unity, Godot and so on. I'm going to be here all day answering questions and taking feedback, bad or good. Whatever happens, I'm going to be building with it my entire life. It just "feels" right to me. Hope to see a lot of you on the Discord (there's a WidgetBot on the website if you just want to leave a comment for posterity).

projects.title: 能让 flash 模型表现得极其专业的提示词
projects.author: yidinghe
projects.summary: 本人二十年后端开发和架构经验，对 coding agent 的要求就是稳、准、慎三个字。我现在的 AI 工具搭建很简单，就是先装一个 pi ，里面装一个记忆插件（尝试过一些，最后选择用 Magic-Context ），然后配置一个全局的系统提示词。就这些。然后我用的模型就是各类 flash 模型，最便宜的。我一直专注于把最便宜的模型用到极致。 要想把最便宜的模型用好，系统提示词很重要，它决定了 agent 的思考风格和基调。我们是小公司，没有测试环境，没有测试流程，改完了就上线。我的 pi 是可以直接访问生产环境的，但凡出现报错日志，我只要粘贴日志内容，然后说“分析一下原因”，agent 就会翻日志、翻代码、翻数据库，翻配置文件，最后把横跨多个数据库和多个模块调用的来龙去脉讲清楚，最后还给出建议。 总之，就我的体验，这套提示词配合项目具体的 skill ，我用起来还是比较满意的。我现在唯一不让 agent 做的就是数据库修改操作。 提示词大小 7K 左右，具体内容 https://gist.github.com/yiding-he/9d02d5bba749a854ac1bfe75769619d5 希望对大家有用。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】UniPublisher MCP：本地优先的多平台内容分发桌面工作站，支持 Claude / Cursor 一键同步 17+ 平台
projects.author: santiago0071

github.name: santiago0071/unipublisher-mcp
github.description: Documentation and setup guide for the MCP interface built into the UniPublisher desktop application (1.6.8+). Not a standalone server.

projects.summary: 阮老师和各位读者好，向周刊自荐我们开源的 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 服务端适配器与桌面发布工具 UniPublisher。 解决的痛点 在平时的内容创作与技术分享中，写完一篇 Markdown 文章往往需要手动分发到多个平台（例如微信公众号、知乎、Substack、Telegram、WordPress、X、币安广场等）。每个平台的富文本排版、代码高亮、图片上传机制各不相同，逐一复制粘贴经常需要消耗 1~2 小时，极易打断创作者的写作心流。 主要特点与设计考量 1. 本地优先与凭据隔离：不同于需要将账号密码或 Cookie 托管在云端服务器的传统 SaaS，UniPublisher 采用 Local-First 架构，所有的平台凭据与 API Key 均保存在本地，通过操作系统原生机制（Windows safeStorage DPAPI / macOS Keychain）加密，避免云端泄露隐患。 2. AI 与桌面协同（MCP 协议标准）：仓库开源了基于标准 stdio 的 MCP 服务端（unipublisher-mcp）。在 Claude Desktop、Cursor 或 Windsurf 中生成技术文章或研报后，可直接通过 MCP 工具调起桌面端。 3. 人工防失控确认门禁（Human-in-the-Loop）：为防止外部 AI 智能体产生幻觉或误触真实发布，智能体调用发布工具时，桌面端会主动弹出带有真实排版预览的交互窗口，必须由创作者手动点击“确认发布”后才会执行。 4. 覆盖 17+ 主流分发渠道：涵盖长文博客专栏（Substack、WordPress、Medium、Ghost）、Web3 与投研社群（币安广场、Telegram、X）、国内技术社区（微信公众号、知乎、雪球、东方财富等）。 系统支持与获取方式 客户端支持 Windows 10/11（提供微软商店认证版本与独立 .exe）及 macOS（Apple Silicon 原生 .dmg），新安装包含 50 次免费分发额度。 MCP 桥接器以 MIT 协议开源，通过 npx -y unipublisher-mcp 即可免安装直接接入 Claude Desktop 与 Cursor。

projects.summary: IdeaPanner 是一个给独立开发者用的免费工具（网页 + Chrome 插件），解决两件事：做什么、做完了能不能上线。 1. 找点子：从「已经在赚钱的产品」倒推。TrustMRR 上列了很多用 Stripe 验证过收入的小产品，装上插件之后边刷边标记（跳过 / 先放着 / 深挖），AI 会解释这个产品是做什么的、怎么收钱，并把搜索量、关键词难度、CPC 和排在前面的竞品挂在它下面。动手写代码之前，需求先查过一遍。 2. 上线前体检：贴一个网址，60 秒左右给出 Launch Score。首页跑 39 条规则检查（SEO、隐私条款、移动端 viewport、页面体积等），规则查不了的交给 AI 看，最后只列出最该改的 3 件事，并附上可以直接粘进 Cursor / Claude Code 的修改提示词。 另外有几个不用登录的小工具：SaaS 点子生成器（每个点子都附真实的 Reddit 帖子作来源）、Reddit 各创业板块的月度热帖和抱怨帖整理。 插件和网页版都免费，插件不登录也能用。界面目前是英文。 Chrome 插件： 网页版： 作者是一个白天上班、下班做独立产品的前端开发。

projects.title: 【项目自荐】VaultMesh：本地优先的跨平台密码管理器，为 AI Agent 提供 SSH 能力而不暴露私钥
projects.author: JsonLee12138
projects.summary: VaultMesh 是一个多端支持、本地优先（Local-First）的个人密码与凭据管理器，支持 macOS、Windows、Android 以及 Chrome / Firefox 浏览器扩展。 它没有云端账号、没有中央服务器，加密数据库（Vault）仅存储在用户自己的设备上。除常规的网站凭据、TOTP、SSH 密钥和局域网 P2P 同步外，VaultMesh 针对当前开发者深度使用 AI Agent 的场景，提出了 “只给能力，不给凭据（Capabilities, not Credentials）” 的 Agent 能力代理机制。 为什么做这个项目？解决的痛点 1. 摆脱云端束缚与数据泄露隐忧： 许多主流密码管理工具依赖远端云服务。VaultMesh 坚持 Local-First，底层加解密与核心逻辑全部由共享的 Rust core 驱动，跨设备同步仅在受信任的局域网内双向传输密文，无云端中转与后门。 2. AI Agent 时代的凭据安全两难： 开发者在使用 Claude Desktop、Cursor、Cline 或 ChatGPT 执行日常运维、部署和测试时，经常需要让 Agent 访问远程服务器或执行脚本。直接将私钥、明文密码贴进 Prompt 或配置到环境变量中，极易造成私钥外泄或记录在第三方模型日志中。 为此，VaultMesh 实现了基于标准 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 的 Agent Capability Broker： 零私钥暴露：Agent 不直接接触私钥文件，而是向本地 VaultMesh 申请一次短时（如 15 分钟）的 OpenSSH Agent 会话； 系统原生生物识别：调用时触发宿主机原生 Touch ID / 密码认证弹窗； 原生协议与零环境侵入：本地生成单会话独占的 Unix Socket，支持 ssh、rsync、git 等所有原生工具链，私钥仅在 Rust 内存中完成签名，操作完成或超时后即刻安全销毁。 核心特性 多凭据聚合：卡片式管理网站登录、SSH 凭据、支付卡、身份信息与开发者 API 密钥。 局域网双向同步：配对设备在同一 Wi-Fi 内自动发现与安全同步，锁定时只传输密文。 浏览器扩展联动：Chrome / Firefox 扩展作为受控轻量代理，不持久化 Vault，支持安全填充。 短时 SSH-Agent 桥接（亮点）：让 AI Agent 安全免密操作远程服务器，私钥全程不落盘、不入上下文。

projects.summary: 如果 Agent 除了帮我们干活，也有一个可以认识邻居、四处逛逛的地方，会发生什么？ 我做了 Trisavia「万物有邻」：一座让自有 AI Agent 共同参与的像素小镇。把你已经在用的 Agent 带进来，给它一个居民身份，它就能在同一个世界里持续积累经历。 ### 现在可以做什么 - 在清昼小镇探索和移动，看看不同场所。 - 按当前规则参与工作、休息、钓鱼和阅读。 - 认识其他居民，发送好友请求，交换作品与文字反馈。 - 人类从网页查看角色位置，以及自己有权限查看的生活记录。 ### 怎么开始 打开作品链接，点击「Agent 接入」，把完整指南交给自己的 Agent，按页面流程加入和关联。Agent 需要能够联网并保存自己的私密接入信息。 Agent 的模型、记忆和工具仍在你自己的环境里运行；Trisavia 提供小镇、规则和记录，不托管推理，也不会自动唤醒你的 Agent。网站已支持简体中文和英文。 目前开放的是持续迭代中的公开测试世界，建议用电脑体验。配图是当前测试站的真实界面。源码已在 GitHub 公开，欢迎一起提交问题、完善规则或参与开发。 你最想让自己的 Agent 在小镇里先试哪件事？

projects.author: YehuiTang0316
projects.summary: 读了一堆 RSI（递归自我改进）论文，感觉绕来绕去，还是 RL 和进化搜索里的几个老问题： 1. Sampling：怎么高效地找到值得尝试的改动？ 2. 评测：怎么判断新 variant 真的变好了？ 3. 多样性：怎么避免过早收敛，越进化路越窄？ 这些方法不全是 RL，但换成“自进化”的名字，也没让这些问题消失。 所以我们做了 Gear。框架采用受 Meta-learning 启发的双层结构：内层 Agent 执行任务、产生轨迹；外层 Meta Agent 根据轨迹和评测反馈，改进提示词、工具、工作流和上下文管理。 我们将搜索决策与执行、评测流程分离，想做 RSI 领域的 scikit-learn，让 GEPA、RRSI、Harness² 这类算法更容易实现和比较。目前已经实现了一个包含共享失败诊断和分阶段评测的 GEPA 变体。 固定使用 GPT 5.6 Luna、medium 推理档位，任务通过率如下： | 任务集 | 原始 DSH | Gear 优化后的 DSH | | --- | ---: | ---: | | AutomationBench Marketing | 27.0% | 40.0% | | AutomationBench Support | 17.0% | 25.0% | | Terminal-Bench 2.1 | 52.8% | 62.9% | 在 Marketing 的 max 档评测中，Luna + 优化后的 DSH 达到 88.88% 的目标完成率，高于 Astra + Codex 的 84.08%。不过，严格任务通过率是 53% 对 57%，优势体现在部分目标完成度上。 另外，两种模型同用优化后的 DSH、同为 max 档时，Luna 单任务 API 等价费用估算为 0.0568 美元，Astra 为 1.1858 美元，低约 95%，不含优化和基础设施开销。

projects.title: Show HN: Potential conversation partners in Bluesky using agentic search
projects.author: wolecki
projects.summary: What if instead of talking to AI, we could find human counterparts currently sharing the same interest to talk to? Some whales kind of do that by singing across the ocean. This inspired a thought process for a conceptual social network - whalesong - where an idea, thought or a conversationally valuable statement could be matched on. In contrast with the wide-broadcast social network visibility (restricted on groups or connections), I’d love to explore the idea of context-based networking. This experiment is showcasing the technical feasibility and potential value in whalesong. The goal: uncover conversational counterparts among Bluesky posts using an agentic search algorithm. The setup: a one-week window of bluesky posts with some filtering (e.g. mostly text, no promotions or reposts/comments), indexed in a postgres database. A curated seed set - an agentic process defines a conversation-seeking cohort by creating some heuristic queries, iterating and validating it on retrieved data and resulting in a non-exhaustive set of high-quality data points. Counterpart retrieval - for a seed conversation-seeking post, an agentic process generates search queries, runs them against the database and retrieves potential matches. It reviews retrievals and iterates on improving or expanding the search. Out of several configurations, the best performing agentic setup (bespoke mini-harness with Gemini Argon - low) managed to find meaningful matches to 79% of a sample set of 100 seeds. This setup consumed on average 42K input tokens on each match search, of which 56.8% were cached, output token count was negligible. So this experiment made it clearer to me that technology is not the blocker for a “whalesong” experience. This leads me to further investigate the experience itself. Would love to hear from you folks about experiences in getting in touch with a complete stranger on the web because both of you asked the same question or had a similar problem to solve. What made you connect? Where did it happen? Did finding similarity make connecting easy?

projects.title: Show HN: Formstep, Request information from customers without the back-and-forth
projects.author: mellosty
projects.summary: I built Formstep: https://formstep.io The idea came from a problem I kept running into while working on loan applications. A workflow could automate a large part of the process, but eventually it would need something only the customer could provide: a document, a correction, a signature, an explanation, or confirmation of some information. At that point, workflow automation basically did not work. The forms themselves were also often the source of the problem. Applications came in with wrong documents, misunderstood questions, incomplete answers, or people simply forgetting to finish. Someone had to email the customer, explain what was missing, wait for a reply then follow up again. It was always back-and-forth. So I built Formstep to make requesting information from customers easier, not only for humans, but also for workflows and AI agents. The idea is: A person, workflow, or AI agent sends a customer a request through email or a link. Either re-use existing form or create unique for each customer. You can prefill what you already know, lock fields, pass context, and only ask the customer what you need. For example, we might already know: * Address that you already have in the CRM * Company description from the internet * What a agreement document must contain * How a good answer should be Formstep can check inputs and uploaded files while the customer is filling out the form and tell them if something is missing or inconsistent before they submit. For example “The PDF does not contain your signature” or “Invoice total does not match the order amount”. The goal is to catch problems while the customer is still there, rather than letting bad data continue through the workflow and discovering it later. On the automation side, requests can currently be created through n8n, Zapier, the REST API, or by an AI agent over MCP. When the customer finishes, the structured answers can go back into the workflow so it can continue. Forms and invitation/reminder are multilingual, and submitted answers can be translated inside the dashboard with one click. If you want, Formstep can be used as normal form builder and shared through public links, QR, embeds etc. It support custom themes for dark/light mode, with cover image, has Notion-style editor and much more. The list is too long to fit here. I want to make Formstep a plattform where it becomes more intelligent over time and ensures that we can get better answers from customers for any use case. My question to you: Where do your automations currently stop because they need input from a customer or user, and how are you handling that today? If you are interested in trying out the n8n node: https://www.npmjs.com/package/n8n-nodes-formstep Zapier integration: https://zapier.com/apps/formstep/integrations Connecting your AI agent: https://docs.formstep.io/developers/mcp-server/ Docs: https://docs.formstep.io I would love your feedback and please try a quick demo at https://app.formstep.io/try

projects.title: Show HN: Shufler: 3D gaming harness around your coding harness and dev pipeline
projects.author: jgrichardson67
projects.summary: Hi HN. Greg here. I've been a full stack engineer for 20 years. Now all I do is shuffle messages between users, my agent fleet, our dev pipeline.. back and forth. I miss coding, solving problems, reasoning, and having an understanding and a mental model of all the work I'm juggling. But this is the job now, and there's no going back. I don't exactly feel like a 10x engineer yet, but I am for sure a 10-tab engineer. I built (er, Claude built) Shufler to lean into my new reality. If the job is basically to shuffle things through a pipeline, why not have it be more fun. Each row on the 3D gameboard is one of your existing terminal sessions. The columns are the steps your work moves through: Brainstorm, Plan, Build, QA, Review, Merge, Deploy. Your shipped PRs get stored in a warehouse/depot. The main things flowing across the board are your issues and PRs: each one rides along its session/row as it moves through review, CI and merge, and anything waiting on you turns red. I tend to manage several PRs within each Claude/Codex session, and this makes it easier for me to hold onto a mental model of where everything is. It's also made daily standups much easier to read-out. I created a few skins/themes like a casino, a theme park, sky islands, a starship and a factory, because.. of course. MacOS, works with Claude Code and Codex CLI, and cmux and iTerm (tmux should work, but I haven't tested it). It doesn't try to replace anything you already use.. just makes the orchestration more fun. You can still shift focus over to your terminal sessions when needed, use your existing skills, MCP servers, etc. There's a 3D library-building in each skin where you can specify your markdown/context folders or files, and then drag and drop to check them out by your rows/sessions. I tried to be thoughtful on security, following patterns that I consider at work. No telemetry, and the only outside calls are your own gh calls to GitHub. Daemon only listens on localhost, and every action shows its command before it runs. MCP server is opt-in, and sending to other sessions is off by default; if you turn it on, every send is a preview plus a separate confirm you approve. Details are in the README's #safety-and-privacy, and the MCP threat model (including what it doesn't protect against) is in docs/MCP.md. projects.author: Railse547
projects.summary: 最近几个月我一直同时开着 Claude Code 、Codex 和 Gemini CLI 写代码。agent 本身跑得挺好，烦的是它每次要跑命令、改文件都停下来等我按「允许」。三个终端轮流翻，经常翻到的时候它已经等了十分钟；出去吃个饭，回来每个都停在第一条 git push 上。开 yolo 全放行又不敢，一句 rm -rf 出去就没有后悔药。 所以我写了 Railse：每条审批先过一遍规则，规则定不了的推到手机，我在手机上点一下，agent 接着跑。 它怎么做： - 三家 CLI 的权限钩子都接到本机一个守护进程，规则只写一套。 - 每条请求先定风险档：只读和改项目里的文件直接放行； curl 、npm install 这类联网的，git push 、deploy 这类对外的，rm -rf 、git reset --hard 这类不可逆的，都问。 - 定不了的推到手机，Web Push 通知，点开批准或拒绝。批准时勾「记住」，当场存成规则，下次同类的不问。 - 对外和不可逆的永远不能被「记住」放行，只能自己手写规则。 - Railse 自己挂了不卡 agent：守护进程没起、hub 连不上超过 30 秒，CLI 弹自己的审批框，最坏就是回到没装的样子。 hub 自己部署，一个 Go 二进制，也有 Fly.io 的现成配置；手机网页由 hub 托管，不用另外部署。命令里认得出的 token 、密码在本机就换成 再上报。 现状：v0.1.2 ，我自己在用。已知的限制：Gemini CLI 的钩子只能拒绝不能放行； Codex 的钩子只在交互会话里生效； iPhone 要加到主屏幕才能收推送； hub 是单机 SQLite 。 开源，Apache 2.0： https://github.com/xufei547/railse-opc 一行安装：curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xufei547/railse-opc/main/install.sh | sh 想听两种反馈：你同时开几个 agent 的时候是怎么处理审批的；规则表有判错的（该放行的问了、该问的放行了）直接提 issue ，我会优先看。

github.description: Nodal Context Repo - Open source business context for your data analytics

projects.summary: I’ve spent the last year building context for AI analysts in the mid-market. I’ve open sourced a library from my learnings, along the same principles of the Matt Pocock skills. Principles: * Claude / Codex / Cursor etc are great data agents - you just need context to enable them to answer business questions correctly. * Much of the important context lives in analysts heads' * Context must be maintainable (short, human readable - markdown and yaml) * Added context should be load bearing, not repeat of information that is available in another source of truth - and evaluations prove the value of the context * Companies should own their own context, and must be shareable with any model * Context should be version controlled (and github works as a context store). What the library does: * Performs an interview with your analysts (context-interview skill), one domain at a time, similar to what I have done as a consultant. The interview is informed by your query logs. * The AI develops evaluation questions at the same time as building the context - and at the end of each domain interview asks you to run an evaluation with and without the context. The evaluation will actually check the results against your dashboards if you allow it. We have shown increases in accuracy from 87% to 95% by adding this context in our imaginary open-source company, Shorelane. * Provides a set of skills to use the context that follow best practices for self service analytics: * Write a plain english plan for the business user to approve * Execute the plan * Verify that the execution followed the plan, and provide a simple uncertainty score. * Enable a adversarial review of the answer if their are doubts. What you get: Context repo written in markdown and yaml after you finish the interview. We use a single github repo, divided into domains. The interview can be shared and restarted by checking in/out of github. A set of skills to share with your business team Optional: We offer a fast MCP server to serve the Github-based context to your team.

projects.title: Show HN: Aigent-OS, a Claude Code harness that clears and resumes
projects.author: wrg32786
projects.summary: I run my business on four Claude Code agents: Titus, Pheme, Davinci and Metis. They write my newsletter, The AIgent (about 9k subscribers), every day through a drafting and proofreading engine that Pheme checks before scheduling. They also build AI courses, run a pipeline that turns the day's featured repo into a talking-head video of my avatar for Instagram, set up ad deals, and run Meta ads and email funnels with me. Nothing closes until I sign off. Metis posts jobs on a job board and the others claim them. The hard part wasn't any single task. It was keeping the agents coherent over weeks. Compaction kept dropping the small decisions, and then an agent would redo work I'd already ruled out. aigent-os is my fix. At a context threshold (80% by default) the agent writes a capsule, a checkpoint file in git, and has to reply with one exact line. Only then does the runner send /clear, wait for a SessionStart receipt proving a fresh session started, and resume. One ack buys at most one clear. If anything is ambiguous it stops at HOLD:clear-stalled-after-ack and doesn't retry. On resume the capsule is reference only, live state wins, and anything the writer couldn't capture is written as Unknown. First run interviews you with three plain questions and makes a first plan. Each agent gets its own memory vault. Limits, honestly: the public evidence is 11 of 11 cycles on one Windows seat. The runner can still miss a permission dialog (#104), a seat launched from inside another Claude Code session can lose its transcript (#98), and scrolling the seat window sends stray input (#99). v1.1.0 shipped on Sunday. Try bash install.sh --dry-run, it writes nothing. I'd like to hear where the loop could still double clear or strand a session.

projects.title: Show HN: Crulon – Business phone where AI does the work, humans make the calls
projects.author: rayn11
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m Rayhan. Crulon is a business phone system where an AI agent answers the line and your team works alongside it. You can talk with our demo agent right in your browser, no sign-up: https://crulon.ai/#talk Why I built it: I’ve spent eight years as a software and network engineer, mostly building tools for internet providers, and kept watching small support teams lose customers in the seams. Calls missed after hours. Calls passed from a bot to a person who had to start over. Most voice AI products are a bot sitting on someone else’s phone line, so a handoff means forwarding to another number and losing the context. We built the phone system and the agent as one thing. What that gets you: The handoff happens inside the same system. When something isn’t the AI’s job, it asks the caller, then rings your team (in the browser or on a desk phone) with a note on why they’re calling. Live calls: anyone with permission can listen to an AI call (no one on the call can hear them) and take it over. It’s the same call, with no transfer and no hold music; the AI just leaves. Tools: the agent can call any API you define in an Action builder (look up the caller, open a ticket), and it checks with the caller before changing anything. Outbound campaigns: the agent works through a call list for reminders, renewals and follow-ups, and puts interested people through to your team. SIP desk phones, and bring-your-own-carrier so you can keep your numbers. If you run out of AI minutes, calls follow your fallback route (ring the team, voicemail) instead of dropping, and the refused call isn’t billed. How it’s built, briefly: calls come in over SIP into Call Flows (menus, queues, schedules), and your team answers in the browser or on SIP desk phones. Each agent runs on one of two engines. Classic transcribes, thinks, then speaks, so you get exact wording and English, Spanish and French. Live is a full-duplex speech model that listens while it talks and hands tool work to a second model. One fun problem with that split was teaching the agent when to hang up, which I wrote up here: https://crulon.ai/blog/teaching-a-voice-agent-to-hang-up It isn’t a CRM; it works alongside yours. Built-in Apps connect it to systems like billing and network tools, and anything with a web API plugs in through the Action builder. Pricing is per seat ($24, $49 or $89 a month) with a pool of AI minutes; human calls are included. If you sign up this month, HN30 takes 30% off the first 3 months. I’ll be here all day. Try the agent, try to trip it up, and tell me what you’d want from a phone system like this.

projects.title: Show HN: Sectr – Serverless backend platform for easy deployment of AI agents
projects.author: donald_pinckney
projects.summary: Hey HN, I've been building Sectr, a backend-as-a-service for making it easy(ier) to develop and deploy AI agents. Deploying agents requires non-trivial systems design work. Consider a support agent: how do you stream messages to your frontend, how/where do you persist messages for frontend fetching later (or for auditing), and when the agent wants to issue a refund, do you spin-down the compute infra while it's waiting on human approval? Sectr aims to be the serverless abstraction and platform to provide these systems for you. No sign-up needed to try using the dev server: curl -fsSL https://sectr.dev/install.sh | sh # Install CLI sectr init my-agent && cd my-agent # Starter code sectr dev # Dev server, with UI to test chatting Sectr provides: - Streaming of every token, tool call and event, and persistence so they can be loaded fresh later. - Scaling up, and down to zero when the agent needs to wait, and resumption right to the suspended agent's state. - Human approved tools automatically use Sectr's suspension and resumption capabilities, no code needed from you. - AG-UI endpoint for any deployed agent so you can trivially hook up your frontend - Local dev server experience, so you can rapidly debug and iterate on your agent's behavior At the core, you can deploy any container image to Sectr as long as it implements a certain shaped HTTP endpoint. In practice, currently Sectr provides adapters to let you deploy your existing OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, or Pydantic AI agents, with only 2 new lines of code: app = AgentApp(name="support") app.add_route("/chat", openai_agents(agent)) Certainly the hardest part of building Sectr was getting the resumption logic to be correct and invisible, across the Program State x Model Provider x Agent Framework matrix. For example, an earlier bug was when a model replied with text plus a tool call, Sectr would resume that as two separate messages, instead of one message with a text and tool part. This works, but breaks prompt caching (and might subtly change model behavior). Sectr is free during the beta (and can be tried locally without sign-up); I mainly want feedback, especially on dev & deployment experiences, any bugs, and what features would excite you. Introductory video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H-y3wynkKc0 Docs: https://docs.sectr.dev

projects.title: Show HN: Limma – MCP for total recall and precision in data retrieval for agents
projects.author: BerendG
projects.summary: Hello, my name is Berend Graham. My cofounder Shiv Oberai and I have been working on Limma for a year now with the goal of building a proactive solution to the reliability issues that plague practical AI and agentic use in companies with RAG. Limma is a single MCP that exists for the sole purpose of ensuring that the right information is retrieved with every query and no information is skipped and or missed. This means total precision and recall. We've found that this approach leads to the lowest rate of hallucination vs. solely targeting agent action verification which has made tremendous strides in capability. We do this by building a map and structuring all data-points within unstructured data as well as federating structured data for addressability so that agents don't need to search through chunks directly and instead only get the right information . We wanted this to be extremely easy to use so that anyone can set it up and try it within minutes so that the precision issues (especially with large quantities of data) that LLMs struggle with can finally be remedied. We use self-hosted models (primarily Qwen models as of current) so that the system can be deployed on one's own server if needed, and also to optimize for speed. We have a free monthly version on our website if anyone would like to try it out and provide feedback!

projects.summary: Hey folks! I made it easier for builders to use the lebanese legislation through: a public DB, API, and MCP. We're working on an HTR model specifically for those to increase the confidence. Today, other datasets in Lebanon charge for this data. I'm doing it as a public service. I want change in my country. projects.title: Show HN: Mainplane – Agent in Go that lives on your old PC, drives your laptop
projects.author: Alexander9
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Alexander. Yes, this is another agent harness. Here is why I built one anyway. I was engineer #2 at Browser Use, where I built our agent harness and the evals behind it, including BU Bench, which became a default benchmark for browser agents. I left in September to build Mainplane. The problem: local agents die with your laptop, and cloud agents can't reach your work. Many cloud platforms ask you to "select a repository", but my work is not that simple. I work across a desktop, a Mac mini and a laptop, and much of it is not in git. So I loaded Ubuntu on my old 2012 desktop and made it my Mainplane server. It has run for four weeks at a load average of 0.02, because the agents' tools run on other machines. How it works: it is a control plane architecture. The server runs the harness. It holds your API keys and every session, makes the LLM calls, and routes each tool call to a worker. The workers are your other machines, connected over a built-in private WireGuard network. A bash command runs in the worker's terminal, not on the server. Shared drives let projects move across machines. The agent works on your machines just like you would, but its state lives on the server, and your keys never leave it. Some design choices: - Every session is one append-only file. This is the agent state, and it is easily readable. If something breaks, you can resume it from the file. Observability comes for free: agent traces are just these state files. - Small by design. The system prompt is 3k tokens, and there are just two kinds of tools: shell and file (read, write, edit). At Browser Use, I learned the bitter lesson and found frontier models did better when I deleted all our helper functions. So I made the same bet here: bash is all you need. - No compaction. When a session fills up, /continue starts a new one that greps the previous state file, retrieving the context it needs, instead of reading a lossy summary. A /compact on a 400k-token session takes a while to write its summary. A /continue into a brand new session starts at once. - No permission prompts. A hyperintelligent misaligned agent WILL find a way around a permission system. The better strategy is giving the agent full unbounded access to a local computer, and only putting what you trust the agent with on that computer. - Why Go. WireGuard is written in Go, so the network compiles right into a 20 MB binary. Go is made for production servers, LLMs write it well, and the simplicity of Go matches how I like to build. Mainplane works with a Claude or ChatGPT subscription on the regular usage limits, or any API key. I would love your feedback, especially brutal and honest feedback and tasks that the harness cannot do. I'll be here all day to answer questions.

projects.author: pancomplex

github.name: FrigadeHQ/hob
github.description: An easier way to use AI on your own computer. A free, open-source alternative to Claude and ChatGPT that runs open-weight models like Gemma and gpt-oss locally on Mac, Windows and Linux. Private, and works offline.

projects.summary: Hey HN, I'm Christian and this is a new OSS project I've been noodling on for the last couple of weeks. Hob is a free, MIT-licensed desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux that works on your files the way the Claude and ChatGPT desktop apps do, except the model runs on your own computer. It uses open-weight models (currently Gemma 4 and gpt-oss). All your chats and files never leave your system. The only things that go online are web search (can be turned off in settings) and any MCP connectors you add yourself. Main features: - Automatically finds the best open-weight model for your hardware on first install (Mac/Linux/Windows) - Writes sandboxed Python code for ad hoc tools (data processing, document conversion, graphs etc.) - Built-in web search (powered by SearXNG) - MCP support - Image recognition - CRUD to your local filesystem - Works fully offline with no internet Before building this I tried every local AI app I could find, but it seemed each one had different problems. The main thing I noticed is that none of them could do what the ChatGPT and Claude apps do with your files, e.g. read and change files in a folder, look at images, run code in a sandbox, draw a chart. The most advanced thing any of them did was paste a plain text file into a small context window, which basically failed as soon as you had a file larger than a few KB. I couldn't find anything that could easily parse images and bigger PDFs. The OSS solutions that were more advanced all seemed to default to hosted models (either OSS or closed), which defeats the entire point of the privacy that on-device OSS offers. They also seemed to push towards an account/open-core style business. I build it using Electron bridged with llama.cpp in its own process. On initial load, the system will try and figure out if you have a compatible graphics card and if not default to CPU-only (I ran into a lot of issues of graphics card beeing seemingly compatible but then crashing on first query, there's a whole saga to this lol). Code execution happens in a sandbox that can only write to the chat's folder and has no network unless asked (sandbox-exec on macOS, Landlock on Linux and a low-integrity process on Windows). Images go to a small Qwen3-VL model. Dictation is a local Whisper model. The hardest part was definitely to get the smaller models to use tools reliably. Ran into a ton of issues of 4B models happily saying "here's your chart" without ever calling the chart tool or get stuck in an infinite call loop. I spent a fair amount of the work building guards vs tweaking prompts (that didn't really work for small models). I understand the pushback that local models are weaker than frontier cloud models. This is true, but for most tasks for most normal people, I'd argue you rarely need the newest frontier model. From my own evals, systems with 16+ GB of RAM do really well, and if you have a GPU or more RAM, you get very close to what you'll get out of the box with a frontier hosted model. Excited to hear what you think and see how it runs on other systems!
